BURHAN:v4p406/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p406/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p406/r1.claim: The listed ما clauses include relative ما: what is harvested and stored, what was prepared for the seven years, what fathers married, and what people worship besides God.

BURHAN:v4p3/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p3/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p3/r4.claim: The plural prohibition distributes individually: each addressee is forbidden his own mother and daughter, not every addressee's relatives to everyone.
BURHAN:v4p3/r4.anchor: فإنه لم يحرم على كل واحد من المخاطبين جميع أمهات المخاطبين وإنما حرم على كل واحد أمه وبنته

DAMGHANI:v1p189/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p189/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p189/r6.claim: Rabība means a stepdaughter raised in a man’s household.
DAMGHANI:v1p189/r6.anchor: ولد زوجة الرجل إذا ربي في بيته

DAMGHANI:v1p42/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p42/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p42/r1.claim: Umm can mean a nursing mother or wet nurse, with the source specifying nursing during the first two years.
DAMGHANI:v1p42/r1.anchor: الرابع : الأم يعني المرضع . قوله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r5.claim: A rabība is a man’s stepdaughter; ḥijr refers to the front of a garment and came to mean a child’s care and protection there.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r5.anchor: الربيبة: بنت زوج الرجل من غيره. الحجر بفتح الحاء وكسرها: مقدم ثوب الإنسان وما بين يديه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r6.claim: Ḥalīla means wife and ḥalīl means husband; the author derives the wife’s name from dwelling wherever her husband settles.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r6.anchor: الحليلة: الزوجة، والحليل الزوج قال: أغشى فتاة الحي عند حليلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r7.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r7.claim: He derives ḥalīla from ḥalāl, meaning that she is made lawful; another explanation says each spouse makes the other’s waistcloth lawful.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r7.anchor: وذهب الزجاج وغيره إلى أنها من لفظ الحلال، فهي حليلة بمعنى محللة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r8.claim: Ṣulb means the back, with ṣalība denoting strength and firmness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r8.anchor: الصلب: الظهر، وصلب صلابة قوي واشتد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r9.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r9.claim: He reports regional pronunciation: Hijaz speakers say ṣulb with a rounded vowel, while Tamim and Asad say ṣalb with open vowels, citing verse evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r9.anchor: أن الصلب وهو الظهر، على وزن قفل هو لغة أهل الحجاز ويقول فيه تميم وأسد:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r10.claim: An unnamed poet’s line using ṣulb is cited as evidence for the regional pronunciation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p553/r10.anchor: وصلب مثل العنان المؤدم ... قال وأنشدني بعض بني أسد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r1.speaker: محمد بن عمر الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r1.claim: He raises six objections to deriving the full prohibition from the verse alone: its passive form, possible temporary scope, addressed audience, past tense, apparent all-to-all reading, and suggestion of prior permissibility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r1.anchor: وقال محمد بن عمر الرازي: فيها عندي بحث من وجوه: أحدها: أن بناء الفعل للمفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r2.claim: The author says these objections are unhelpful: the omitted agent is known to be God, and surrounding clauses confirm the divine source of prohibition and permission.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r2.anchor: ومعلوم أن المحرم هو الله تعالى. ألا ترى إلى آخر الآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r3.claim: Divine prohibition implies permanence unless the text specifies a temporary exception, as it does for necessity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r3.anchor: ومتى جاء التحريم من الله فلا يفهم منه إلا التأبيد، فإن كان له حالة إباحة نص عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r4.claim: Past-tense legal wording can establish a new rule or reaffirm an existing one; it need not limit the rule to the past, as in a future-oriented oath.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r4.anchor: وأما أنه صيغة ماض فيخصه فالأفعال التي جاءت يستفاد منها الأحكام الشرعية، وإن كانت بصيغة الماضي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r5.claim: The phrase does not make every person’s mother universally forbidden to everyone; generic scope pairs each addressee with his own mother, not all mothers collectively.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r5.anchor: فإنما المفهوم: حرم على كل واحد واحد منكم كل واحدة، واحدة من أم نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r6.claim: The legally prohibited mother is any woman from whom a person descends through birth, whether through his father’s or mother’s line.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p577/r6.anchor: والأم المحرمة شرعا هي كل امرأة رجع نسبك إليها بالولادة من جهة أبيك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r1.claim: Umm literally means the woman who gave birth to you; applying it to grandmothers is literal if the word is shared or polysemous, figurative if not, otherwise their prohibition comes from consensus or another text.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r1.anchor: ولفظ الأم حقيقة في التي ولدتك نفسه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r2.claim: Mothers and daughters have been forbidden since Adam; intercourse is degrading, so mothers are protected from it in return for their immense beneficence to children.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r2.anchor: وحرمة الأمهات والبنات كانت من زمان آدم عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r3.claim: A prohibited daughter is any female descended from you through birth at any degree; whether a granddaughter is literally or figuratively a daughter parallels the grandmother question.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r3.anchor: كل أنثى رجع نسبها إليك بالولادة بدرجة أو درجات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r4.speaker: النضر بن شميل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r4.claim: Al-Naḍr ibn Shumayl records that pre-Islamic Ḥājib ibn Zurārah married his daughter and became a Magian.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r4.anchor: ذكر ذلك: النضر بن شميل في كتاب المثالب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r5.claim: A prohibited sister is anyone sharing with you a paternal backbone or womb; paternal and maternal aunts mean the father's and mother's sisters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r5.anchor: الأخت المحرمة كل من جمعك وإياها صلب أو بطن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r6.claim: The text names aunts but not their daughters; grand-aunts are also prohibited, with some collateral aunt relations allowed when they are unrelated to the brother's descendants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r6.anchor: وخص تحريم العمات والخالات دون أولادهن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r7.claim: Nieces remain prohibited however far they descend; singular brother and sister are used because a plural follows, while the singular conveys the whole gendered class.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r7.anchor: وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت تحرم بناتهما وإن سفلن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r8.claim: Seven women are permanently forbidden by lineage: mother and daughter through birth, plus sister, aunt, and brother's or sister's daughter through sibling relations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r8.anchor: فهؤلاء سبع من النسب تحريمهن مؤبد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r9.claim: The verse names nursing mothers and sisters to treat milk kinship like lineage: it gives one example from each of the birth and sibling categories to indicate the rest.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p578/r9.anchor: نبه بذلك على إجراء الرضاع مجرى النسب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r1.claim: The Prophetic rule that nursing forbids what lineage forbids confirms the analogy indicated by the verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r1.anchor: يحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم من النسب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r2.claim: Milk kinship maps through the wet nurse and her husband: his parents are grandparents, his sister an aunt, his other children paternal siblings, and her children by him full siblings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r2.anchor: فزوج المرضعة أبوه، وأبواه جداه، وأخته عمته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r3.claim: Two exceptions to the nursing rule are marrying one's nursing son's sister or nursing brother's mother, since the intercourse that creates the corresponding lineage bar is absent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r3.anchor: تحريم الرضاع كتحريم النسب إلا في مسألتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r4.claim: The verse does not settle nursing age, number of feeds, milk-father, or ways of administering milk into the stomach; jurists disagree on these matters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r4.anchor: ولا عدد الرضعات. ولا للبن الفحل، ولا لإرضاع الرجل لبن نفسه للصبي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r5.claim: Most read اللاتي أرضعنكم; ʿAbd Allāh reads اللاي, Ibn Hurmuz التي, and Abū Ḥaywah reads الرضاعة with a kasra on rāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: اللاتي أرضعنكم. وقرأ عبد الله: اللاي بالياء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r6.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r6.claim: Most authorities take mothers of wives as an unrestricted prohibition, whether or not the marriage to the daughter was consummated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r6.anchor: وأمهات نسائكم الجمهور على أنها على العموم. فسواء عقد عليها ولم يدخل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r7.speaker: علي ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r7.claim: ʿAlī, Mujāhid, and others allow marrying a wife's mother if the wife was divorced before consummation, treating her like a stepdaughter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r7.anchor: وروي عن علي ومجاهد وغيرهما: أنه إذا طلقها قبل الدخول، فله أن يتزوج أمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r8.speaker: علي وداود وأهل الظاهر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r8.claim: They read “stepdaughters in your care” as a condition: if the daughter was not in his care, a man who consummated with her mother may marry her; both custody and consummation must be present for prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p579/r8.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب علي، وبه أخذ داود وأهل الظاهر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p582/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p582/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p582/r1.claim: “Wives of your sons” refers to wives; merely purchasing a slave woman does not bar her to the buyer's father or son, but touching or kissing her does, while lustful looking is disputed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p582/r1.anchor: وظاهر قوله: وحلائل أبنائكم اختصاص ذلك بالزوجات كما ذكرناه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p605/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p605/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p605/r5.claim: Expressions imply linked rules: reluctance hints consensual inheritance transfer; the ban on coercing wives allows restraint for their benefit; the prohibition on fathers' wives recalls pre-Islamic practice; permission points to prior bans; slave-marriage conditions and human weakness point to desire.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607/r4.claim: He calls “forbidden to you” followed by “made lawful” verbal antithesis; “chaste, not fornicators” also opposes guarding sexuality to making it freely available.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607/r4.anchor: وفي قوله: والمحصنات من النساء، أي حرام عليكم ثم قال: وأحل لكم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607/r5.claim: “Those you have entered upon” excludes unconsummated marriages; “stepdaughters in your care” and “of women” add qualifications. The statements about faith and shared origin are parenthetical, with omissions elsewhere.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p607/r5.anchor: والاحتراس في قوله: اللاتي دخلتم بهن احترز من اللاتي لم يدخل بهن

BURSEVI:v2p148/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r1.claim: The prohibition of mothers means prohibition of marrying them, as customary usage understands a forbidden thing through its intended use: marrying women, drinking wine, and eating pork.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r1.anchor: لأن المفهوم في العرف من حرمة كل شيء ما هو الغرض المقصود منه

BURSEVI:v2p148/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r2.claim: Mothers includes all ascending grandmothers through either parent; daughters includes biological daughters and all descendants; sisters includes full, paternal, and maternal sisters.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r2.anchor: والأمهات تعم الجدات وإن غلون من الأب والأم أو من قبل إحداهما

BURSEVI:v2p148/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r3.claim: The bans on mothers and daughters have held from Adam to the present in every revealed religion; Zoroaster permitted them, but most Muslims judged him a liar.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r3.anchor: واعلم أن حرمة الأمهات والبنات كانت ثابتة من زمن آدم عليه السلام إلى هذا الزمان ولم يثبت حل نكاحهن

BURSEVI:v2p148/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r4.claim: A report says marriage between siblings was permitted in Adam's time only because of necessity.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r4.anchor: أما نكاح الأخوات فقد نقل أن ذلك كان مباحا في زمن آدم عليه السلام وإنما حكم الله بإباحة ذلك على سبيل الضرورة

BURSEVI:v2p148/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r5.speaker: الإمام
BURSEVI:v2p148/r5.claim: The Imam explains that intercourse is humiliating and usually hidden, so mothers must be protected from it because their benefaction is greatest; daughters are part of oneself and likewise must be spared this humiliation, as must the other listed relatives.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r5.anchor: وذكر العلماء أن السبب لهذا التحريم أن الوطء إذلال وإهانة فإن الإنسان يستحيي من ذكره

BURSEVI:v2p148/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r6.claim: A paternal aunt is any female child of one's father, near or distant; a maternal aunt is any female child of one's mother, likewise including sisters of ancestors through either side.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r6.anchor: العمة كل أنثى ولدها من ولد والدك قريبا أو بعيدا

BURSEVI:v2p148/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r7.claim: Nieces of brothers and sisters from every side, including their descendants however remote, are forbidden.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r7.anchor: من كل جهة ونوافلهما وإن بعدت

BURSEVI:v2p148/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r8.claim: The verse names fourteen forbidden categories: seven by lineage and seven by cause, then begins the latter list with nursing mothers and milk sisters.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r8.anchor: واعلم أن الله تعالى نص على تحريم أربعة عشر صنفا من النسوان سبع منهن من جهة النسب

BURSEVI:v2p148/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r9.claim: Nursing mothers and milk sisters are forbidden like their counterparts by lineage; God gives the wet nurse the status of mother and a nursing partner the status of sister.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r9.anchor: أي حرم نكاح الأمهات والأخوات كلتاهما من الرضاعة كما حرمتا من النسب

BURSEVI:v2p148/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r10.claim: The wet nurse’s husband is the nursling’s father and his parents are grandparents; his children by other women are paternal siblings, while the wet nurse’s mother and sister are grandmother and aunt.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r10.anchor: وكذلك زوج المرضعة أبوه وأبواه جداه وأخته عمته وكل ولد ولد له من غير المرضعة قبل الإرضاع وبعده

BURSEVI:v2p148/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r11.claim: The wet nurse’s children by that husband are full siblings; her children by another husband are maternal siblings.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r11.anchor: وكل من ولد لها من هذا الزوج فهم إخوته وأخواته لأبيه وأمه ومن ولد لها من غيره فهم إخوته وأخواته لأمه

BURSEVI:v2p148/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v2p148/r12.claim: The Prophet states the general rule that nursing forbids the same relations forbidden by lineage.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r12.anchor: ومنه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم "يحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم من النسب"

BURSEVI:v2p148/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r13.claim: Certain apparent milk relations are forbidden through affinity rather than lineage, including a father’s partner, a man’s partner’s daughter or mother, and a grandfather’s partner.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r13.anchor: وأما أم أخيه لأب وأخت ابنه لأم وأم أم ابنه وأم عمه وأم خاله لأب ليست حرمتهن

BURSEVI:v2p148/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148/r14.claim: Mothers of wives means women married to the men, whether or not the marriage was consummated.
BURSEVI:v2p148/r14.anchor: المراد بالنساء المنكوحات على الإطلاق سواء كن مدخولا بهن أم لا

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r1.claim: The majority hold that a wife's mother is forbidden whether or not the marriage was consummated; a Prophetic report allows marrying the daughter after divorce before consummation but forbids marrying the mother.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r1.anchor: جمهور العلماء وقد روي عن النبي عليه السلام أنه قال في رجل تزوج امرأة

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r2.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r2.claim: The Prophet reportedly ruled that a man divorced before consummation may marry his former wife's daughter but may not marry her mother.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r2.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي عليه السلام أنه قال في رجل تزوج امرأة ثم طلقها قبل الدخول بها

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r3.claim: The rules also extend to women touched or otherwise sexually contacted, and mothers includes wet nurses and grandmothers.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r3.anchor: ويلحق بهن الموطوءات بوجه من الوجوه المعدودات فيما سبق آنفا والممسوسات ونظائرهن وأمهات تعم المرضعات

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r4.claim: A rabiiba is a wife's daughter from another man, so named because a stepfather commonly raises her as he raises his own child; the term is an intensive form with passive sense, made into a noun by the feminine ending.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r4.anchor: الربيب ولد المرأة من آخر سمي به لأنه يربه كما يرب ولده في غالب الأمر فعيل بمعنى مفعول

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r5.speaker: ابن السكيت
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit says حجر has two pronunciations and denotes the cloth gathered over a person's thighs; in the verse, being in one's حجر means being raised in one's care.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن السكيت حجر الإنسان وحجره بالفتح والكسر هو ما يجمع على فخذيه من ثوبه

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r6.claim: The lap is a metaphor for upbringing because a caregiver seats a child there; it is comparable to being in someone's custody, from حضن, the armpit.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r6.anchor: والسبب في هذه الاستعارة أن كل من ربى طفلا أجلسه في حجره فصار الحجر عبارة عن التربية

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r7.speaker: جمهور العلماء
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r7.claim: The majority do not require a stepdaughter to have lived in her stepfather's care for the marriage prohibition to apply; the phrase reflects the usual situation, as wives with grown daughters rarely remarry while those with young children often do.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r7.anchor: كون التربية في حجر الراب ليس بشرط للحرمة عند جمهور العلماء والوصف في الآية خرج على الأغلب

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r8.claim: The same wording that reflects the usual case is compared with the prohibition of sexual relations during retreat in mosques, although relations outside mosques during retreat are also forbidden.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r8.anchor: والمباشرة في غير المساجد حالة الاعتكاف حرام أيضا

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r9.claim: Entering unto the wives means intercourse, expressed euphemistically as admission behind a curtain; touching and similar acts also count, and without intercourse a man may marry the daughters after separation or the mother's death.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r9.anchor: ومعنى الدخول بهن إدخالهن الستر والباء للتعدية وهي كناية عن الجماع

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r10.claim: The phrase حَلائل أبناءكم names sons' wives; حليلة is explained either by a wife's being lawful to her husband, living in his place, or each partner's access to the other's garment.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r10.anchor: أي : وحرم عليكم زوجات أبنائكم سميت الزوجة حليلة لحلها للزوج

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r11.claim: The prohibition also covers women illicitly approached by one's son and comparable cases of touching or sexual contact.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r11.anchor: وفي حكمهن مزنياتهم ومن يجري مجراهن من الممسوسات ونظائرهن

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r12.claim: The phrase sons from your loins excludes adopted sons, while sons' descendants and milk sons, however far down, count as sons by lineage for this rule.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r12.anchor: لإخراج الأدعياء دون أبناء الأولاد والأبناء من الرضاع فإنهم وإن سفلوا في حكم الأبناء الصلبية

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r13.claim: An adoptive father may marry the former wife of an adopted son; Muhammad married Zaynab after Zayd, whom he had adopted, divorced her, and critics were answered by revelation.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r13.anchor: وقد تزوج النبي عليه السلام زينب ابنة جحش الأسدية بنت عمته أميمة ابنة عبد المطلب حين فارقها زيد بن حارثة

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r14.claim: Combining two sisters in marriage is forbidden, while their simultaneous ownership is not; combining intercourse with both under ownership is included by implication because the operative basis is shared.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r14.anchor: أي وحرم عليكم الجمع بين الأختين في النكاح لا في ملك اليمين وأما جمعهما في الوطء بملك اليمين

BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r15.claim: The exception for past conduct is disconnected: past acts are not held against people; God forgives pre-Islamic conduct and is merciful to those who repent and obey.
BURSEVI:v2p148#2/r15.anchor: استثناء منقطع أي لكن ما قد مضى لا تؤاخذون به

ELMALILI:4:23/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:23/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:23/r1.claim: If a man has not consummated marriage with a woman's mother, he may marry her daughter; consummation makes the daughter forbidden, while the marriage contract alone forbids the mother.
ELMALILI:4:23/r1.anchor: Demek ki anaları vat’ kızları haram kılar. Kızları mücerred nikâh da anaları haram kılar.

ELMALILI:4:23/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:23/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:23/r2.claim: The wives of one's direct and indirect biological sons are forbidden, including the wives of all descendants; “from your loins” excludes step-sons and adopted sons.
ELMALILI:4:23/r2.anchor: Sulblerinizden bizzat ve bi’l-vâsıta gelen oğullarınızın halîleleri olan gelinleriniz ki bütün torunların zevcelerine de şâmildir, مِنْ أَصْلَٰبِكُمْ kaydıyla üvey oğullardan ve oğulluklardan[^2] ihtiraz edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:4:23/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:23/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:23/r3.claim: It is forbidden to combine two sisters in marriage, and likewise two women who could not lawfully marry one another if one were imagined male, such as a girl with her aunt.
ELMALILI:4:23/r3.anchor: İki hemşire beynini taht-ı nikâhta cem‘etmeniz, kezâlik biri erkek farz edildiği takdirde diğerine nikâhı câiz olmayan iki kadının

ELMALILI:4:23/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:23/r4.speaker: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm
ELMALILI:4:23/r4.claim: A prophetic hadith forbids marrying a woman together with her paternal or maternal aunt, brother's daughter, or sister's daughter.
ELMALILI:4:23/r4.anchor: Aleyhissalâtü vesselâm meşhur bir hadîsinde buyurmuştur ki: لاَ تـُنْكَحُ الْمَرْأَةُ عَلَى عَ َّمتِهَا

ELMALILI:4:23/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:23/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:23/r5.claim: The exception exempts past cases from blame; Jacob's law had permitted marrying two sisters, but the prohibition applies now and in the future.
ELMALILI:4:23/r5.anchor: ancak mâzîde geçmiş olanlar müstesnâ, onlardan dolayı muâheze yoktur. Nitekim Ya‘kūb aleyhisselâm’ın şeriatında vardı

ELMALILI:4:23/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:4:23/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:4:23/r6.claim: God is forgiving and merciful, while these combinations remain prohibited in the present and future.
ELMALILI:4:23/r6.anchor: Fakat hâlen ve istikbâlen bunlar memnû‘ve haramdırlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r1.claim: The following three verses explain impediments to marriage; all religions and human legal systems forbid marriage among relatives within defined degrees.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r1.anchor: Buradan itibaren üç âyette evlenme mânileri açıklanmaktadır. Hemen bütün dinlerde ve beşerî hukuklarda belli derecelerdeki yakınlar arasında evlenme yasaklanmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r2.claim: In Islam, marriage impediments draw also on Sunnah and consensus, whose explanations complete the list of women a man may not marry.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r2.anchor: İslâm’a göre evlenme mânileri bu âyetler yanında sünnet ve icmâ kaynaklarına da dayanmış, bu kaynaklardaki açıklamalarla –aralarında evlenme akdi yapılması câiz olmayanlar listesi– tamamlanmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r3.claim: The forbidden classes include ascendants: mothers and all grandmothers through either the maternal or paternal line.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r3.anchor: Usul (üst soy hısımları). Anne ile anne ve baba tarafından bütün nineler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r4.claim: The forbidden descendants are daughters and all granddaughters through daughters or sons.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r4.anchor: Fürû (alt soy hısımları). Kızlar ile kız ve oğul tarafından bütün kız torunlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r5.claim: Forbidden collateral blood relatives include full or half sisters, paternal and maternal aunts, and nieces.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r5.anchor: İster ana-baba bir olsun, ister yalnızca anadan veya babadan olsun kız kardeşler, halalar ve teyzeler, kız yeğenler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r6.claim: Nursing makes the woman the child’s milk-mother and her husband the milk-father, barring marriage with milk relatives corresponding to the first three blood-relative classes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r6.anchor: Bir çocuk bir kadından süt emince kadın sütannesi, kadının kocası sütbabası olur ve 1, 2, 3. maddelerde sayılan soy hısımları düzeyindeki süt hısımları ile evlenemez.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r7.speaker: İslâm âlimlerinin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r7.claim: Most Islamic scholars also include a spouse’s milk ascendants and descendants, and the spouses of one’s milk ascendants and descendants, among prohibited relations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r7.anchor: İslâm âlimlerinin çoğunluğuna göre eşinin süt usulü ve fürûu ile, süt usulünün ve fürûnun eşleri de bu kapsamdadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r8.claim: Affinity creates permanent and temporary impediments: a wife’s mother and her female ancestors are permanently forbidden even without intercourse; after intercourse, her daughters by a former husband and their daughters are forbidden, as are sons’ and grandsons’ wives and fathers’ wives.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r8.anchor: Devamlı haram olanlar. Cinsî temas yapılmamış olsa dahi nikâh yapılan zevcenin annesi (kayınvâlide) ve onun annesi... Nikâhtan sonra cinsî temas da yapılmış olan zevcenin –daha önceki kocasından olma– kızları ve bunların kızları

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r9.claim: It is temporarily forbidden to marry certain female relatives of one’s wife simultaneously; if the two women would be barred from marrying one another were one male, they cannot be married together.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r9.anchor: Zevcenin belli derecedeki yakınlarını ikinci eş olarak almak. Bu yakınlığın sınırı şöyle tesbit edilmiştir: Zevcenin yakını olan kadının erkek olduğu var sayıldığında birbiriyle evlenmeleri –akrabalık dolayısıyla– câiz değilse bu iki kadını bir arada nikâhlamak da câiz değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r10.claim: A further prohibited class is women still married to another man, even if living separately, unless the husband, arbitrators, or judge has divorced or separated them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r10.anchor: Başkalarının nikâhı altında bulunan (fiilen ayrı yaşasalar bile

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r11.claim: Verse 4:19 had barred forcibly inheriting women and marrying fathers’ wives against their wishes; the present verse clarifies that marriage to stepmothers is forbidden even when both sides consent.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r11.anchor: 19. âyette kadınlara zorla vâris olmak yasaklanırken babaların eşleriyle (üvey analar) –onlar istemediği halde– evlenmek de yasaklanmıştı. Bu âyette konuya açıklık getirilmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r12.claim: The principle that kinship bars marriage is widespread, while the scope differs with a system’s basic beliefs, philosophy, view of human nature, sexual morality, and valuation of family.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r12.anchor: Akrabalığın ve hısımlığın evlenmeye engel olması kaide olarak bütün dinlerde, hukuk ve ahlâk sistemlerinde vardır. Sınırların geniş veya dar tutulması bu sistemlerin oturduğu temel inanca, felsefeye, sistemin insan fıtratı ve tabiatıyla ilişkisine, fuhuş anlayışına ve aileye verdiği öneme bağlı olmuştur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r13.claim: Islam regards family as society’s core and favors a broad family network for mutual concern and solidarity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r13.anchor: İslâm’a göre cemiyetin çekirdeği ailedir, bu sebeple ailenin ilgi ve dayanışma açısından geniş tutulması öngörülmüştür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r14.claim: Because extended-family members often interact, sexual attraction could lead to illicit relations; banning marriage as well as sexual intercourse removes the prospect of treating one another as potential spouses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r14.anchor: cinsî ilişkinin evlenmek suretiyle olması dahi yasaklanmış; böylece birbirlerine, geleceğe yönelik, muhtemel karı-koca olarak bakmaları ihtimali de ortadan kaldırılmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r18.claim: Milk kinship as a marriage bar is a distinct Islamic rule established by relevant verses and hadiths; a wet nurse sustains the helpless infant’s life in the first two years as a birth mother does, so she is treated as a mother and her relatives are barred.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r18.anchor: Çocuğun tabii olarak başka bir gıda ile beslenip gelişemediği bir çağında (ilk iki yaş) onu emziren kadın, tıpkı doğuran ana gibi çocuğun hayatının idamesini sağlamakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r19.speaker: Bazı âlimler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r19.claim: Some scholars hold that if a child is weaned within the first two years and can eat other food, subsequent nursing no longer creates a marriage bar even before age two.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r19.anchor: bazı âlimlere göre ilk iki yaşı içinde bile çocuk sütten kesilir, başka gıdalarla beslenir hale gelirse bundan sonra –henüz iki yaş dolmadığı halde– emzirme haram kılıcı olmaz (İbn Âşûr, IV, 297).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r20.speaker: Müctehid ve müfessirlerin çoğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r20.claim: Most jurists and exegetes limit marriage-prohibiting nursing to the child’s first two years.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r20.anchor: Müctehid ve müfessirlerin çoğuna göre haram kılan emzirmenin çağı çocuğun ilk iki yaşı ile sınırlıdır (Bakara 2/233).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r21.speaker: Hz. Âişe
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r21.claim: Aisha and some scholars, including Layth ibn Sa‘d, infer from certain Prophetic actions that there is no age limit and nursing at any age bars marriage.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r21.anchor: sahâbeden Hz. Âişe, müctehidlerden Leys b. Sa‘d gibi bazı âlimler, Hz. Peygamber’in bazı tasarruflarına bakarak bu konuda yaş sınırı bulunmadığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r22.speaker: Peygamber’in diğer hanımları (ümmehâtü’l-mü’minîn) ve müctehidlerin çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r22.claim: The Prophet’s other wives and most jurists regard those nursing precedents as a special, temporary permission that cannot be extended to others.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r22.anchor: Peygamber’in diğer hanımları (ümmehâtü’l-mü’minîn) ve müctehidlerin çoğunluğu ise haklı olarak, bu konudaki uygulamaların özel ve geçici bir izin olduğu, başkalarına teşmil edilemeyeceği görüşünü benimsemişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r23.speaker: Müctehidlerin çoğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r23.claim: Most jurists say even one swallowed sip of milk by a child under two is enough to establish milk kinship; others infer from reports that five full feeds are required.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:4:22/r23.anchor: Müctehidlerin çoğuna göre iki yaşını doldurmamış çocuğun midesine inen bir yudum süt dahi “süthısımlığı” ilişkisi için yeterlidir. Bazı rivayetlere dayanarak bunu beş doyumluk emmeye kadar çıkaranlar olmuştur

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r1.speaker: حمزة
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r1.claim: Ḥamza reads the mīm in إمهاتكم with kasra, while al-Kisāʾī reads it with fatḥa.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r2.claim: Al-Kisāʾī's fatḥa preserves the mīm's original vowel because the sound change affects the hamza, not the mīm; the preceding kasra or yāʾ is assimilated to the hamza.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r2.anchor: أما فتح الكسائي الميم في إمهاتكم فهكذا ينبغي، لأن التغيير والإتباع إنما جاء في الهمزة، ولم يأت في الميم،

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r3.claim: Ḥamza's kasra is explained as vowel harmony from the hamza to the mīm, a pattern that requires transmitted usage; منحدر is an analogy.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r3.anchor: ووجهه أنه أتبع الميم الهمزة، كما قالوا: منحدر من الجبل، فأتبعوا حركة الدال ما بعدها،

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r4.claim: The forms عليهمي and عليهمو ولا support the two readings respectively: the former extends yāʾ-like kasra through hāʾ to mīm, while the latter extends the wāw-like ḍamma to mīm.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p138/r4.anchor: ويقوي ذلك قول من قال: عليهمي ولا [الفاتحة/ 7] ألا ترى أنه أتبع الهاء الياء ثم أتبع الميم الهاء،

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r1.speaker: عمران بن حصين
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r1.claim: ʿImran ibn Husayn treats mothers of wives as mothers among those prohibited in marriage.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة عن عمران بن حصين في قوله تعالى ﴿ وأمهات نسائكم ﴾ قال هي مما حرم الأم

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r2.speaker: مسروق بن الأجدع
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r2.claim: Masruq calls the prohibition of mothers of wives unqualified and says to leave the matter as stated.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r2.anchor: قال وقال مسروق بن الأجدع وسئل عنها فقال إنها مبهمة فدعها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r3.speaker: الحسن والزهري
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Zuhri are reported to disapprove of the case concerning mothers of wives.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r3.anchor: قال معمر وكان الحسن والزهري يكرهانها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r4.speaker: طاوس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r4.claim: Ṭawus is also reported to disapprove of the case concerning mothers of wives.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي طاوس عن أبيه أنه كرهها أيضا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud lists further prohibited or disliked unions involving slave women, including combining sisters, a slave woman previously intimate with one’s father or son, a fornicator, one in another’s waiting period, and one with a husband.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة أن ابن مسعود قال حرم الله اثنتي عشرة امرأة وأنا أكرهثنتي عشرة الأمة وأمها وبنتها والأختين يجمع بينهما

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r6.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r6.claim: Al-Nakhaʿi says Ibn Masʿud treated sale of a slave woman as divorce and disapproved of a polytheist slave woman and paternal or maternal aunts by nursing.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p152#2/r6.anchor: قال النخعي وكان ابن مسعود يقول بيعها طلاقها واكره أمتك مشركة وعمتك من الرضاعة وخالتك من الرضاعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r1.speaker: الطحاوي وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r1.claim: They explain the stepdaughters' association with the household as describing the usual case; stepdaughters remain forbidden even when they are not actually in the man's custody.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r1.anchor: إضافتهن إلى الحجور حملا على أغلب ما يكون الربائب، وهي محرمة وإن لم تكن في الحجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes “in your households” as explaining the prohibition: the girls are or may be raised by you, and after intercourse with their mothers they function like your own daughters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r2.anchor: فائدته التعليل للتحريم، وأنهن لاحتضانكم لهن، أو لكونهن بصدد احتضانكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r3.claim: The phrase “from your wives who you have entered” appears to modify only the stepdaughters clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r3.anchor: من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن ظاهر هذا أنه متعلق بقوله: وربائبكم فقط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r4.claim: The relative pronoun modifies the wives governed by من, not the wives in “mothers of your wives,” because the two phrases have different grammatical governors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r4.anchor: واللاتي: صفة لنسائكم المجرور بمن، ولا جائز أن يكون اللاتي وصفا لنسائكم من قوله: وأمهات نسائكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r5.claim: The phrase cannot be attached to an omitted element governing both mothers-in-law and stepdaughters: من identifies which wives for the former but marks origin for the latter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r5.anchor: لاختلاف مدلول حرف الجر إذ ذاك، لأنه بالنسبة إلى قوله: وأمهات نسائكم يكون من نسائكم لبيان النساء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari proposes attaching من نسائكم to both wives and stepdaughters, taking من to mean connection, as in the verse and cited expressions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r6.anchor: إلا أن أعلقه بالنساء والربائب، وأجعل من للاتصال كقوله تعالى: المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan says no one recognizes “connection” as a meaning of من; the cited verse, poetry, and report have other explanations, and the proposed attachment makes the mothers-in-law phrase redundant and unidiomatic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p580/r7.anchor: ولا نعلم أحدا ذهب إلى أن من معاني من الاتصال. وأما ما شبه به من الآية والشعر والحديث، فمتأول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r1.claim: Entering upon a woman is a euphemism for intercourse, as in expressions meaning that a man built over her or put a veil over her.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r1.anchor: والدخول هنا كناية عن الجماع لقولهم: بنى عليها، وضرب عليها الحجاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وطاوس وابن دينار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r2.claim: They take the bāʾ as causative, meaning the women brought under the covering; on this view a man divorced after the wedding but before intercourse may marry her daughter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r2.anchor: والباء: للتعدية، والمعنى: اللاتي أدخلتموهن الستر قاله: ابن عباس، وطاوس، وابن دينار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r3.speaker: عطاء ومالك وأبو حنيفة والثوري والأوزاعي والليث والشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r3.claim: These jurists, in one of al-Shafiʿi's positions, hold that touching the woman with desire makes both her mother and daughter forbidden, as well as making her forbidden to the man's father and son.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء، ومالك، وأبو حنيفة، والثوري، والأوزاعي، والليث: إذا مسها بشهوة حرمت عليه أمها وابنتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r4.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى والشافعي ومالك والكوفيون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r4.claim: On lustful looking, Ibn Abi Layla and al-Shafiʿi require touching; Malik counts looking pleasurably at hair or beauty; the Kufans count lustful looking at the genital area.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r4.anchor: واختلفوا في النظر إليها بشهوة، فقال ابن أبي ليلى: لا يحرم النظر حتى تلمس، وهو قول الشافعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r5.speaker: الثوري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r5.claim: Al-Thawri says looking at her genital area is prohibitive when deliberate, without stipulating desire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r5.anchor: وقال الثوري: يحرم إذا كان تعمد النظر إلى فرجها، ولم يذكر الشهوة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r6.speaker: عطاء وحماد بن أبي سليمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r6.claim: They say looking at a woman's genital area bars marriage to her mother or daughter, and extend this ruling to enslaved women.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء، وحماد بن أبي سليمان: إذا نظر إلى فرج امرأة فلا ينكح أمها ولا ابنتها، وعدوا هذا الحكم إلى الإماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r7.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says an enslaved woman is never lawful for the owner's son if he has touched her lustfully, uncovered her, or kissed her.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن: إذا ملك الأمة وغمزها بشهوة، أو كشفها، أو قبلها، لا تحل لولده بحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r8.speaker: مسروق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r8.claim: Masruq ordered that his enslaved woman be sold after his death, saying even his limited touching and looking had made her forbidden to his son.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r8.anchor: وأمر مسروق أن تباع جاريته بعد موته وقال: أما إني لم أصب منها إلا ما يحرمها على ولدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r9.speaker: عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r9.claim: Umar stripped an enslaved woman with whom he had been alone; when his son asked for her, Umar said she was not lawful to him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r9.anchor: وجرد عمر أمة خلا بها فاستوهبها ابن له فقال: لا تحل لك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r10.claim: “No blame if you did not enter upon them” means no blame in marrying the stepdaughters, but permission also presupposes separation from their mothers by divorce or the mothers' death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r10.anchor: وليس جواز نكاح الربائب موقوفا على انتفاء مطلق الدخول، بل لا بد من محذوف مقدر تقديره: فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن، وفارقتموهن بطلاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r11.claim: The jurists agree that a father's contracted wife is forbidden to his son and a son's contracted wife to his father, whether intercourse occurred; حليلة means wife rather than an enslaved concubine, so the contract itself suffices.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r11.anchor: أجمعوا على تحريم ما عقد عليه الآباء على الأبناء، وما عقد عليه الأبناء على الآباء كان مع العقد وطء، أو لم يكن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r12.claim: “From your loins” limits sons to biological sons and removes the metaphorical sense used for adopted sons; the verse about Muhammad not being the father of any of their men addresses that usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r12.anchor: وجاء الذين من أصلابكم وهو وصف لقوله: أبنائكم، برفع المجاز الذي يحتمله لفظ أبنائكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r13.claim: The Prophet married Zaynab bint Jahsh after Zayd ibn Harithah divorced her, and jurists agree a foster son's wife is forbidden just like a biological son's wife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p581/r13.anchor: وقد تزوج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زينب بنت جحش الأسدية وهي بنت عمته، أميمة بنت عبد المطلب حين فارقها زيد بن حارثة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r1.claim: The prohibited women are prohibited as objects of marriage, not as persons: legal prohibition concerns acts, marriage is the salient intended act, and the surrounding context concerns marriage; therefore the verse is not ambiguous, contrary to al-Karkhī.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r1.anchor: والمراد تحريم نكاحهن لأنه معظم ما يقصد منهن ولأنه المتبادر إلى الفهم ولأن ما قبله وما بعده في النكاح

ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r2.claim: The author regards the clause as performative rather than a report of a past prohibition; some investigators allow a report-like reading, taking the past form as timeless as in formal definitions.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r2.anchor: والجملة إنشائية وليس المقصود منها الإخبار عن التحريم في الزمان الماضي وقال بعض المحققين : لا مانع

ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r3.claim: The passive form is used because it is obvious that God is the one who made these women forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r3.anchor: وبني الفعل لما لم يسم فاعله لأنه لا يشتبه أن المحرم هو الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.claim: “Your mothers” includes grandmothers at every level because “mother” denotes an origin, as in “Mother of the Book” and “Mother of Cities”; on this analysis the term's true sense includes them.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r4.anchor: و ( أمهاتكم ) تعم الجدات كيف كن إذ الأم هي الأصل في الأصل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r5.claim: Some treat “mother” for a grandmother as figurative and establish the prohibition by consensus; the author says the intended meaning is “origin” either way, so grandmothers fall under the general figurative usage, with consensus identifying that intent.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r5.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى أن إطلاق الأم على الجدة مجاز وأن إثبات حرمة الجدات بالإجماع

ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r6.claim: Daughters include one's own daughter and descendants' daughters: “daughter” can truly mean a branch, or may be extended to descendants figuratively; even those who deny that extension accept their prohibition by consensus.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r6.anchor: والمراد بالبنات من ولدتها أو ولدت من ولدها وتسمية الثانية بنتا حقيقة بإعتبار أن البنت يراد به الفرع

ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r7.claim: The prohibition of grandmothers and descendants' daughters can also follow from the text's indication: aunts are daughters of grandmothers, and descendants' daughters are closer than nieces, so the nearer relations are prohibited a fortiori.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r7.anchor: قد يستدل على تحريم الجدات وبنات الأولاد بدلالة النص

ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.claim: The verse's apparent Arabic meaning prohibits marrying one's biological daughter born of fornication, since no evidence transfers the ordinary meaning of “daughter” to a technical legal meaning here.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r8.anchor: ثم ظاهر النص يدل على أنه يحرم للرجل بنته من الزنا لأنها بنته والخطاب إنما هو باللغة العربية مالم يثبت نقل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r9.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r9.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī permits the fornication-born daughter to her biological father because lineage and its other legal consequences are not established for her, citing the Prophetic dictum that a child belongs to the marital bed.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p249#2/r9.anchor: وفي ذلك خلاف الإمام الشافعي رضي ا لله تعالى عنه فقد قال : إن المخلوقة من ماء الزنا تحل للزاني

ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r1.speaker: بعض الشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r1.claim: Some Shāfiʿīs say the daughter becomes forbidden if the Prophet Jesus, at his descent, informs the man that she was conceived from his semen; the author replies that the Lawgiver severed her lineage from him, so her physical origin is irrelevant.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r1.anchor: وقال بعض الشافعية : تحرم إن أخبره نبيكعيس عليه السلاموقت نزوله

ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r2.claim: Opponents of the prohibition argue that biological paternity cannot suffice: a man who buys a virgin, deflowers her, and later fathers a child is not automatically assigned that child without acknowledgment; legal lineage cannot suffice either, since Muslim consensus denies the fornication-born child lineage from the fornicator.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r2.anchor: وأعترضوا على القائلين بالحرمة بأنهم إما أن يثبتوا كونها بنتا له بناءا على الحقيقة لكونها مخلوقة من مائه أو بناءا على حكم الشرع

ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r3.claim: The author answers that biological fact makes a person the daughter of the man whose semen produced her, whether licitly or illicitly; physical part-wholeness is the basis of the marriage prohibition, and the mother is certainly forbidden her own child born of fornication.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r3.anchor: وأجيب بإختيار الشق الأول إذ لا خلاف بين أهل اللسان في أن المخلوقة من ماء إنسان بنته سواء كان ذلك الماء ماء حلال أو سفاح

ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r4.claim: The distinction between a child separating bodily from its mother and a daughter separating from her father only mentally does not disprove shared substance; Arabic calls a child a piece of its father, and absence of inheritance from the father is due to consensus, not lack of true daughterhood.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250/r4.anchor: والتفرقة بين المسألتين بأن الولد في المسألة الثانية بعضها وأنفصل منها إنسانا ولا كذلك البنت في المسألة الأولى لأنها أنفصلت منه ذهنيا لا تفيد سوى أن البعضية في المسألة الثانية أظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r1.claim: In the school discussion of a concubine's child, Abū Ḥanīfa says that if the master did not withdraw and protected her from suspicion, religious duty obliges him to claim the child; withdrawal or failure to protect her creates a contrary presumption allowing denial.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r1.anchor: فالمروى عن أبي حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنهأنه إن كان حين وطئها لم يعزل عنها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r2.speaker: أبو يوسف
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r2.claim: Abū Yūsuf says a master must claim a child born before he performed post-intercourse waiting, whether or not he withdrew or protected the woman, out of good opinion of her; this matches the majority.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r2.anchor: وعن أبي يوسف إذا وطئها ولم يستبرئها بعد ذلك حتى جاءت بولد فعليه ان يدعيه سواء عزل عنها أو لم يعزل حصنها أو لم يحصنها تحسينا للظن بها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r3.speaker: محمد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r3.claim: Muḥammad says the master should not claim the child if he does not know it is his, but should free the child; al-Īḍāḥ presents both Abū Yūsuf's claim and Muḥammad's emancipation as recommendations.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r3.anchor: وعن محمد لا ينبغي أن يدعي ولدها إذا لم يعلم أنه منه ولكن ينبغي أن يعتق الولد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r4.speaker: بعض فضلاء الدرس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r4.claim: A scholar in the lesson argues that admission of intercourse aimed at procreation, or admission that the master did not withdraw and protected the woman, should establish lineage without requiring a separate statement “this is my son”; the author sees no obstacle to adopting this position in the school.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا قال بعض فضلاء الدرس : ينبغي أنه لو أقر أنه كان لا يعزل عنها وحصنها أن يثبت نسبه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r5.claim: Al-Mabsūṭ says that a long delay supports assigning the child to the master because his conduct, such as accepting congratulations, indicates acknowledgment and functions like an explicit admission.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p250#2/r5.anchor: وفي المبسوط أنه إذا تطاول الزمان ألحق به لأن التطاول دليل إقراره لأنه يوجد منه حينئذ ما يدل على الإقرار من قبول التهنئة ونحوه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r1.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r1.claim: Al-Baḥr distinguishes proof in court, which requires a claim, from the relation established before God, for which jurists do not require one.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r1.anchor: إن أراد الثبوت عند القاضي ظاهرا فقد صرحوا أنه لا بد من الدعوة مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r2.claim: A child conceived from the master's semen is his child in reality; an illegitimate child is likewise, with acknowledgment strengthening the case.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r2.anchor: المولود ولد للمولى في نفس الأمر لأنه مخلوق من مائه وولد الزنا كذلك وزيادة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r3.claim: Since the prohibition rests on filiation, real filiation makes marriage forbidden before God, even when inheritance and judicial attribution are not established.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r3.anchor: والله سبحانه جعل مناط الحرمة البنوة وهي متحققة في مسألتنا فكيف يحل النكاح في نفس الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r4.claim: A fact may be true without judicial proof, and a judicial ruling may not match reality; he illustrates this with the Prophet's horse purchase and Khuzayma's testimony.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r4.anchor: فكم متحقق في نفس الأمر لا يقضى به وكم مقضى به غير متحقق في نفس الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r5.claim: One cannot conclusively deny conception from the husband in an east-west marriage, since extraordinary travel or a jinn could make intercourse possible.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r5.anchor: فلا نسلم القطع فيها بأن الولد ليس مخلوقا من مائه لثبوت كرامات الأولياء

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r6.speaker: الأصحاب
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r6.claim: The jurists deny a boy's paternity of a child born to his wife because intercourse is inconceivable; physical possibility is required, and marriage alone does not suffice.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r6.anchor: لو جاءت أمرأة الصبي بولد لم يثبت نسبه منه لعدم تصور ذلك هناك والتصور شرط

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r7.claim: Judicial attribution can serve as a protective presumption; in reality, a husband's child must derive from his semen, while the presumption protects free women and prevents a child being abandoned.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r7.anchor: ولعل إعتبار هذه البنوة قضاءا وإلا فحيث لم يكن الولد مخلوقا من مائه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r8.speaker: الشافعي ومالك وأحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r8.claim: In the law of a slave concubine, these jurists attribute a child to the master when he admits intercourse even with withdrawal; anal intercourse also entails paternity for Malik and a weak Shafi‘i position.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r8.anchor: الجارية إذا ولدت يثبت نسب الولد من المولى إذا أقر بوطئها مع العزل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r9.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r9.claim: One view says the east-west marriage case is far less plausible than concubine paternity, where intercourse is at least established without an impossible journey.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r9.anchor: وقيل : إن بين هذه المسألة ومسألة تزويج المشرقي بمغربية بعدا كبعد ما بين المشرق والمغرب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r10.claim: The plural banāt is commonly derived from bint, whose lām is correctly said to be wāw; the deleted element returns in akhawāt but not in banāt, whose masculine is banūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r10.anchor: والبنات جمع بنت في المشهور وصحح أن لامها واو كأخت وإنما رد المحذوف في أخوات ولم يرد في بنات

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r11.speaker: الدنوشري
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r11.claim: A poem poses the morphological puzzle of why the plural of ukht restores its lost letter while the plural of bint does not, although both use a compensating tāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r11.anchor: وقد نظم الدنوشري السؤال فقال : أيها الفاضل اللبيب تفضل بجواب به يكون رشادي

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r12.claim: His proposed answer is that ukht carries a prefix connection suited to wāw, so it takes the lost letter back.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r12.anchor: لفظ أخت له إنضمام بصدر ناسب الواو فأكتسي بالمعاد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r13.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r13.claim: Abū al-Baqā argues that tāʾ in these forms is not feminine, since feminine tāʾ would follow a vowel and become hāʾ at pause; he analyzes banāt as banah.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r13.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء : التاء فيها ليست للتأنيث لأن تاء التأنيث لا يسكن ما قبلها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r14.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r14.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the kasra in banāt as a signal of an omitted letter; other grammarians take the original vowel as fatḥa, matching banūn, the Basran view.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r14.anchor: فبنات ليس بجمع بنت بل بنه وكسرت الباء تنبيها على المحذوف قاله الفراء

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r15.claim: In akhawāt the tāʾ replaces wāw, and the listed aunts include sisters across all three parental lines.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r15.anchor: وما أخت فالتاء فيها بدل من الواو لأنها من الأخوة والأخوات ينتظمن الأخوات من الجهات الثلاث

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r16.claim: Paternal and maternal aunts include descendants of grandparents at every generation, and this extension is agreed by consensus.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r16.anchor: ويدخل في العمات والخالات أولاد الأجداد والجدات وإن علوا وكذا عمة جده وخالته

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r17.speaker: الخانية والمحيط
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r17.claim: An aunt of an aunt is forbidden when the nearer aunt is paternal or both-sided, but not when she is maternal; the ruling follows whether the connection reaches a blood grandparent or only a grandfather's wife.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r17.anchor: وأما عمة العمة لأم فلا تحرم وفي المحيط : وأما عمة العمة فإن كانت العمة القربى

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r18.speaker: المحيط
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r18.claim: For an aunt of a maternal aunt, the aunt is forbidden when the nearer aunt is both-sided or maternal, but not when she is paternal, since the relevant link is a grandfather's wife.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r18.anchor: وأما خالة الخالة فإن كانت الخالة القربى خالة لأب وأم أو لأم فخالتها تحرم عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r19.claim: The same listed kinship prohibitions apply reciprocally to a woman marrying the corresponding male relatives.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p251/r19.anchor: كما يحرم على الرجل أن يتزوج بمن ذكر يحرم على المرأة التزوج بنظير من ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r1.claim: The verse's prohibitions were not necessarily present in every religion, although mothers and daughters were forbidden even in Adam's time.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r1.anchor: والظاهر أن هذا التحريم الذي دلت عليه الآية لم يثبت في جميع المذكورات في سائر الأديان

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r2.claim: Some claimed Zoroaster permitted marriage to mothers and daughters; most Muslims considered him a liar.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r2.anchor: وقيل : إن زرادشت نبي المجوس بزعمهم قال بحله وأكثر المسلمين أتفقوا على أنه كان كذابا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r3.claim: Zoroaster's reported survival of molten metal is no miracle, since medicines can protect people from fire, as the author says he has witnessed.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r3.anchor: عدم إيذاء الصفر المذاب له لأدوية كان يلطخ بها جسده

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r4.claim: A reported account says sibling marriage was permitted among Adam's children from necessity, with each twin pair marrying a sibling from another birth.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r4.anchor: وأما حل نكاح الأخوات فقد قيل : إنه كان مباحا في زمان آدم عليه السلام للضرورة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r5.speaker: بعض المسلمين
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r5.claim: Some Muslims reject that account and say houris were sent from Paradise to marry Adam's sons; al-Ālūsī rejects this because their descendants would not then be solely Adam's offspring, contrary to consensus.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r5.anchor: وبعض المسلمين ينكر ذلك ويقول : إنه بعث الحور من الجنة حتى تزوج بهن أبناء آدم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r6.claim: The source lists variants of riḍāʿ, including forms with different vowels and a reciprocal form; the form with ḍamma implies shared nursing.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r6.anchor: والرضاعة بفتح الراء مصدر رضع كسمع وضرب ومثله الرضاعة بالكسر والرضع بسكون الضاء وفتحها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r7.claim: A woman is called murḍiʿ while she has a child to nurse, but murḍiʿa when described as nursing the child.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r7.anchor: ويقال : أرضعت المرأة فهي مرضع إذا كان لها ولد ترضعه فإن وصفتها بإرضاع الولد قلت : مرضعة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r8.claim: Nursing means milk from a human woman's breast reaching an infant's stomach through mouth or nose during the legally relevant period; actual sucking is not required.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r8.anchor: ومعناها لغة مص الثدي وشرعا مص الرضيع من ثدي الآدمية في وقت مخصوص

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r9.speaker: الخانية
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r9.claim: Suckling is only the usual cause of milk reaching the stomach, so pouring milk through the nose and similar methods count as well.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r9.anchor: وإنما ذكروا المص لأنه سبب للوصول فأطلقوا السبب وأرادوا المسبب وقد صرح في الخانية أنه لا فرق بين المص والسعوط

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r10.speaker: البخاري
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī says al-Bukhārī alone held that a boy and girl nursing from a goat become milk kin, and calls this the cause of his ordeal.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r10.anchor: وتفرد الإمام البخاريوهو سبب فتنته في قولفذهب فيما إذا أرتضع صبي وصبية من ثدي شاة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r11.claim: The definition covers virgin or previously married women, alive or dead; limiting it to humans excludes men and animals.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r11.anchor: وأطلقت لتشمل البكر والثيب الحية والميتة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r12.claim: Milk reaching through the mouth or nose counts, while entry through the ear, urethra, wounds, head injury, or enema is excluded in the apparent position.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r12.anchor: وقيدنا بالفم والأنف ليخرج ما إذا وصل بالأقطار في الأذن والأحليل والجائفة والآمة وبالحقنة في ظاهر الرواية

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r13.claim: If a nursing infant only takes the nipple into the mouth and milk entry is uncertain, marriage is not prohibited because the operative cause is doubtful.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r13.anchor: لا يحرم النكاح لأن في المانع شكا وقد نزل الله سبحانه الرضاعة منزلة النسب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r14.claim: Milk kinship makes the wet nurse a mother and a co-nursed girl a sister; the wet nurse's husband is the child's father, his parents grandparents, and his sister an aunt.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r14.anchor: حتى سمى المرضعة أما للرضيع والمراضعة أختا وكذلك زوج المرضعة أبوه وأبواه جداه وأخته عمته

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r15.claim: All children of the wet nurse's husband are the infant's paternal siblings, including those born before or after nursing; children she bears with him are full siblings.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r15.anchor: وكل ولد ولد له من غير المرضعة قبل الرضاع وبعده فهم إخوته وأخواته لأبيه وأم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r16.claim: The wet nurse's mother is a grandmother and her sister an aunt; children she has with another husband are maternal siblings of the nursed child.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r16.anchor: وأم المرضعة جدته وأختها خالته وكل ولد لها من هذا الزوج فهم إخوته وأخواته

ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r17.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r17.claim: A report from ʿĀʾisha and Ibn ʿAbbās, recorded by al-Bukhārī and Muslim, states that nursing forbids the same relations as lineage.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p252/r17.anchor: ومن هنا قال صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فيما أخرجه البخاري ومسلم من حديث عائشة وإبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهم : يحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم بالنسب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r1.speaker: كثير من المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r1.claim: Many investigators, including Shaykh al-Islām, read the hadith's rule universally; apparent exceptions are prohibited through affinity rather than lineage.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r1.anchor: وذهب كثير من المحققين كمولانا شيخ الإسلام وغيره إلى أن الحديث جار على عمومه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r2.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r2.claim: Al-Baḥr enumerates eighty-one exceptions to the hadith's general rule and treats the subject at length.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r2.anchor: وأنهى في البحر المسائل المستثنيات إلى إحدى وثمانين مسألة وأطال الكلام في هذا المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r3.claim: The verse indicates that little or much nursing creates prohibition once milk reaches the infant's stomach; the Muslim report denying prohibition from one or two sucklings is abrogated.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r3.anchor: وظاهر الآية أنه لا فرق بين قليل الرضاع وهو ما يعلم وصوله إلى الجوف وكثيره في التحريم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās said that the rule denying prohibition from one or two sucklings applied earlier and was then abrogated.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r4.anchor: قيل له : إن الناس يقولون : إن الرضعة لا تحرم فقال : كان ذلك ثم نسخ

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd said the final rule is that little and much nursing both prohibit.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r5.anchor: وعن إبن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه قال : آل أمر الرضاع إلى أن قليله وكثيره يحرم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar is reported to say even a small amount prohibits; when told al-Zubayr permitted one or two sucklings, he recited the verse and preferred God's ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r6.anchor: وعنه أنه قيل له : إن الزبير يقول : لا باس بالرضعة والرضعتين فقال : قضاء الله تعالى خير من قضاء إبن الزبير

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r7.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r7.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires five full sucklings at separate, conventionally distinct times for prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r7.anchor: وقال الشافعي عليه الرحمة على ما نقله أصحابنا عنه لا يثبت التحريم إلا بخمس رضعات مشبعات في خمسة أوقات متفاصلة عرفا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r8.speaker: أحمد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r8.claim: Aḥmad has two transmitted positions: one matching the Hanafis and one matching al-Shāfiʿī.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r9.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r9.claim: Shafi‘i proponents cite a report from al-Zubayr in Ibn Ḥibbān's Ṣaḥīḥ denying prohibition from one or two sucklings or nursing actions; they infer prohibition begins at five.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r9.anchor: وأستدل على ذلك بما أخرجه إبن حبان في صحيحه من حديث الزبير أنه قال : قال صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : لا تحرم المصة والمصتان ولا الإملاجة والإملاجتان

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r10.speaker: إبن الهمام
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r10.claim: Ibn al-Humām objects that al-Shāfiʿī requires five satiations at separate times, not five individual sucks, and that sucking is the infant's act while imlāj is the nurse's.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r10.anchor: أما أولا فلأن مذهب الشافعي ليس التحريم بخمس مصات بل بخمس شبعات في أوقات

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r11.speaker: إبن الهمام
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r11.claim: He further argues that imlāj is not itself the cause but a consequence of nursing, so denying two imlājas only denies their corresponding sucklings.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r11.anchor: أما ثانيا فلأن المصة فعل الرضيع والإملاجة إلا رضاعة فعل المرضعة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r12.speaker: إبن الهمام
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r12.claim: Combining both wordings as one report would duplicate the same denial and cannot establish a four-suckling threshold; al-Zubayr likely combined two statements heard on separate occasions.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p253/r12.anchor: وعلى هذا يجب كون الراوي وهو الزبير رضي الله تعالى عنهأراد أن يجمع بين ألفاظه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم التي سمعها منه في وقتين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r1.claim: Another argument says the report disproves the Imam's view and establishes al-Shāfiʿī's because no one distinguishes between them; the author reports a rebuttal from hadith imams who held three sucklings.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r1.anchor: وقيل : في وجه الإستدلال طريق آخر وهو أن الحديث ناف لماذهب إليه الإمام الأعظم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r2.speaker: أبو ثور وإبن المنذر وداؤد وأبو عبيد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r2.claim: These hadith authorities held that three sucklings prohibit; the author says their view cannot be dismissed and has a stronger rationale than al-Shāfiʿī's.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r2.anchor: أبو ثور وإبن المنذر وداؤد وأبو عبيد وهؤلاء أئمة الحديث قالوا : المحرم ثلاث رضعات

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r3.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r3.claim: A Muslim report from ʿĀʾisha says ten known sucklings were revealed, then abrogated by five; the Prophet died while the latter wording was still recited.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r3.anchor: وأستدل بعض أصحابه على هذا المطلب بما رواه مسلم عن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت : كان فيما نزل من القرآن عشر رضعات معلومات يحرمن ثم نسخن بخمس رضعات معلومات يحرمن

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r4.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r4.claim: Another version says the written passage lay on a sheet under her bed and domestic birds ate it after the Prophet died.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r4.anchor: أنه كان في صحيفة تحت سريري

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r5.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r5.claim: In ʿĀʾisha's report about Sahlah and Salim, the Prophet tells her to nurse Salim five times so she may receive him; Shafi‘i proponents cite it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r5.anchor: وبما روى عن عائشة أيضا قالت : جاءت سهلة بنت سهيل أمرأة أبي حذيفة إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت : يارسول الله إني أرى في وجه أبي حذيفة من دخول سالم وهو حليفه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r6.claim: The Hanafi response is that all these reports are abrogated, as Ibn ʿAbbās explicitly said earlier.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254/r6.anchor: والجواب أن جميع ذلك منسوخ كما صرح بذلك إبن عباس فيما مر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r1.claim: The birds' consumption does not disprove abrogation; the passage may have been recently written and not yet washed away when the birds entered.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r1.anchor: وما في الرواية لا ينافي النسخ لجواز أن يقال : إنها رضي الله تعالى عنها أرادت أنه كان مكتوبا ولم يغسل بعد للقرب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r2.claim: The claim that recitation was abrogated while the ruling remained is unsupported: ordinarily removing a text also removes its ruling unless separate evidence preserves it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r2.anchor: والقول بأن ما ذكر إنما يلزم منه نسخ التلاوة فيجوز أن تكون التلاوة منسوخة مع بقاء الحكمكالشيخ والشيخة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r3.claim: The stoning example only preserves a ruling because Sunnah and consensus establish it; it cannot by itself support retaining a rule after its text is abrogated.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r3.anchor: لولا ما علم بالسنة والإجماع لم يثبت به

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r4.claim: Sahlah's instruction cannot mean five full, separate feeds to satiate adult Salim, since that much milk is ordinarily impossible for a woman to provide.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r4.anchor: أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لم يرد أن يشبع سالما خمس رضعات في خمسة أوقات متفاصلات جائعا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r5.speaker: القاضي
