ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r5.claim: Perhaps the five refer to measured suckling actions; al-Qāḍī suggests that she expressed an amount equivalent to five feeds for Salim to drink, though the author calls the report problematic.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r5.anchor: فلعل المراد أن تحلب له شيئا مقداره خمس رضعات فيشربهكما قال القاضي

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r6.claim: The report would otherwise make adult nursing legally effective, since Salim was then a man, a position rejected by the four imams.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r6.anchor: وقد يقال : هو منسوخ من وجه آخر لأنه يدل على أن الرضاع في الكبر يوجب التحريم لأن سالما كان إذ ذاك رجلا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r7.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa sets the nursing period that creates prohibition at thirty months.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r7.anchor: فإن مدة الرضاع التي يتعلق به التحريم ثلاثون شهرا عند الإمام الأعظم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r8.speaker: صاحبا أبي حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r8.claim: Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad set the period at two years; the author says their evidence is very strong and that three imams also adopt this limit.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r8.anchor: وسنتان عند صاحبيه ومستندهما قوي جدا وإلى ذلك ذهب الأئمة الثلاثة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r9.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r9.claim: Mālik has several reported limits: two years plus one month, two months, or days, and in another view as long as the child needs milk.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r9.anchor: وعن مالك : سنتان وشهر وفي رواية أخرى شهران وفي أخرى سنتان وأيام وفي أخرى مادام محتاجا إلى اللبن

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r10.speaker: زفر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r10.claim: Zufar sets the nursing limit at three years; other scholars report limits of fifteen or forty years.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r10.anchor: وقال : زفر ثلاث سنين نعم قال بعضهم : خمس عشرة سنة وقال آخرون : أربون سنة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r11.speaker: داؤد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r11.claim: Dāwūd holds that adult nursing also prohibits and sets no age limit, a view also transmitted from ʿĀʾisha.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r11.anchor: وقال داؤد : الإرضاع في الكبر محرم أيضا ولا حد للمدة وهو مروى عن عائشة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r12.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r12.claim: When ʿĀʾisha wanted a man to enter, she would have her sister Umm Kulthūm or a niece nurse him.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r12.anchor: وكانت إذا أرادت أن يدخل عليها أحد من الرجال أمرت أختها أم كلثوم أو بعض بنات أختها أن ترضعه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r13.speaker: أم سلمة وسائر أزواج النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r13.claim: Umm Salama and the Prophet's other wives disagreed with ʿĀʾisha's adult-nursing practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r13.anchor: وروى مسلم عن أم سلمة وسائر أزواج النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r14.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري وإبن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r14.claim: A man told Abū Mūsā that milk from his wife's breast entered his stomach; Abū Mūsā judged her forbidden, but Ibn Masʿūd said nursing counts only within two years, and Abū Mūsā deferred to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r14.anchor: وفي الموطأ وسنن أبي داؤد عن يحيى بن سعيد أن رجلا سأل أبا موسى الأشعري فقال : إني مصصت من أمرأتي ثديها لبنا فذهب في بطني

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r15.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r15.claim: When a man said his wife had nursed his slave girl to make her forbidden to him, ʿUmar told him to resume relations with the slave, since only infant nursing counts.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r15.anchor: وفيه عن إبن عمر جاء رجل إلى عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه فقال : كانت لي وليدة فكنت أصيبها فعمدت أمرأتي إليها فأرضعتها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r16.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r16.claim: Al-Tirmidhī grades as sound a report from Umm Salama stating that only nursing that reaches the intestines at the breast before weaning prohibits.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r16.anchor: وروى الترمذيوقال حديث صحيحمن حديث أم سلمة أنه قال صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : لا يحرم من الرضاع إلا فتق الأمعاء في الثدي وكان قبل الفطام

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r17.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r17.claim: An Abū Dāwūd report from Ibn Masʿūd says only nursing that forms flesh and strengthens bones prohibits.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r17.anchor: وفي سنن أبي داؤد من حديث إبن مسعود يرفعه لا يحرم من الرضاع إلا ما أنبت اللحم وأنشز العظم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r18.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r18.claim: In a Ṣaḥīḥayn report from ʿĀʾisha, the Prophet tells her to verify who her milk brothers are and says nursing is only that of infancy.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r18.anchor: في الصحيحين عنها أنها قالت : دخل على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعندي رجل فقال : ياعائشة من هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r19.claim: Al-Ālūsī privileges ʿĀʾisha's transmitted report over her legal opinion, which he regards as inattentive and mistaken in its reasoning.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r19.anchor: وأعتبر مرويها دون رأيها لظهور غفلتها فيه وعدم وقوع إجتهادها على المحز

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r20.speaker: كثير من العلماء
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r20.claim: Many scholars suspect ʿĀʾisha later retracted after learning of abrogation, as Abū Mūsā had done.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r20.anchor: ولهذا قيل : يشبه أنها رجعت كما رجع أبو موسى لما تحقق عندها النسخ

ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r21.speaker: كثير من العلماء
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r21.claim: Many scholars treat the Salim report as a dispensation specific to Sahlah and Salim; they also treat permission to touch the private area as a special ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p254#2/r21.anchor: وحمل كثير من العلماء حديث سهلة على أنه مختص بها وبسالم وجعلوا أيضا العفو عن مباشرة العورة من الخواص

ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r1.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r1.claim: Al-Suyūṭī's maqāma challenges Ibn al-Karkiy to explain why the verse's wording seems to signal five sucklings, while the reversed wording would suggest one.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r1.anchor: ماذا صنعت بالسؤال المهم الذي دار في البلد ولم يجب عنه أحد وهو الفرق بين قوله تعالى : ( وأمهاتكم اللاتي أرضعنكم ) وبين مالو قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī proposes that the phrase distinguishes nursing mothers from the mothers already mentioned, with nursing considered five times in the syntax: verb, subject, object, relative clause, and adjective.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r2.anchor: فأتى سبحانه بقوله : ( اللاتي أرضعنكم ) بيانا لذلك دافعا لتوهم التكرار فكان القيد الأرضاع الواقع صلة معتنا به أتم إعتناء

ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r3.claim: He takes those five syntactic considerations as a rhetorical indication that five sucklings establish milk-motherhood, not as proof; the legal school instead relies on reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r3.anchor: فهذه خمس ملاحظات للأرضاع في هذا التركيب تشير إلى أن ما به تحصل الأمومة خمس رضعات

ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r4.claim: The verse's rhetorical form exemplifies how textual structure can suggest a real relation, as with the marital reciprocity expressed in 2:228.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r4.anchor: مثل ما وقع في قوله تعالى : ( ولهن مثل الذي عليهن بالمعروف ) من الإحتباك المشير إلى ما بين الزوجين من الإئتلاف

ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r5.claim: He says the assimilation in yamill in 2:282 may indicate the speaker's tongue is tied, as many exegetes hold.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r5.anchor: وما وقع في قوله تعالى : ( أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو فليملل وليه ) من الإدغام في ( يمل ) المشير إلى حال الفاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r6.claim: He says the unchanging order in “each in an orbit” may signal the celestial spheres' roundness, according to one view.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p255/r6.anchor: وما وقع في قوله تعالى : ( كل في فلك ) من عدم الإستحالة بالإنعكاس المشير إلى كرية الإفلاك في رأى

ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the fivefold reading is only a rhetorical indication that strengthens an argument; jurists requiring five sucklings based their rule on reports, not this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r1.anchor: وليس هذا من باب الإستدلال بل من باب الإشارة المقوية له ألا ترى أنه لم يستدل أحد ممن ذهب إلى إشتراط الخمس بهذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r2.claim: The hypothetical reversed wording lacks a reason to distinguish these mothers from a prior mention, so nursing need only be considered once, at the minimum needed to establish the category.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r2.anchor: لأن العطف فيه لا يوهم التكرار لعدم تقدم نظيره فلا يشرأب الذهن إلى ما يذكر بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r3.claim: Because the phrase would follow “your mothers” as an apposition, its emphasis could signal that even one suckling creates the surprising prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r3.anchor: بل يكفي إعتباره مرة واحدة وهي أدنى ما تتحقق به الماهية لا سيما وقد ذكر بعد ( أمهاتكم ) على أنه بدل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r4.speaker: النووي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r4.claim: A version of al-Nawawī's commentary reports that Mālik used the verse to argue for prohibition after one suckling because it specifies no number.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r4.anchor: وقد رأيت في بعض نسخ شرح صحيح مسلم للإمام النووي

ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r5.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r5.claim: Shafi‘i scholars object that this would follow only if the verse said, “those who nursed you are your mothers”; al-Ālūsī says al-Nawawī only denies proof for one, not that the verse explicitly signals five.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r5.anchor: وأعترض اصحاب الشافعي على المالكية فقالوا : إنما كانت تحصل الدلالة لكم لو كانت الآية واللاتي أرضعنكم أمهاتكم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r6.claim: A manuscript's added conjunction between “nursed you” and “your mothers” is likely a copyist's error, and forcing an interpretation is strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r6.anchor: والظاهر أنها غلط من الناسخ وإلتزام توجيهها تعسف رأينا تركه ربحا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī presents his explanation tentatively, says learned contemporaries did not resolve the puzzle, and urges reflection and adherence to truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r7.anchor: ولست على يقين أنه الأولى والأحرى فتأمل فلمسلك الذهن إتساع والحق أحق بالإتباع

ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r8.claim: The verse now begins the affinity-based prohibitions after the nursing prohibitions, which are kinship-like in closeness.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p256/r8.anchor: شروع في بيان المحرمات من جهة المصاهرة إثر بيان المحرمات من جهة الرضاعة التي لها لحمة كلحمة النسب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r1.claim: “Your women” means wives whether consummated with or not, by agreement of the four imams; the marriage must be valid, while an invalid marriage makes the wife's mother forbidden only after intercourse with the daughter.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r1.anchor: والمراد بالنساء المنكوحات على الإطلاق سواء كن مدخولا بهن أولا وهو مجمع عليه عند الأئمة الأربعة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r2.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r2.claim: A report through ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb from his father and grandfather says a wife's mother is forbidden upon marriage even before consummation; marrying the daughter is allowed after an unconsummated marriage to her mother ends.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r2.anchor: أخرج البيهقي في سننه وغيره من طريق عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال : إذا نكح الرجل المرأة فلا يحل له أن يتزوج أمها دخل بالإبنة أو لم يدخل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r3.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r3.claim: One report from Ibn ʿAbbās, transmitted by Ibn al-Mundhir, says a wife's mother remains forbidden even if the husband divorces her before intercourse or she dies.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r3.anchor: فقد أخرج إبن المنذر عنه أنه قال : النساء مبهمة إذا طلق الرجل أمرأته قبل أن يدخل بها أو ماتت لم تحل له أمها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r4.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r4.claim: In another report, Ibn ʿAbbās told Muslim ibn ʿUwaymir, whose wife died before consummation, to marry her mother, contradicting the first report.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r4.anchor: وأخرج هوأيضا عن مسلم بن عويمر أنه قال : نكحت أمرأة فلم أدخل بها حتى توفي عمي عن أمها فسألت إبن عباس فقال : أنكح أمها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r5.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r5.claim: In Mālik's transmission, Zayd ibn Thābit says a wife's mother is unconditionally forbidden, while only stepdaughters have a consummation condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r5.anchor: لا الأم مبهمة ليس فيها شرط إنما الشرط في الربائب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r6.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r6.claim: Another report from Zayd says marrying the mother is disliked if the wife died and he inherited from her, but allowed if he divorced her before consummation.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r6.anchor: وأخرج إبن جرير وجماعة عنه أنه كان يقول : إذا ماتت عنده فأخذ ميراثها كره أن يخلف على أمها وإذا طلقها قبل أن يدخل بها فلا بأس أن يتزوج أمها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r7.speaker: إبن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd first permitted marrying the mother after an unconsummated marriage to her daughter, then retracted and ordered the man to separate from her.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257/r7.anchor: ثم رجع عن ذلك فقد أخرج مالك عنه أنه أستفتى بالكوفة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r1.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r1.claim: Ali held that a man's mother-in-law remains like a stepdaughter's mother: forbidden even if he divorced or lost his wife before intercourse.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r1.anchor: هي بمنزلة الربيبة وإلى ذلك ذهب إبن الزبير ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r2.speaker: إبن الزبير ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr and Mujahid are also reported to treat the mother-in-law like a stepdaughter's mother, forbidden without consummation.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r2.anchor: وإلى ذلك ذهب إبن الزبير ومجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r3.claim: The term mothers includes grandmothers on both the father's and mother's sides, however far upward.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r3.anchor: يدخل في لفظ الأمهات الجدات من قبل الأب والأم وإن علون

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r4.claim: If the wife is enslaved, her mother is forbidden only after intercourse or its preliminaries, since wives' women here means free women, as in divorce-oath rules.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r4.anchor: لأن لفظ النساء إذا أضيف إلى الأزواج كان المراد منه الحرائر كما في الظهار والإيلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r5.claim: A reading repeats the entry condition after mothers-in-law as well as placing it with stepdaughters.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r6.claim: Rabāʾib is the plural of rabība; rabīb is a passive-pattern noun, and the feminine suffix marks its shift into a lexicalized noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r6.anchor: الربائب جمع ربيبة ورب وربى بمعنى والربيب فعيل بمعنى مفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r7.claim: A stepchild is the woman's child by another man, called rabīb because the husband usually raises the child as he raises his own.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r7.anchor: والربيب ولد المرأة من آخر سمى به لأنه يربه غالبا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r8.claim: Hujūr is plural of ḥijr/ḥajr, literally the lap from below the armpit to the waist; being in someone's lap means their care and protection.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r8.anchor: والحجور جمع حجر بالفتح والكسر وهو في اللغة حضن الإنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r9.claim: The lap description reflects the usual custom of a daughter staying with her mother and strengthens the rationale for prohibition; naming stepdaughters highlights that rationale.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r9.anchor: ووصف الربائب بكونهن في الحجور مخرج مخرج الغالب والعادة إذ الغالب كون البنت مع الأم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r10.claim: Another explanation treats the lap phrase as condemnation or emphasis, like the description of multiplied usury, not as a limiting condition.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r11.claim: If the lap phrase were restrictive, its absence would permit marriage by the contrary implication; without that implication, original permissibility still returns when the stated restriction is absent.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r11.anchor: لثبتت الإباحة عند إنتفائه بدلالة اللفظ في غير محل النطق

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r12.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r12.claim: Ali reportedly allowed marrying a stepdaughter who had not been raised in the man's home; Malik ibn Aws said his late wife's daughter lived in Taif, not with him, and Ali told him to marry her.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r12.anchor: فلقيني علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله تعالى وجهه فقال : مالك

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r13.speaker: داود
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r13.claim: David al-Ẓāhirī followed the view that a stepdaughter outside the man's home is not prohibited; the majority hold the contrary, and Ibn Masʿud later returned to the majority position.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r13.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب داؤد والأول مذهب الجمهور وإليه رجع إبن مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r14.claim: The prohibition extends to descendants of a stepdaughter or stepson, while the narrower terms for fathers and sons do not extend in the same way; hence certain cross-generational in-law marriages remain permitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p257#2/r14.anchor: ويدخل في الحرمة بنات الربيبة والربيب وإن سفلن لأن الأسم يشملهن بخلاف الأبناء والآباء

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r1.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r1.claim: Some investigators say the prohibition of the listed women is established by consensus.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r2.claim: The phrase about wives entered upon is a circumstantial phrase attached to stepdaughters or their implicit pronoun, meaning those settled in the man's care from wives he has entered upon; the relative clause restricts the wives, so an unconsummated wife's daughter is not forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r2.anchor: الجار والمجرور متعلق بمحذوف وقع حالا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r3.claim: Making the phrase circumstantial to mothers-in-law would require a different explanatory sense of min than its connection to stepdaughters, and an attempted combined sense is strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r3.anchor: ضرورة أن الحالية من ربائبكم أو من ضميره يقتضي كون

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r4.claim: The construction that combines an originative and explanatory sense of min is too remote and should not be attributed to the Qur'anic wording.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r4.anchor: بل ينبغي أن ينزه ساحة التنزيل عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r5.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r5.claim: The alternate reading is weak in transmission and, even if sound, should be understood as abrogated.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r5.anchor: وأما القراءة فضعيفة الرواية وعلى تقدير الصحة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r6.claim: The bāʾ in bihinna marks causation with an accompanying sense, or means with them; entering upon them is a euphemism for intercourse.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r6.anchor: والباء من بهن للتعدية وفيها معنى المصاحبة أو بمعنى مع أي دخلتم معهن الستر وهو كناية عن الجماع

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r7.speaker: الحريري
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r7.claim: Al-Ḥarīrī calls the expression banā bihā, used for consummating a marriage, a mistake; al-Ālūsī says that correction itself is mistaken.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r8.speaker: الإمام الأعظم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r8.claim: Abu Hanifa counts touching and its equivalents as intercourse for these rules.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r8.anchor: واللمس ونظائره في حكم الجماع عند الإمام الأعظم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r9.speaker: بعض الفضلاء
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r9.claim: An objection says the ruling has no basis in the verse's actual conditional wording, and a non-famous report would not fit the school's principles.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r9.anchor: بأن ماذهب إليه لا مجال له لأن صريح الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r10.claim: The response says the bāʾ explicitly indicates attachment: dakhala bihā can mean that he took her in and brought her into the house, so the text itself supports the ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r10.anchor: ويدفع بأنه من صريح النص لأن باء الإلصاق صريحة فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r11.claim: A figurative phrase need not require the literal sense, but that sense may be intended when contextual evidence supports it; reports suffice as such evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r11.anchor: أجيب بأنه لم يلزم إرادته لكن لا مانع منه عند قيام قرينة على إرادته

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r12.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r12.claim: A report says the Prophet forbade a man who had only fondled his wife from marrying her daughter; al-Ālūsī calls it mursal and disconnected, but acceptable to the school when its transmitters are trustworthy.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r12.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قال في الذي يتزوج المرأة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r13.speaker: إبن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r13.claim: Ibn Umar says intercourse, lustful kissing or touching, or lustful looking at a woman's private parts makes her forbidden to the man's father and son, and her mother and daughter forbidden to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p258/r13.anchor: إذا جامع الرجل المرأة أو قبلها أو لمسها بشهوة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r1.claim: Touching and similar acts fall under the textual indication of intercourse; the objection from the condition's contrary implication assumes a principle the author rejects, and any general implication could be specified.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r1.anchor: أجيب بأنه داخل بدلالة النص وماذكر من مخالفة صريح الشرط مبني على إعتبار مفهوم الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r2.claim: Vaginal fornication creates affinity prohibitions according to the author, contrary to al-Shafiʿi, who says unlawful sex cannot create the prohibition that is a blessing; the author analogizes all intercourse to lawful intercourse because its capacity to cause offspring is the operative cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r2.anchor: والزنا في الفرج محرم عندنا فمن زنى بأمرأة حرمت عليه بنتها خلافا للشافعي

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r3.claim: The author argues that lawful status is irrelevant: intercourse with a shared slave, a son's slave, a menstruating or otherwise prohibited partner, and other forbidden cases still creates the affinity prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259/r3.anchor: وصف الحل لا دخل له في المناط فإن وطء الأمة المشتركة وجارية الإبن والمكاتبة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r1.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r1.claim: A man who had committed fornication before Islam asked whether he could marry the woman's daughter; the Prophet answered that he did not think so and said it was improper for her to know what her mother had revealed to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r1.anchor: لا أرى ذلك ولا يصلح أن تنكح امرأة تطلع من إبنتها

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes that this counter-report is disconnected, cited against the opposing report, and criticized by hadith scholars; ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq's Ibn Umar route contains the abandoned transmitter Isḥāq ibn Abī Farwa.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r2.anchor: وهذا وإن كان فيه إرسال وإنقطاع لكن جئنا به في مقابلة خبرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r3.speaker: صاحب الهداية
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r3.claim: The author of al-Hidāya answers that intercourse creates the prohibition as a cause of offspring, not because of intercourse itself or its being fornication.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r3.anchor: وأجاب صاحب الهداية عن قولهم في تعليل كون الزنا لا يوجب حرمة المصاهرة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r4.speaker: فتح القدير
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r4.claim: Fatḥ al-Qadīr calls the blessing argument fallacious: affinity, which makes strangers into kin and helpers, is the benefit, but fornication creates no such affinity and its reports are balanced, leaving analogy to decide.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r4.anchor: وفي فتح القدير أن هذا القول مغلطة فإن النعمة ليست التحريم من حيث هو تحريم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r5.claim: The author's analogy makes intercourse itself, without an added qualification of lawful status, the operative cause of affinity prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r5.anchor: فالمرجع القياس وقد بينا فيه إلغاء وصف زائد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r6.claim: If the man did not have intercourse with his wife's mother, he may marry her daughter after divorce or death; this explicitly clarifies the earlier implication and dispels the idea that living in his home is the relevant condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r6.anchor: أصلا في نكاح بناتهن إذا طلقتموهن أو متن

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r7.claim: The first faʾ links the consequence to what precedes, and stating only non-entry as the basis for no prohibition shows that intercourse, rather than whether the stepdaughter lived with him, is decisive.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#2/r7.anchor: وفي الإقتصار في بيان نفي الحرمة على نفي الدخول إشارة إلى أن المعتبر في الحرمة إنما هو الدخول

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r1.claim: If residence in the man's home mattered, the verse would have mentioned its absence as well; Arabic usage can attach negation of a ruling to the absence of the full or one part of its composite cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r1.anchor: فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن ولسن في حجوركم أو فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن أو لسن في حجوركم

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r2.claim: Ḥalāʾil means wives, named because spouses share a bed or go wherever the other goes; ḥalīl may derive from intimacy or from each being lawful to the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r2.anchor: أي زوجاتهم جمع حليلة سميت الزوجة بذلك لأنها تحل

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r3.claim: The verse directly forbids a son's wife; prohibiting other women the son has had intercourse with rests on separate evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r3.anchor: والآية ظاهرة في تحريم الزوجة فقط وأما حرمة من وطئها الإبن ممن ليس بزوجة فبدليل آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r4.speaker: إبن الهمام
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r4.claim: Ibn al-Humam says that if ḥalīla means bedmate or one whose clothing is shared, the term covers women possessed, approached by mistake, or approached through fornication, but not a merely contracted wife; other evidence establishes the son's fornicate as forbidden to the father.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r4.anchor: إن أعتبروا الحليلة من حلول الفراش أو حل الإزار تناول الموطوأة بملك اليمين أو شبهة أو زنا

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r5.claim: The term sons includes descendants, so the rule forbids a descendant's wife to an ancestor, including a daughter's son.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r5.anchor: فيجب إعتباره في أعم من الحل والحل ثم يراد بالأبناء الفروع

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r6.speaker: اللغويين
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r6.claim: Lexicographers apparently use ḥalīla for a wife; some instead choose the wider sense, including a slave woman, to include both wife and possession.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r6.anchor: والظاهر من كلام اللغويين أن الحليلة الزوجة كما أشرنا إليه وأختار بعضهم إرادة المعنى الأعم الشامل لملك اليمين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r7.claim: Some explain the broad term as warning that a man might assume his son's slave belongs to him because a child's property belongs to the father, and so might wrongly have intercourse with her.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r7.anchor: ليكون السر في التعبير بها هنا دون الأزواج أو النساء أن الرجل ربما يظن أن مملوكة إبنه مملوكة إبنه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r8.claim: Intercourse, not the mere categories of touching, follows the same rule as intercourse by sons.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r8.anchor: وحكم الممسوسات ونحوهن حكم اللائي وطئهن الأبناء

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r9.claim: The phrase from your loins qualifies sons and excludes an adopted son's wife; the verse was revealed after the Prophet married Zayd ibn Haritha's former wife, while the phrase does not exclude a nursing-son's wife, also forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r9.anchor: وذكر لإسقاط حليلة المتبني وعن عطاء أنها نزلت حين تزوج صلى الله عليه وسلم أمرأة زيد بن حارثة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p259#3/r10.claim: The phrase those from your loins is an adjective qualifying sons.

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r1.claim: The prohibition on combining sisters is coordinated with the preceding prohibited categories and concerns marriage, not merely ownership.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r1.anchor: في حيز الرفع عطف على ما قبله من المحرمات

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r2.claim: The rule covers sisters by blood or nursing; if a stranger woman breastfeeds two wives, their marriages are both dissolved.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r2.anchor: ولا فرق بين كونهما أختين من النسب أو الرضاعة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r3.speaker: الشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r3.claim: Al-Shafiʿi is reported to hold that, in that nursing-sister case, only the later marriage is dissolved.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r3.anchor: وحكى عن الشافعي أنه يفسد نكاح الثانية فقط

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r4.claim: Owning two sisters is not itself prohibited, but having intercourse with both is prohibited by textual implication because the same operative cause applies; this is the majority view, also held by Ibn Masʿud, Ibn Umar, and Ammar.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260/r4.anchor: نعم جمعهما في الوطء بملك اليمين ملحق به بطريق الدلالة لإتحادهما في المدار

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r1.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r1.claim: Ali reportedly said a man with two owned sisters who had intercourse with one must relinquish ownership before intercourse with the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r1.anchor: فأخرج البيهقي وإبن أبي شيبة عنه أنه سئل عن رجل له أمتان أختان وطيء إحداهما

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r2.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r2.claim: Another report has Ali say one verse permits and another forbids the two owned sisters, so he neither commands, forbids, permits, nor prohibits the practice, and he and his household do not do it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r2.anchor: أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية ولا آمر ولا أنهى

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r3.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to regard combining two owned sisters as permissible; the same view is attributed to Uthman.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r3.anchor: أن الجمع مما لا بأس به

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r4.speaker: عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r4.claim: Umar said he did not like to allow the combination and forbade the questioner from doing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r4.anchor: ما أحب أن أجيز الجمع ونهى السائل عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r5.claim: Some say the Companions who initially allowed combining later adopted the majority view; if not, a later consensus overrides the earlier disagreement, and otherwise prohibition is preferred when reports conflict.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r5.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الظاهر أن القائل بالحل من الصحابة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r6.claim: A man may marry the sister of his owned slave with whom he had intercourse, but cannot have intercourse with either woman until he makes the slave forbidden to himself through sale, marriage, transfer, emancipation, or a similar cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r6.anchor: وإذا تزوج أخت أمته الموطوأة صح النكاح وحرم وطء واحدة منهما حتى يحرم الموطوأة على نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r7.claim: A void marriage to the slave's sister does not bar intercourse with the slave until consummation; then the real combination arises. Ihram, menstruation, postpartum bleeding, fasting, pledge, lease, and deferred manumission do not forbid intercourse with the slave.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r7.anchor: ولو تزوج الأخت نكاحا فاسدا لم تحرم عليه أمته الموطوأة إلا إذا دخل بالمنكوحة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r8.claim: If ownership of the slave returns by rescission or a new purchase, intercourse with either remains barred until the slave is again made forbidden to him; the school's wording implies the marriage is valid because it is contracted by a competent person upon a valid subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r8.anchor: وإذا عادت الموطوأة إلى ملكه بعد الإخراج سواء كان بفسخ أو شراء جديد

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r9.claim: The objection that the wife is treated as sexually enjoyed by the marriage, causing a notional combination, is answered by the man's ability to end that status; actual intercourse is barred afterward, without invalidating the marriage.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r9.anchor: وأورد عليه أن المنكوحة موطوأة حكما بإعترافهم فيصير بالنكاح جامعا وطءا حكما

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r10.claim: The verse attaches prohibition to the act of combining, rather than permanently prohibiting the second sister, and the same principle covers combining a woman with her aunt or niece.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r10.anchor: وإسناد الحرمة إلى الجمع لا إلى الثانية

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r11.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r11.claim: A report from al-Tabarani says the Prophet warned that combining relatives cuts kinship ties; a mursal report from Abu Dawud similarly gives fear of rupture as the reason for forbidding marriage over a relative.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r11.anchor: فإنكم إن فعلتم ذلك قطعتم أرحامكم وما رواه أبو داؤد في مراسيله عن عيسى بن طلحة

ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r12.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r12.claim: Some investigators treat the Prophet's express ban on marrying a woman alongside her aunt or niece as an interpretive explanation of the kinship rationale.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p260#2/r12.anchor: من قبيل بيان التفسير لا بيان التعبير عند بعض المحققين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r1.speaker: آخرون
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r1.claim: Other scholars say the aunt-and-niece hadith is well known, authenticated or transmitted by major hadith collections, and accepted by early generations and many Companions; it can specify the general permission even if solitary.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r1.anchor: إن الحديث مشهور فقد ثبت في صحيحي مسلم وإبن حبان

ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r2.speaker: إبن الهمام
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r2.claim: Ibn al-Humam says fame must apparently be established because the hadith functions as abrogation, not specification.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r2.anchor: الظاهر أنه لا بد من أدعاء الشهرة لأن الحديث موقعه النسخ

ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r3.claim: The phrase except what has passed is a disconnected exception; treating it as emphatic confirmation is inappropriate because the following description of God as forgiving and merciful does not fit emphatic prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r3.anchor: إستثناء منقطع وقصد المبالغة والتأكيد هنا غير مناسب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r4.claim: What has passed means conduct before the ban, when people used to combine sisters.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r4.anchor: والمراد مما سلف ما مضى قبل النهي فإنهم كانوا يجمعون به الأختين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r5.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r5.claim: Fayruz al-Daylami's report says he embraced Islam while married to two sisters, and the Prophet told him to divorce whichever one he chose; al-Tirmidhi graded the report hasan.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r5.anchor: عن فيرز الديلمي أنه أدركه الإسلام وتحته أختان

ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r6.speaker: عطاء والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r6.claim: Aṭāʾ and al-Suddī say the exception refers to Jacob's marriage to the sisters Leah, mother of Judah, and Rachel, mother of Joseph; the author says this would have been lawful in Jacob's own law.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r6.anchor: معناه إلا ما كان من يعقوب عليه السلام إذ جمع بين الأختين

ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r7.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says pre-Islamic Arabs prohibited God's prohibited categories except marrying one's father's wife and combining sisters; Muhammad ibn al-Hasan is reported similarly.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r7.anchor: وعن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما كان أهل الجاهلية يحرمون ما حرم الله تعالى إلا أمرأة الأب

ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r8.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r8.claim: Shaykh al-Islam takes the repeated exception after the two bans as evidence that both exceptions have the same intended sense; al-Ālūsī objects that their differing continuations contradict this.
ALUSI-FULL:v4p261/r8.anchor: يشير إلى كون الإستثناء فيهما على سنن واحد ويأباه إختلاف ما بعدهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r1.claim: The verse identifies forbidden women through kinship ties; the total forbidden categories in the Qurʾān are fourteen, seven by lineage and seven by other causes.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r1.anchor: ، بين الله تعالى في هذه الآية المحرمات بسبب الوصلة، وجملة المحرمات في كتاب الله تعالى أربع عشرة:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r2.claim: Among the seven forbidden by cause are two through nursing, four through affinity, and the seventh is married women.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r2.anchor: فمنها اثنتان بالرضاع وأربع بالصهرية والسابعة المحصنات، وهن ذوات الأزواج.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r3.claim: Mothers includes grandmothers of every ascending generation on both the maternal and paternal sides.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r3.anchor: فيدخل فيهن الجدات وإن علون من قبل الأم ومن قبل الأب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r4.claim: Daughters includes granddaughters of every descending generation.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r5.claim: Sisters are forbidden whether they share both parents or only one.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r5.anchor: سواء كانت من قبل الأب والأم أو من قبل أحدهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r6.claim: Paternal aunts includes all sisters of one's fathers and grandfathers, however far ascending.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r6.anchor: ويدخل فيهن جميع أخوات آبائك وأجدادك وإن علون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r7.claim: Maternal aunts includes all sisters of one's mothers and grandmothers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r7.anchor: ويدخل فيهن جميع أخوات أمهاتك وجداتك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r8.claim: Nieces includes the daughters of siblings' children, however far descending.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r8.anchor: ويدخل فيهن بنات أولاد الأخ والأخت وإن سفلن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r9.claim: The categories can be generalized as ascendants, descendants, descendants of the first ascendants, and the first branch of each later ascendant.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r9.anchor: وجملته: أنه يحرم على الرجل أصوله وفصوله وفصول أول أصوله وأول فصل من كل أصل بعده،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r10.claim: The two nursing categories named are foster mothers and foster sisters; the general rule is that nursing forbids what lineage forbids.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r10.anchor: وجملته: أنه يحرم من الرضاعة ما يحرم من النسب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r11.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet's rule that nursing makes unlawful the same relationships as birth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p188/r11.anchor: عن عائشة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r1.speaker: عائشة أم المؤمنين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r1.claim: Aisha reports that ten known nursing feeds were first revealed as prohibiting marriage, then abrogated by five; at the Prophet's death those words were still recited.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r1.anchor: عن عمرة بنت عبد الرحمن، عن عائشة أم المؤمنين رضي الله عنها أنها قالت: كان فيما أنزل الله في القرآن عشر رضعات معلومات يحرمن،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r2.claim: A wife's mother and ascending grandmothers, whether related by nursing or lineage, become forbidden to the husband as soon as he contracts the marriage.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r2.anchor: كل من عقد النكاح على امرأة تحرم على الناكح أمهات المنكوحة وجداتها وإن علون من الرضاعة والنسب بنفس العقد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r3.claim: Rabāʾib are a wife's daughters; the term denotes a girl raised by the husband.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r3.anchor: والربائب جمع: ربيبة: وهي بنت المرأة، سميت ربيبة لتربيته إياها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r4.claim: In your rooms means in your care and upbringing, and entering upon a wife means having intercourse with her.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r4.anchor: ، وقوله: {في حجوركم} أي: في تربيتكم، يقال: فلان في حجر فلان إذا كان في تربيته، {دخلتم بهن} أي: جامعتموهن.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r5.claim: A wife's daughters and their descendants, by nursing or lineage, become forbidden after intercourse with her.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r5.anchor: ويحرم عليه أيضا بنات المنكوحة وبنات أولادها، وإن سفلن من الرضاع والنسب بعد الدخول بالمنكوحة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r6.claim: If a husband separates from a wife before intercourse or she dies, he may marry her daughter, but her mother remains forbidden because mothers are prohibited without a consummation condition.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190/r6.anchor: لأن الله تعالى أطلق تحريم الأمهات وقال في تحريم الربائب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r1.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r1.claim: Ali holds that a wife's mother becomes forbidden only after intercourse with her daughter, just like a stepdaughter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r1.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه: أم المرأة لا تحرم إلا بالدخول بالبنت كالربيبة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r2.claim: A son's wife is called ḥalīla, and the husband ḥalīl.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r2.anchor: {وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم} يعني: أزواج أبنائكم، واحدتها: حليلة، والذكر حليل،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r3.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r3.claim: One proposed etymology for ḥalīla and ḥalīl is that each spouse is lawful to the other.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r3.anchor: حلال لصاحبه، وقيل: سميا بذلك لأن كل واحد منهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r4.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r4.claim: Another proposed etymology connects the terms with settling: each spouse settles where the other settles.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r4.anchor: يحل حيث يحل صاحبه من الحلول وهو النزول، وقيل: إن كل واحد منهما يحل إزار صاحبه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r5.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r5.claim: A further proposed etymology says each spouse loosens the other's waist-wrapper, from ḥall as the opposite of binding.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: إن كل واحد منهما يحل إزار صاحبه من الحل وهو ضد العقل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r6.claim: A man's sons' and grandsons' wives, by nursing or lineage, are forbidden as soon as the marriage contract is made.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r6.anchor: أنه يحرم على الرجل حلائل أبنائه وأبناء أولاده وإن سفلوا من الرضاع والنسب بنفس العقد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r7.claim: The phrase from your loins clarifies that a son's wife is not forbidden merely because the son was adopted; the Prophet married Zayd's former wife after Zayd had been adopted by him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r7.anchor: وإنما قال "من أصلابكم" ليعلم أن حليلة المتبنى لا تحرم على الرجل الذي تبناه، فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تزوج امرأة زيد بن حارثة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r8.claim: A father's or grandfather's wife is forbidden to a son and his descendants by contract, whether the father is a milk relative or a lineage relative.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r8.anchor: فيحرم على الولد وولد الولد بنفس العقد سواء كان الأب من الرضاع أو من النسب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r9.claim: Any woman forbidden through marriage is also forbidden through intercourse in ownership or intercourse under a mistaken marriage; this also makes her mother and daughter forbidden and bars her from the man's father and son.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r9.anchor: وكل امرأة تحرم عليك بعقد النكاح تحرم بالوطء في ملك اليمين، والوطء بشبهة النكاح،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r10.speaker: علي وابن مسعود وابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r10.claim: They, along with Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, ʿUrwa, al-Zuhrī, Mālik, and al-Shāfiʿī, hold that zina does not forbid a man the adulterated woman's mother or daughter, though it forbids her to his father or son.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r10.anchor: قول علي وابن مسعود وابن عباس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r11.speaker: عمران بن حصين وأبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r11.claim: They report the opposing rule that zina creates affinity prohibitions; Jābir ibn Zayd, al-Ḥasan, and the legal rationalists also hold it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r11.anchor: يروى ذلك عن عمران بن حصين وأبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما، وبه قال جابر بن زيد والحسن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r12.claim: On whether lustful touching or kissing creates affinity prohibitions, including a stepdaughter prohibition, the sounder view held by most scholars says it does; the second view denies this, as with lustful looking.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p190#2/r12.anchor: فيه قولان، أصحهما وهو قول أكثر أهل العلم: أنه تثبت به الحرمة، والثاني: لا تثبت كما لا تثبت بالنظر بالشهوة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r1.claim: A man may not marry two sisters together, whether their sisterhood is by lineage or nursing; after an irrevocable divorce, he may marry the former wife's sister.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r1.anchor: لا يجوز للرجل أن يجمع بين الأختين في النكاح سواء كانت الأخوة بينهما بالنسب أو بالرضاع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r2.claim: A man may not have intercourse with two owned sisters; after intercourse with one, he cannot approach the other until he makes the first forbidden to himself.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r2.anchor: لم يجز له أن يجمع بينهما في الوطء، فإذا وطئ إحداهما لم يحل له وطء الأخرى حتى يحرم الأولى على نفسه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r3.claim: One may not combine a wife with her paternal or maternal aunt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r3.anchor: وكذلك لا يجوز أن يجمع بين المرأة وعمتها ولا بين المرأة وخالتها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet's prohibition on combining a woman with her paternal or maternal aunt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p191/r4.anchor: عن مالك، عن أبي الزناد، عن الأعرج، عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنهم أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا يجمع بين المرأة وعمتها، ولا بين المرأة وخالتها"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p192/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p192/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p192/r1.claim: The exception for what preceded means earlier conduct is forgiven because people practiced it before Islam.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p192/r1.anchor: يعني: لكن ما مضى فهو معفو عنه، لأنهم كانوا يفعلونه قبل الإسلام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p192/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p192/r2.speaker: عطاء والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p192/r2.claim: They say the exception refers to Jacob, who married Leah, Judah's mother, and Rachel, Joseph's mother, while the sisters were both alive.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p192/r2.anchor: وقال عطاء والسدي: إلا ما كان من يعقوب عليه السلام فإنه جمع بين ليا أم يهوذا وراحيل أم يوسف،

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r1.claim: The verse prohibits marrying the listed women, not the women themselves; marriage is the main intended relation and the context confirms it, as “prohibited to you is carrion” means eating it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r1.anchor: ليس المراد تحريم ذواتهن بل تحريم نكاحهن

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r2.claim: Mothers include the woman who bore a person and all maternal and paternal grandmothers; daughters include daughters and all granddaughters.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r2.anchor: وأمهاتكم تعم من ولدتك أو ولدت من ولدك وإن علت

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r3.claim: Sisters include the three lines of sisterhood; likewise the other categories extend through ascending and descending generations.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r3.anchor: وأخواتكم الأخوات من الأوجه الثلاثة. وكذلك الباقيات

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r4.claim: The paternal aunt is any woman descended through a male child of one’s male ancestor; the maternal aunt is through a female child of one’s female ancestor, near or distant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r4.anchor: والعمة كل أنثى ولدها من ولد ذكرا ولدك

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r5.claim: Nieces through brothers and sisters include both close and remote descendants.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r5.anchor: وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت تتناول القربى والبعدى

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r6.claim: God gives milk kinship the status of lineage, naming a wet nurse a mother and a fellow nursling a sibling; the rule follows the wet nurse and the child’s milk-producing father.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r6.anchor: نزل الله الرضاعة منزلة النسب حتى سمى المرضعة أما والمرضعة أختا

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r7.speaker: النبي
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r7.claim: The Prophet says that breastfeeding prohibits the same relations as lineage.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r7.anchor: يحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم من النسب

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r8.claim: The author rejects including a man’s milk-sister or milk-brother’s mother under this rule; their prohibition in blood relations arises from affinity, not milk kinship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r8.anchor: واستثناء أخت ابن الرجل وأم أخيه من الرضاع من هذا الأصل ليس بصحيح

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r9.claim: The sequence lists lineage prohibitions, then breastfeeding because it is like lineage, then affinity because its prohibition arises incidentally from marriage.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r9.anchor: ذكر أولا محرمات النسب ثم محرمات الرضاعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r10.claim: Rabāʾib is the plural of rabība, a wife’s child by another man, named for usually being raised as one’s own; it is a passive form that became a noun.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r10.anchor: والربائب جمع ربيبة. والربيب ولد المرأة من آخر

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r11.claim: The phrase “of your women” attaches to stepdaughters, and the following relative clause restricts the wording and ruling by consensus.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r11.anchor: ومن نسائكم متعلق بربائبكم، واللاتي بصلتها صفة لها

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r12.claim: Attaching the clause to mothers would force min to mean explanation rather than origin, and one word cannot bear two meanings according to most grammarians.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23/r12.anchor: والكلمة الواحدة لا تحمل على معنيين عند جمهور الأدباء

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r1.speaker: علي
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r1.claim: Ali is reported to treat “in your care” as a condition for the stepdaughter prohibition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r1.anchor: وقد روي عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه جعله شرطا

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r2.claim: The majority view is that the condition is not restricted to stepdaughters actually in one’s custody.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r3.claim: The phrase “you entered upon them” means being alone with the women under the curtain, a euphemism for intercourse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r3.anchor: دخلتم بهن أي دخلتم معهن الستر وهي كناية عن الجماع

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r4.claim: Affinity prohibitions can also result from intercourse outside a valid marriage, including intercourse by mistake or with a slave woman.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r4.anchor: ويؤثر في حرمة المصاهرة ما ليس بزنا كالوطء بشبهة

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa treats touching one’s wife and similar contact as consummation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r5.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة لمس المنكوحة ونحوه كالدخول

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r6.claim: Explicitly stating the rule for a marriage without intercourse blocks an inference by analogy.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r7.claim: A son’s ḥalīla is his wife; the term derives either from being lawful to him or from living with him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r7.anchor: سميت الزوجة حليلة لحلها أو لحلولها مع الزوج

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r8.claim: “From your loins” excludes adopted sons, but not sons’ sons.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r8.anchor: احتراز عن المتبنين لا عن أبناء الولد

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r9.claim: The ban on combining two sisters is coordinated grammatically with the forbidden relations and appears to cover ownership as well as marriage; Uthman and Ali cite this ban against the permission in the next verse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r9.anchor: في موضع الرفع عطفا على المحرمات، والظاهر أن الحرمة غير مقصورة على النكاح

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r10.claim: A poetic line is cited as an exception where the relation can be understood as connectedness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r10.anchor: على معنى أن أمهات النساء وبناتهن متصلات بهن،

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r11.claim: The Prophet distinguished the rules: after divorce before consummation, a man may marry his former wife’s daughter but not her mother; the generality of scholars follows this.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r11.anchor: " إنه لا بأس أن يتزوج ابنتها ولا يحل له أن يتزوج أمها "

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r12.speaker: علي
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r12.claim: A report from Ali restricts the prohibition in both cases.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r12.anchor: غير أنه روي عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنه تقييد التحريم فيهما.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r13.claim: The second relative clause cannot modify both occurrences of “women,” because their governing words differ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r13.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون الموصول الثاني صفة للنساءين لأن عاملهما مختلف،

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r14.claim: The custody phrase strengthens the rationale: stepdaughters resemble one’s own children when their mothers are consummated and the girls are in or near one’s care.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r14.anchor: وفائدة قوله { في حجوركم } تقوية العلة وتكميلها،

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23#2/r15.claim: Mothers and stepdaughters include both near and distant generations.

BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23-24/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23-24/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23-24/r4.claim: The exception may attach to an implied consequence, or be disconnected and mean that past cases are forgiven by God's mercy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:4:23-24/r4.anchor: استثناء من لازم المعنى، أو منقطع

BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r8.claim: The ban on mothers is stated again through their persons to intensify it and honor the father; it covers sexual enjoyment through marriage or ownership.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r8.anchor: أسند التحريم إلى الذات تأكيدا للتحريم فقال : { أمهاتكم } أي التمتع بهن بنكاح أو ملك يمين ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r9.claim: Daughters include descendants at every level; this prohibition and the mother's prohibition are forbidden in every religion, and the daughter's ban also protects her mother.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r9.anchor: { وبناتكم } أي وإن سفلن لما في ذلك من ضرار أمهاتهن , وهذان الصنفان لم يحللن في دين من الأديان { وأخواتكم }

BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r10.claim: Sisters may be full or half-sisters; aunts are defined through the siblings of male or female ancestors, including cross-line cases.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r10.anchor: { وأخواتكم } أي أشقاء أو لا { وعماتكم } كذلك { وخالاتكم } أيضا , والضابط لهما أن كل ذكر يرجع نسبك إليه فأخته عمتك ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r11.claim: Nieces through brothers or sisters are forbidden whether full or half-siblings, including their descendants.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p231/r11.anchor: { وبنات الأخ } شقيقا كان أو لا { وبنات الأخت } أي كذلك , وفروعهن وإن سفلن .

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r1.claim: The lineage prohibitions comprise seven categories; the affinity prohibitions comprise eight, with fathers' wives singled out first for honor and married women last.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r1.anchor: ولما انقضى أمر النسب وهو سبعة أصناف أتبعه أمر السبب وهو ثمانية : أوله أزواج الآباء , أفردها وقدمها تعظيما لحرمتها ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r2.claim: Milk kinship makes the nursing woman a mother, including the woman who nursed you or your nurse, and creates corresponding maternal, paternal, and sibling relations through the milk-giving husband.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r2.anchor: فكل أنثى انتسب باللبن إليها فهي أمك , وهي من أرضعتك , أو أرضعت امرأة أرضعتك ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r3.claim: The prohibition of foster siblings applies after five nursing sessions within the first two years.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r3.anchor: كما في النسب بشرط أن يكون خمس رضعات وفي الحولين

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r4.claim: The Prophet says that milk kinship prohibits the same relationships prohibited by blood kinship.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r4.anchor: كما بينه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله ( يحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم من النسب )

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r5.claim: The mother and sister examples signal the remaining milk prohibitions by the shared causes of birth and siblinghood.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r5.anchor: فالصورتان منبهتان على بقية السبع ؛ الأم منبهة على البنت بجامع الولادة , والأخوات على العمات والخالات

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r6.claim: A wife's mother is prohibited whether or not the marriage was consummated, because the relationship commonly disrupts family harmony.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r6.anchor: { وأمهات نسائكم } أي دخلتم بهن أو لا - لما في ذلك من إفساد ذات البين غالبا { وربائبكم }

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r7.claim: A stepdaughter is prohibited when she is actually or potentially in one's care and comes from a wife with whom one has had intercourse; intercourse establishes the relevant affinity.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r7.anchor: { وربائبكم } وذكر سبب الحرمة فقال : { اللاتي في حجوركم } أي بالفعل أو بالقوة - لما فيهن من شبه الأولاد { من نسائكم }

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r8.claim: Without consummation, marrying the stepdaughter is lawful; the entry condition applies to the daughter's prohibition, unlike the wife's mother's prohibition.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r8.anchor: { فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن } أي الأمهات { فلا جناح عليكم } أي في نكاحهن ؛

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r9.claim: A son's wife or concubine is forbidden when the son is biological, including descendants; adopted sons are excluded, while foster sons count through milk kinship.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r9.anchor: { وحلائل أبنائكم } أي زوجة كانت أو موطوءة بملك يمين ؛ ولما لم يكن المتبنى مرادا قيد بقوله : { الذين من أصلابكم } أي وإن سفلوا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r10.claim: It is temporarily forbidden to combine two sisters in marriage or sexual ownership; when one is a wife and the other enslaved, the marriage is stronger, so the wife remains lawful and the enslaved sister forbidden.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r10.anchor: { وأن } أي وحرم عليكم أن { تجمعوا } بعقد نكاح لأن مقصوده الوطء , أو بوطء في ملك يمين { بين الأختين }

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r11.claim: When the marriage or sexual bond that prevented combination ends, the other sister becomes lawful even during the former wife's waiting period.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r11.anchor: فإذا زال الحل حلت الأخرة ولو في عدة التي كانت حلالا .

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r12.claim: The exception for past combination reflects that it was permitted by earlier law; God lifts guilt out of mercy.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r12.anchor: ولما كان الجمع بين الأختين شرعا قديما قال : { إلا ما قد سلف } أي فإنه لا إثم عليكم فيه رحمة من الله لكم ,

BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r13.claim: God is forgiving by covering chosen errors and their effects, and merciful through the highest honor befitting divinity.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p232/r13.anchor: ثم علل رفع حرجه فقال : { إن الله } أي المحيط بصفات الكمال { كان غفورا } أي ساترا لما يريد من أعيان الزلل وآثاره { رحيما * }

DURR-FULL:v2p469/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p469/r1.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
DURR-FULL:v2p469/r1.claim: Muqatil says a deceased man’s relative could claim his widow in pre-Islamic custom; after Abu Qays died, his son married the widow, and the prohibition was revealed, excusing what preceded it.
DURR-FULL:v2p469/r1.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قال: كان إذا توفي الرجل في الجاهلية عمد حميم الميت إلى امرأته فألقى عليها ثوبا فيرث نكاحها

DURR-FULL:v2p469#2/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p469#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p469#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas divides the prohibitions into seven by blood and seven by marriage, identifying the first listed women through one’s sister’s daughter as consanguineal and the remainder as affinity.
DURR-FULL:v2p469#2/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: حرم من النسب سبع ومن الصهر سبع ثم قرأ {حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم} إلى قوله {وبنات الأخت}

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says there are seven prohibitions by affinity and seven by blood, and breastfeeding prohibits the same relationships as blood.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سبع صهر وسبع نسب ويحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم من النسب

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r2.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet’s rule that breastfeeding prohibits the same relationships that birth prohibits.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r2.anchor: عن عائشة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: الرضاعة تحرم ما تحرم الولادة

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r3.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r3.claim: Aisha says ten known nursing sessions were abrogated to five, which she said remained recited when the Prophet died.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r3.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كان فيما أنزل من القرآن عشر رضعات معلومات فنسخن بخمس معلومات فتوفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهن فيما يقرأ من القرآن

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r4.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r4.claim: Aisha says the number was reduced from ten nursing sessions to five, while part of the Qurʾanic material was taken up at the Prophet’s death.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r4.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: لقد كانت في كتاب الله عشر رضعات ثم رد ذلك إلى خمس ولكن من كتاب الله ما قبض مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r5.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r5.claim: Aisha reports a recitation that only ten or five known nursing sessions prohibit marriage.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r5.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: كان مما نزل من القرآن سقط لا يحرم إلا عشر رضعات أو خمس معلومات

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r6.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r6.claim: Aisha says a verse about stoning and ten adult nursing sessions was on a sheet beneath her bed, which a tame animal ate after the Prophet died.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r6.anchor: فلما مات رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وتشاغلنا بموته دخل داجن فأكلها

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r7.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r7.claim: Ibn Umar attributes to Aisha, through Ibn al-Zubayr, the view that fewer than seven nursing sessions do not prohibit marriage.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r7.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه بلغه عن ابن الزبير أنه يأثر عن عائشة في الرضاعة لا يحرم منها دون سبع رضعات

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r8.claim: Ibn Umar rejects the seven-session threshold, arguing that the verse states no minimum number of nursing sessions.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r8.anchor: قال: الله خير من عائشة إنما قال الله تعالى {وأخواتكم من الرضاعة} ولم يقل رضعة ولا رضعتين

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r9.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r9.claim: Tawus says the earlier rules of ten and then five sessions were superseded, and even one nursing session now establishes prohibition.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r9.anchor: عن طاوس أنه قيل له: إنهم يزعمون أنه لا يحرم من الرضاعة دون سبع رضعات ثم صار ذلك إلى خمس قال: قد كان ذلك فحدث بعد ذلك أمر جاء التحريم المرة الواحدة تحرم

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says one nursing session is sufficient to establish prohibition.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: المرة الواحدة تحرم

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r11.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r11.claim: Ibn Umar says one suck is sufficient to establish prohibition.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r11.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: المصة الواحدة تحرم

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r12.speaker: علي وعبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r12.claim: Ibrahim reports that Ali and Ibn Masud held that little or much breastfeeding is prohibited.
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r12.anchor: عن إبراهيم أنه سئل عن الرضاع فقال: إن عليا وعبد الله بن مسعود كانا يقولان: قليله وكثيره حرام

DURR-FULL:v2p471/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r13.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v2p471/r13.anchor: عن طاوس قال: اشترط عشر رضعات

DURR-FULL:v2p472/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r1.speaker: قيل
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r1.claim: An unnamed opinion says one nursing session establishes prohibition.
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r1.anchor: ثم قيل: إن الرضعة الواحدة تحرم وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن علي قال

DURR-FULL:v2p472/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r2.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r2.claim: Ali says breastfeeding prohibits marriage only when it occurs during the first two years.
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r2.anchor: عن علي قال: لا يحرم من الرضاع إلا ما كان في الحولين

DURR-FULL:v2p472/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وابن عمر وأبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r3.claim: Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, and Abu Hurayra are reported to give the same two-year limit.
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وابن عمر وأبي هريرة مثله

DURR-FULL:v2p472/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r4.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet’s statement that nursing is only from hunger, restricting the relevant nursing to infancy.
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r4.anchor: عن عائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إنما الرضاعة من المجاعة

DURR-FULL:v2p472/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r5.claim: The Prophet says a wife’s mother is forbidden as soon as he marries the daughter, while a daughter becomes lawful if he marries her mother but divorces before consummation.
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إذا نكح الرجل المرأة فلا يحل له أن يتزوج أمها دخل بالإبنة أم لم يدخل

DURR-FULL:v2p472/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r6.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says a wife’s mother remains forbidden even if the husband separates before touching the wife; the condition applies only to stepdaughters.
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r6.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت أنه سئل عن رجل تزوج امرأة ففارقها قبل أن يمسها هل تحل له أمها فقال: لا

DURR-FULL:v2p472/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r7.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r7.claim: Ata likewise says the mother is unconditionally forbidden, and denies that Ibn Abbas read a qualification restricting this to wives consummated with.
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r7.anchor: قلت لعطاء: الرجل ينكح المرأة ولم يجامعها حتى يطلقها أتحل له أمها قال: لا هي مرسلة

DURR-FULL:v2p472/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says mothers of wives are categorically forbidden, even if the wife is divorced before consummation or dies.
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وأمهات نسائكم} قال: هي مبهمة إذا طلق الرجل امرأته قبل أن يدخل بها أو ماتت لم تحل له أمها

DURR-FULL:v2p472/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r9.speaker: عمران بن حصين
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r9.claim: Imran ibn Husayn calls the prohibition of wives’ mothers unqualified.
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r9.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين في ((أمهات نسائكم)) قال: هي مبهمة

DURR-FULL:v2p472/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r10.claim: In a report from Abu Amr al-Shaybani, Ibn Masud initially allowed a man who divorced before consummation to marry the former wife’s mother.
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r10.anchor: عن أبي عمرو الشيباني أن رجلا من بني شمخ تزوج امرأة ولم يدخل بها ثم رأى أمها فأعجبته فاستفتى ابن مسعود فأمره أن يفارقها ثم يتزوج أمها

DURR-FULL:v2p472/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r11.speaker: أصحاب النبي
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r11.claim: When the case was later put to Umar and the Prophet’s Companions, they ruled that the marriage to the mother was not lawful.
DURR-FULL:v2p472/r11.anchor: ثم أتى ابن مسعود المدينة فسأل عمر وفي لفظ فسأل أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا: لا تصلح

DURR-FULL:v2p474/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r1.speaker: داود
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r1.claim: Dawud reports an Ibn Masud codex reading that makes the stepdaughter clause say “whose mothers you have entered upon.”
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r1.anchor: عن داود أنه قرأ في مصحف ابن مسعود وربائبكم اللاتي دخلتن بأمهاتهم

DURR-FULL:v2p474/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r2.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r2.claim: Ali says the “in your care” phrase limits the stepdaughter prohibition: a daughter not raised in the man’s care may be married.
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r2.anchor: قال: إنها لم تكن في حجرك إنما ذلك إذا كانت في حجرك

DURR-FULL:v2p474/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses entering upon a wife as sexual intercourse.
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: الدخول: الجماع

DURR-FULL:v2p474/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r4.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r4.claim: Tawus likewise glosses entering upon a wife as sexual intercourse.

DURR-FULL:v2p474/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya says a stepdaughter’s daughter and her descendants are forbidden, even down seventy generations.
DURR-FULL:v2p474/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال: بنت الربيبة وبنت ابنتها لا تصلح وإن كانت أسفل لسبعين بطنا

DURR-FULL:v2p475/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r1.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r1.claim: Ata says the prohibition was revealed after Quraysh criticized Muhammad for marrying Zayd’s wife, clarifying that only sons from one’s loins count as sons; the report also cites 33:4 and 33:40.
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r1.anchor: عن عطاء في قوله {وحلائل أبنائكم} قال: كنا نتحدث أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نكح امرأة زيد قال المشركون بمكة في ذلك

DURR-FULL:v2p475/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj similarly reports that Quraysh objected to the Prophet’s marriage to Zayd’s former wife as marrying his son’s wife, prompting the verse.
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: لما نكح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم امرأة زيد قالت قريش: نكح امرأة ابنه فنزلت

DURR-FULL:v2p475/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r3.speaker: الحسن ومحمد
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Muhammad call the prohibitions concerning fathers’ wives, sons’ wives, and wives’ mothers unqualified or general.
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r3.anchor: عن الحسن ومحمد قالا: إن هؤلاء الآيات مبهمات {وحلائل أبنائكم} و (ما نكح آباؤكم) (النساء الآية 22)

DURR-FULL:v2p475/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r4.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r4.claim: Ata says a woman divorced by a son before he had seen her remains forbidden to his father because the sons’ wives clause is general.
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: قلت لعطاء: الرجل ينكح المرأة لا يراها حتى يطلقها تحل لأبيه قال: هي مرسلة

DURR-FULL:v2p475/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r5.claim: The Prophet told Fīrūz al-Daylami, who had accepted Islam while married to two sisters, to divorce whichever sister he chose.
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r5.anchor: عن فيروز الديلمي أنه أدركه الإسلام وتحته أختان فقال له النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم طلق أيتهما شئت

DURR-FULL:v2p475/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says one verse permits a man to have intercourse with two enslaved women who are mother and daughter, while another forbids it, and he would not do so.
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r6.anchor: عن قيس قال: قلت لابن عباس: أيقع الرجل على المرأة وابنتها مملوكتين له فقال: أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية ولم أكن لأفعله

DURR-FULL:v2p475/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
