DURR-FULL:v2p475/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the ban on combining two sisters as applying to marriage.
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r7.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس {وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين} قال: يعني في النكاح

DURR-FULL:v2p475/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly saw no objection to combining two enslaved sisters.
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r8.anchor: من طريق عمرو بن دينار عن ابن عباس أنه كان لا يرى بأسا أن يجمع بين الأختين المملوكتين

DURR-FULL:v2p475/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the prohibition concerns free women, while combining two enslaved sisters is permissible.
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين} قال: ذلك في الحرائر فأما في المماليك فلا بأس

DURR-FULL:v2p475/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r10.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r10.claim: Uthman said one verse permitted combining two sisters in ownership and another forbade it, but he would not do it himself.
DURR-FULL:v2p475/r10.anchor: عن قبيصة بن ذؤيب أن رجلا سال عثمان بن عفان عن الأختين في ملك اليمين هل يجمع بينهما فقال: أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية وما كنت لأصنع ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas divides prohibited women into seven related by blood and seven by marriage, identifying mothers, daughters, sisters, aunts, and nieces as blood relatives.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r1.anchor: حرم عليكم سبع نسبا وسبع صهرا

IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r2.speaker: رسول الله
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r2.claim: The Prophet says nursing prohibits the same relationships that birth prohibits.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r2.anchor: ان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ان الرضاعة تحرم ما تحرم الولادة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r3.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r3.claim: Ata glosses a milk-sister as one's sister through nursing.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r3.anchor: عن عطاء قال : قال الله تعالى : واخواتكم من الرضاعة قال : وهي اختك من الرضاعة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r4.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r4.claim: Ali treats a wife's mother as forbidden like a stepdaughter, even when the marriage ended before consummation.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r4.anchor: قال علي : هي بمنزلة الربيبة ، يعني قوله : وامهات نسائكم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says a wife's mother remains forbidden after divorce or her death before consummation; the same view is reported from Ibn Masud, Imran ibn Husayn, Masruq, Tawus, Ikrimah, Ata, al-Hasan, Mak-hul, Ibn Sirin, Qatada, and al-Zuhri.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p911/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس انه كان يقول : اذا طلق الرجل امراة قبل ان يدخل بها أو ماتت ، لم تحل له امها

IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r1.claim: Ali permits marrying a stepdaughter who was not in the man's care, taking the phrase in your care as a condition.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r1.anchor: قال علي : لها ابنة قلت : نعم وهي بالطائف

IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r2.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says a stepdaughter and her mother are both permissible if the man has not consummated the marriage with the mother.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير قال : الربيبة والام سواء لا باس بهما اذا لم يدخل بالمراة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r3.speaker: مسروق
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r3.claim: Masruq says stepdaughters remain lawful until their mothers are married.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r3.anchor: عن مسروق قال : الربائب حلال ما لم تنكح الامهات

IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r4.claim: The report applies the stepdaughter prohibition when the man has entered into marriage with her mother, citing the verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r4.anchor: وسالته يعني : عكرمة : لا تحل له من اجل انه دخل بامها

IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets entering into a woman as marriage.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن قال : والدخول : النكاح

IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r6.speaker: طاووس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r6.claim: Tawus interprets entering into a woman as sexual intercourse.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r6.anchor: وروي عن طاوس قال : الدخول : الجماع

IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains no blame as no hardship.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله فلا جناح عليكم قال : فلا حرج

IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r8.claim: Said ibn Jubayr rules that a man may marry the daughter of a wife who died before consummation, as the verse says there is no blame.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p912/r8.anchor: سعيد بن جبير عن رجل تزوج امراة فماتت

IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r1.claim: Qatada disapproves of a father marrying a son's former wife even when the son divorced her before consummation, applying the ban on sons' wives.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r1.anchor: وكان قتادة يكره اذا تزوج الرجل المراة ، ثم طلقها قبل ان يدخل بها ان يتزوجها ابوه

IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r2.speaker: الحسن ومحمد
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r2.claim: Hasan and Muhammad treat the bans on sons' wives and mothers-in-law as unconditional; similar views are reported from Tawus, Ibn Sirin, Ibrahim, al-Zuhri, and Mak-hul.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r2.anchor: عن الحسن ومحمد : ان هؤلاء الايات مبهمات وحلائل ابنائكم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r3.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r3.claim: Ata reports that the verse was revealed after the Prophet married Zayd's wife and Meccan polytheists objected.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال : سألت عطاء عن : وحلائل ابنائكم قال : كنا نتحدث والله اعلم ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نكح امراة زيد

IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r4.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r4.claim: Uthman says one verse allows combining two enslaved sisters while another forbids it, and he would not do so.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r4.anchor: فقال عثمان : احلتهما آية ، وحرمتهما آية ، وما كنت لاصنع ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r5.claim: An unnamed Companion says he would make an example of anyone who combined two enslaved sisters; Ibn Shihab thinks he was Ali, and a similar view is reported from al-Zubayr.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r5.anchor: قال ابن شهاب : اراه علي بن أبي طالب . قال : وبلغني عن الزبير بن العوام نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas groups nursing relations, mothers-in-law, stepdaughters after consummation, sons' wives, and combining sisters among seven prohibitions by marriage.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p913/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قال : يحرم من النسب سبع ، ومن الصهر سبع ، ثم قرا وامهاتكم اللاتي ارضعنكم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r1.claim: Ibn Masud rejects combining two enslaved sisters and rebukes the appeal to the right-hand-possession exception by noting that even a camel belongs to one's possession.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود انه سئل عن الرجل يجمع بين الاختين الامتين ، فكرهه فقال : يقول الله تعالى : الا ما ملكت ايمانكم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r2.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r2.claim: Ata ibn Abi Rabah says the exception for what has passed refers to the pre-Islamic period.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r2.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح في قول الله تعالى : الا ما قد سلف قال : في جاهليتهم

IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r3.claim: Qatada says a woman is forbidden to her former husband's father and son even after divorce before consummation, and the exception refers to pre-Islamic men marrying their fathers' wives.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في الرجل يتزوج المراة ، ثم يطلقها قبل ان يراها ، قال : لا تحل لابيه ولا لابنه

IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r4.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains God's forgiveness as covering their former association of partners with God.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : غفورا رحيما قال : غفور لما كان منهم من الشرك

IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r5.claim: Qatada says the forgiveness covers many or major sins.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r5.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : غفورا قال : للذنوب الكثيرة أو الكبيرة

IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r6.claim: Said ibn Jubayr explains merciful as merciful toward His servants.
IBNABIHATIM:v3p914/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قوله : رحيما قال : بعباده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r1.claim: The passage moves from banning marriage to a father’s wife into listing prohibited relatives; the change from a future prohibition to ‘has been forbidden’ marks the latter as an established rule.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r1.anchor: تخلص إلى ذكر المحرمات بمناسبة ذكر تحريم نكاح ما نكح الآباء وغير أسلوب النهي فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Jahiliyya already forbade the relationships Islam forbids except marrying one’s father’s wife and combining two sisters; this explains the latter prohibition’s present-tense wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r2.anchor: ولذلك قال ابن عباس : ( كان أهل الجاهلية يحرمون ما يحرم الإسلام إلا امرأة الأب والجمع بين الأختين )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r3.claim: When prohibition attaches to the names of persons, it means prohibition of the usual act sought from them: eating carrion, drinking wine, and marrying mothers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r3.anchor: وتعلق التحريم بأسماء الذوات يحمل على تحريم ما يقصد من تلك الذات غالبا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r4.claim: The plural ummahāt is retained although Arabic dropped the singular forms amah and amaha; a rare poetic ammah occurs in Ibn Kaysan’s cited line.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r4.anchor: والأمهات جمع أمة أو أمهة ، والعرب أماتوا أمهة وأمه وأبقوا جمعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r5.speaker: ابن كيسان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r5.claim: Ibn Kaysan cites a rare form ummah in a line about a woman’s veil being contested in the markets.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r5.anchor: وورد أمة نادرا في قول شاعر أنشده ابن كيسان : تقبلتها عن أمة لك طالما تنوزع في الأسواق منها خمارها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r6.speaker: قصي بن كلاب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r6.claim: A rare form amaha appears in a verse attributed to Qusay ibn Kilab, naming Kinda and Ilyas as the poet’s mother and father.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r6.anchor: وورد أمهة نادرا في بيت يعزى إلى قصي بن كلاب : عند تناديهم بهالل وهبي أمهتي خندف وإلياس أبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r7.speaker: جرير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r7.claim: Jarir supplies a rare plural amāt in a line describing the mothers of al-Akhtal as disgraceful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r7.anchor: وجاء أمات قليلا في قول جرير : لقد ولد الأخيطل أم سوء مقلدة من الأمات عارا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r8.speaker: الراعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r8.claim: Al-Ra‘i’s line supports the view that amāt is used specifically for non-rational beings; the author says the original singular may have been umm or ummaha, with a deleted form restored in the plural.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p293/r8.anchor: وقيل : إن أمات خاص بما لا يعقل ، قال الراعي : كانت نجائب منذر ومحرق أماتهن وطرقهن فحيلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r1.claim: The Arabic names for family members are unusual because they preserve an older stage of the language, before later refinement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r1.anchor: ومن غريب الاتفاق أن أسماء أعضاء العائلة لم تجر على قياس مثل أب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r2.claim: The prohibited blood relatives include ascending and descending generations; many were already forbidden among Arabs, though their historical status developed across communities and laws.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r2.anchor: والمراد من الأمهات وما عطف عليها الدنيا وما فوقها ، وهؤلاء المحرمات من النسب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, as cited by Ibn Atiyya, said the listed women were forbidden in pre-Islamic Arabia except a father's wife and combining two sisters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس : أن المحرمات المذكورات هنا كانت محرمة في الجاهلية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r4.speaker: محمد بن الحسن صاحب أبي حنيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi transmits the same account from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, who additionally confines the exception phrase to the father's wife and combining sisters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r4.anchor: ومثله نقله القرطبي عن محمد بن الحسن صاحب أبي حنيفة مع زيادة توجيه ذكر الاستثناء بقوله : { إلا ما قد سلف } في هذبن خاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r5.claim: The claim that all these prohibitions were pre-Islamic cannot stand literally, since stepdaughters and foster sisters likely were not forbidden then.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r5.anchor: ولا أحسبهن كن محرمات في الجاهلية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r6.claim: Islam instills reverence for close kin, removing them from erotic use even though marriage has a legitimate end and begins from desire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r6.anchor: غرست لها في النفوس وقارا ينزه عن شوائب الاستعمال في اللهو والرفث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r7.claim: The kinship prohibitions extend reverence from parents and children to nieces and aunts, serving the necessary preservation of honor and human refinement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r7.anchor: من قسم المناسب الضروري ، وذلك من أوائل مظاهر الرقي البشري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r8.claim: In “daughters of the brother and sister,” the definite article stands in for a possessive phrase meaning your brother and your sister.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p295/r8.anchor: و ( ال ) في قوله : { وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت } عوض عن المضاف إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r1.claim: Calling wet nurses mothers follows Arabic usage rather than biological fact; their milk nourishes children and their affection resembles a birth mother's.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r1.anchor: سمى المراضع أمهات جريا على لغة العرب ، وما هن بأمهات حقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r2.claim: The phrase “who suckled you” clarifies that foster mothers are intended, since otherwise the qualifier would add nothing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r2.anchor: دفعا لتوهم أن المراد الأمهات إذ لو لا قصد إرادة المرضعات لما كان لهذا الوصف جدوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r3.claim: The verse leaves nursing's quality, duration, and number unstated, deferring these details to customary understanding.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r3.anchor: وقد أجملت هنا صفة الإرضاع ومدته وعدده إيكالا للناس إلى متعارفهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r4.claim: Nursing creates marriage prohibition when it supplies the child's necessary food, sustaining life in a way analogous to the mother.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r4.anchor: أن الرضاع إنما اعتبرت له هذه الحرمة لمعنى فيه وهو أنه الغذاء الذي لا غذاء غيره للطفل يعيش به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r5.claim: The Prophet said that legally significant nursing is that which satisfies hunger, supporting the nourishment-based criterion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r5.anchor: ولذلك قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( إنما الرضاعة من المجاعة )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r6.claim: The need for nursing ends at two full years, based on the Qur'anic instruction that mothers nurse their children for that period.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r6.anchor: وقد حددت مدة الحاجة إلى الرضاع بالحولين لقوله تعالى : { والوالدات يرضعن أولادهن حولين كاملين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب، وابن مسعود، وابن عباس، والزهري، ومالك، والشافعي، وأحمد، والأوزاعي، والثوري، وأبو يوسف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r7.claim: These authorities hold that nursing after the child has passed two years has no legal effect on kinship prohibitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r7.anchor: ولا اعتداد بالرضاع الحاصل بعد مضي تجاوز الطفل حولين من عمره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r8.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r8.claim: Abu Hanifa sets the nursing period at two years and six months.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r8.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة : المدة حولان وستة أشهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r9.speaker: ابن عبد الحكم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r9.claim: Ibn Abd al-Hakam reports Malik's view as two years plus a few days.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r9.anchor: وروى ابن عبد الحكم عن مالك : حولان وأيام يسيرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r10.speaker: ابن القاسم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r10.claim: Ibn al-Qasim reports from Malik a period of two years and two months.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r10.anchor: وروى ابن القاسم عنه : حولان وشهران

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r11.speaker: الوليد بن مسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r11.claim: Al-Walid ibn Muslim reports from Malik a longer period of two years, two months, and three months.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r11.anchor: وروى عنه الوليد بن مسلم : والشهران والثلاثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r12.claim: Ibn Ashur prefers the two-year limit and denies legal effect to nursing after it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r12.anchor: والأصح هو القول الأول ؛ ولا اعتداد برضاع فيما فوق ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r13.claim: The Prophet instructed Sahlah bint Suhayl, Abu Hudhayfa's wife, to nurse Salim, who entered her home as sons did.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r13.anchor: وما روي أن النبي أمر سهلة بنت سهيل زوجة أبي حذيفة أن ترضع سالما مولى أبي حذيفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r14.claim: The permission for Sahlah to nurse the adult Salim was a specific dispensation for her.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r14.anchor: إذ كان يدخل عليها كما يدخل الأبناء على أمهاتهم ، فتلك خصوصية لها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r15.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r15.claim: Aisha applied the Sahlah report by nursing men she wanted to admit behind her screen.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r15.anchor: وكانت عائشة أم المؤمنين إذا أرادت أن يدخل عليها أحد الحجاب أرضعته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r16.speaker: أمهات المؤمنين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r16.claim: The other Mothers of the Believers rejected Aisha's interpretation and did not permit anyone to enter on that basis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r16.anchor: وهو رأي لم يوافقها عليه أمهات المؤمنين ، وأبين أن يدخل أحد عليهن بذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r17.speaker: الليث بن سعد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r17.claim: Al-Layth ibn Sa'd accepted adult nursing as legally operative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r17.anchor: وقال به الليث بن سعد ، بإعمال رضاع الكبير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r18.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r18.claim: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari later withdrew the ruling after having issued a fatwa supporting adult nursing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p296/r18.anchor: وقد رجع عنه أبو موسى الأشعري بعد أن أفتى به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r1.claim: Calling a woman who nursed the same child a sister follows Arabic usage, just as a wet nurse is called a mother.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r1.anchor: إطلاق اسم الأخت على التي رضعت من ثدي مرضعة من أضيفت أخت إليه جرى على لغة العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r2.claim: The verbal noun rada'a is usually pronounced with an open first vowel; kasra is also possible but unattested in recitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r2.anchor: والرضاعة بفتح الراء اسم مصدر رضع ، ويجوز كسر الراء ولم يقرأ به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r3.claim: The phrase “from nursing” is a causal circumstantial modifier; foster siblinghood requires the girl to have been nursed by the same woman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r3.anchor: ومحل { من الرضاعة } حال من { أخواتكم } و ( من ) فيه للتعليل والسببية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r4.claim: The affinal categories from mothers-in-law through combining sisters are Islamic prohibitions, since pre-Islamic Arabs permitted even wives of fathers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r4.anchor: ولا أحسب أن أهل الجاهلية كانوا يحرمون شيئا منها ، كيف وقد أباحوا أزواج الآباء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r5.claim: When asked about marrying Durra bint Abu Salama, the Prophet said she was his stepdaughter and, independently, foster niece through Thuwayba.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r5.anchor: فسألته إحدى أمهات المؤمنين فقال : ( لو لم تكن ربيبتي لما حلت لي إنها ابنة أخي من الرضاعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r6.claim: The author's view is that Ibn Atiyya's report from Ibn Abbas about pre-Islamic prohibitions is not universal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r6.anchor: فأرى أن هذا من تحريم الإسلام وأن ما حكى ابن عطية عن ابن عباس ليس على إطلاقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r7.speaker: الفخر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r7.claim: Al-Fakhr argues that affinity prohibitions allow family members to visit and interact while preventing desire, jealousy, painful conflict, and divorce.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r7.anchor: لو لم يدخل على المرأة أبو الرجل وابنه ، ولم تدخل على الرجل امرأته وابنتها ، لبقيت المرأة كالمحبوسة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r8.claim: Ibn Ashur classifies the rationale for these affinal prohibitions as a need-based, complementary public benefit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p297#2/r8.anchor: قلت : وعليه فتحريم هؤلاء من قسم الحاجي من المناسب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r1.claim: The consummation condition modifies stepdaughters: a stepdaughter is forbidden only after intercourse with her mother, not upon the marriage contract alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r1.anchor: وهو قيد في تحريم الربائب بحيث لا تحرم الربيبة إلا إذا وقع البناء بأمها ، ولا يحرمها مجرد العقد على أمها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r2.claim: The majority holds that a wife's mother is prohibited as soon as her daughter is married, without requiring consummation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r2.anchor: فقال الجمهور هناك : أمهات نسائكم معناه أمهات أزواجكم ، فأم الزوجة تحرم بمجرد عقد الرجل على ابنتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب، وزيد بن ثابت، وابن عمر، وعبد الله بن عباس، ومجاهد، وجابر، وابن الزبير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r3.claim: These authorities hold that a mother-in-law becomes forbidden only after the husband consummates the marriage with her daughter, applying the qualified rule to the unqualified one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r3.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب ، وزيد بن ثابت ، وابن عمر ، وعبد الله بن عباس ، ومجاهد ، وجابر ، وابن الزبير : لا تحرم أم المرأة على زوج ابنتها حتى يدخل بابنتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur regards the qualified reading requiring consummation as the sounder interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r4.anchor: حملا للمطلق على المقيد ، وهو الأصح محملا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r5.claim: The majority offers no clear rationale or transmitted report for its position; the parallel rationale for stepdaughters supports requiring consummation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r5.anchor: ولم يستطع الجمهور أن يوجهوا مذهبهم بعلة بينة ، ولا أن يستظهروا عليه بأثر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r6.claim: Because mothers-in-law are named before stepdaughters, a consummation condition intended for both would have appeared before the stepdaughter clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r6.anchor: ويظهر أن الله ذكر أمهات النساء قبل أن يذكر الربائب ، فلو أراد اشتراط الدخول بالأمهات في تحريمهن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r7.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r7.claim: A report from Zayd says a man may marry the daughter if he divorced her mother before consummation, but not if the mother died.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r7.anchor: إذا طلق الأم قبل البناء فله التزوج بابنتها ، وإذا ماتت حرمت عليه ابنتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r8.claim: The reported distinction treats death as coercive and divorce as renunciation, but Ibn Ashur says the view has no weight.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p299/r8.anchor: وكأنه نظر إلى أن الطلاق عدول عن العقد ، والموت أمر قاهر ، فكأنه كان ناويا الدخول بها ، ولا حظ لهذا القول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r1.claim: Halila, meaning a wife, may be an active participle because she lives lawfully with her husband; al-Zajjaj instead analyzes it as passive, made lawful by her family.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r1.anchor: الحلائل جمع الحليلة فعيلة بمعنى فاعلة ، وهي الزوجة ، لأنها تحل معه ، وقال الزجاج : هي فعيلة بمعنى مفعولة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes halila as passive, “made lawful,” and compares the passive use of fa'il from a quadriliteral verb to hakim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r2.anchor: أي محللة إذ أباحها أهلها له ، فيكون من مجيء فعيل للمفعول من الرباعي في قولهم حكيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r3.claim: The wording “wives of your sons” varies the expression to avoid repeating earlier terms; the three expressions have no difference in reference.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r3.anchor: والعدول عن أن يقال : وما نكح أبناؤكم أو ونساء أبنائكم إلى قوله : { وحلائل أبنائكم } تفنن لتجنب تكرير أحد اللفظين السابقين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r4.claim: A husband is also called halil, with the same two possible morphological readings; forbidding a son's wife is as clear in rationale as forbidding a father's wife.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r4.anchor: وقد سمي الزوج أيضا بالحليل وهو يحتمل الوجهين كذلك . وتحريم حليلة الابن واضح العلة ، كتحريم حليلة الأب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r5.claim: “From your loins” confirms biological sons, since Arabs treated adopted children as sons until Islam abolished that status.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r5.anchor: تأكيد لمعنى الأبناء لدفع احتمال المجاز ، إذ كانت العرب تسمي المتبنى ابنا ، وتجعل له ما للابن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r6.claim: The command to call adopted children by their fathers abolished adoption as lineage; al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad was considered an exceptional case.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r6.anchor: حتى أبطل الإسلام ذلك وقوله تعالى : { ادعوهم لآبائهم } ( الأحزاب : 5 ) فما دعي أحد لمتبنيه بعد ، إلا المقداد بن الأسود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r7.claim: The Prophet's marriage to Zaynab after Zayd divorced her enacted the rule that adoption does not create biological-son marriage prohibitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r7.anchor: بالإذن لرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بتزوج زينب ابنة جحش ، بعد أن طلقها زيد بن حارثة الذي كان تبناه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r8.claim: Grandsons and granddaughters, however distant through sons or daughters, are biological descendants because the grandfather necessarily contributed to their birth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300/r8.anchor: وابن الابن وابن البنت ، وإن سفلا ، أبناء من الأصلاب لأن للجد عليهم ولادة لا محالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r1.claim: The ban on combining sisters aims to prevent jealousy and preserve affection; its primary application is marriage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r1.anchor: فحكمته دفع الغيرة عمن يريد الشرع بقاء تمام المودة بينهما ، وقد علم أن المراد الجمع بينهما فيما فيه غيرة ، وهو النكاح أصالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r2.claim: The same rationale extends the ban to concubinage, and the general permission in 4:24 is restricted by this prohibition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r2.anchor: ويلحق به الجمع بينهما في التسري بملك اليمين ، إذ العلة واحدة فقوله تعالى : { وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r3.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r3.claim: Asked about combining two sisters as concubines, Uthman cited one verse allowing and another forbidding it, and therefore suspended judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r3.anchor: وروي عن عثمان بن عفان : أنه سئل عن الجمع بين الأختين في التسري فقال : ( أحلتهما ) آية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r4.speaker: علي، وجمع من الصحابة، ومالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r4.claim: Ali, a group of Companions, and Malik forbid combining sisters in concubinage; Malik requires ending the first relationship by sale, contract of manumission, or emancipation before taking the other.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r4.anchor: وروي مثله عن علي ، وعن جمع من الصحابة ، أن الجمع بينهما في التسري حرام ، وهو قول مالك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r5.claim: Malik says there is no hadd punishment if a man combines two sisters as concubines.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r6.speaker: الظاهرية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r6.claim: The Zahirites permit combining sisters as concubines because the verse concerns marriage, while mere joint ownership is unrestricted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p300#2/r6.anchor: وقال الظاهرية : يجوز الجمع بين الأختين في التسري لأن الآية واردة في أحكام النكاح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r1.claim: The exception “except what has passed” follows the same interpretation as the preceding exception in the prior verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r1.anchor: وقوله : { إلا ما قد سلف } هو كنظيره السابق ، والبيان فيه كالبيان هناك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r2.speaker: القرطبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi suggests a further meaning: pre-Islamic marriages combining sisters remain valid, with the man choosing one after Islam without applying Islamic contract rules retroactively.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r2.anchor: ويحتمل معنى زائدا وهو جواز ما سلف وأنه إذا جرى الجمع في الجاهلية كان النكاح صحيحا وإذا جرى الجمع في الإسلام خير بين الأختين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi does not attribute this additional interpretation to any jurist.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r3.anchor: ولم يعز القول بذلك لأحد من الفقهاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r4.claim: The closing mention of forgiveness and mercy fits an exception that confirms prior pre-Islamic marriages: forgiveness ends continuation and mercy explains pardon.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v4p301/r4.anchor: فالمغفرة للتجاوز عن الاستمرار عليه ، والرحمة لبيان سبب ذلك التجاوز

FARRA:v1p259/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p259/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p259/r5.claim: أن تجمعوا بين الأختين is nominative in sense, like the verbal noun الجمع بين الأختين.
FARRA:v1p259/r5.anchor: أن في موضع رفع كقولك: والجمع بين الأختين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r1.claim: A maternal aunt’s aunt is prohibited when she is the mother’s paternal sister, as sister of a grandparent; if only maternal, her aunt is unrelated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r1.anchor: فإن كانت الخالة أخت أم لأب، فعمتها حرام، لأنها أخت جد، وإن كانت الخالة أخت أم لأم فقط فعمتها أجنبية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r2.claim: Nieces of brothers and sisters include full, paternal, and maternal sibling relations.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r2.anchor: وكذلك في بنات الأخ وبنات الأخت العموم والإبهام، سواء كانت الأخوة شقيقة. أو لأب أو لأم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r3.speaker: أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r3.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads al-riḍāʿa with kasra on rāʾ; breastfeeding creates the same marriage prohibitions as lineage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة «من الرضاعة» بكسر الراء، والرضاع يحرم ما يحرم النسب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r4.claim: The nursing mother is a mother; her children, born before or after, are siblings, as are the milk-father’s children.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r4.anchor: والمرضعة أم، وما تقدم من أولادها وتأخر إخوة، وفحل اللبن أب، وما تقدم من أولاده وتأخر إخوة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود، وابن هرمز
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads al-lāʾī with kasra on yāʾ; Ibn Hurmuz uses singular allatī, which can apply to one or many.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود «اللاي» بكسر الياء، وقرأ ابن هرمز «وأمهاتكم التي» بالإفراد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r6.speaker: جمهور أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r6.claim: The majority say a wife’s mother is prohibited by the marriage contract whether or not the husband had intercourse with the daughter; companions, successors, and regional jurists share this.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r6.anchor: واختلف الناس في تأويل قوله تعالى: وأمهات نسائكم فقال جمهور أهل العلم: هي تامة العموم فيمن دخل بها أو لم يدخل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r7.claim: Asked about a man who divorced before intercourse, ʿAlī said he may marry the mother, treating her like a stepdaughter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r7.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب أنه قيل له في رجل تزوج امرأة فطلقها قبل أن يدخل بها أيتزوج أمها؟ قال: نعم، هي بمنزلة الربيبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says ʿAlī means the “consummated with” condition applies both to wives’ mothers and to stepdaughters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r8.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: يريد أن قوله تعالى: من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن شرط في هذه، وفي الربيبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r9.claim: A similar view is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, though another report from him agrees with the majority.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r9.anchor: وروي نحوه عن ابن عباس، وروي عنه كقول الجمهور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r10.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r10.claim: Zayd disliked marrying a wife’s mother after the wife died and he inherited from her, but allowed it if he had divorced her before intercourse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r10.anchor: وروي عن زيد بن ثابت، أنه كان يقول: إذا ماتت عنده فأخذ ميراثها كره أن يخلف على أمها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r11.claim: Mujāhid says consummation is required in both cases, contrary to the majority.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الدخول مراد في النازلتين، وقول جمهور الناس مخالف لهذا القول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r12.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r12.claim: A further report from Zayd says mothers of wives are unqualifiedly prohibited, while the condition applies only to stepdaughters.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r12.anchor: وروي في ذلك عن زيد بن ثابت أنه قال: أمهات نسائكم مبهمة، وإنما الشرط في الربائب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r13.speaker: ابن جريج عن عطاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r13.claim: Ibn Jurayj asks whether Ibn ʿAbbās read the consummation condition after “mothers of wives”; ʿAṭāʾ answers with a phrase understood as no.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r13.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: قلت لعطاء: أكان ابن عباس يقرأ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects extending the condition to wives’ mothers on grammatical grounds: genitives with different governors cannot share an adjective.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32/r14.anchor: ويرد هذا القول من جهة الإعراب أن المجرورين إذا اختلفا لم يكن نعتهما واحدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r1.claim: A rabība is a man’s stepdaughter, named because he raises her in his home; the word is a feminine passive form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r1.anchor: الربيبة: بنت امرأة الرجل من غيره، سميت بذلك لأنه يربيها في حجره فهي مربوبته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r2.claim: “In your households” describes the usual situation rather than a condition: the stepdaughter remains prohibited even outside the home.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: اللاتي في حجوركم ذكر الأغلب في هذه الأمور، إذ هي حالة الربيبة في الأكثر، وهي محرمة وإن كانت في غير الحجر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r3.speaker: علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r3.claim: A report from ʿAlī allows a stepdaughter outside the man’s household even after he consummated her mother, if she lives far away.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r3.anchor: إلا ما روي عن علي أنه قال: تحل إذا لم تكن في الحجر وإن دخل بالأم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r4.claim: Ḥijr can be pronounced with kasra or fatḥa; it first meant the front fold of a garment and the space before its wearer, then protection and shelter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r4.anchor: وهو مقدم ثوب الإنسان وما بين يديه منه في حالة اللبس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، وطاوس، وابن دينار
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r5.claim: They interpret consummation as intercourse, so after the marriage ceremony but before intercourse the daughter remains lawful.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r5.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وطاوس وابن دينار: الدخول في هذا الموضع الجماع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r6.speaker: جمهور من العلماء، ومالك بن أنس، وعطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r6.claim: The majority hold undressing, kissing, lying together, and every form of pleasure also prohibit the daughter, like intercourse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r6.anchor: وقال جمهور من العلماء منهم مالك بن أنس وعطاء بن أبي رباح وغيرهم: إن التجريد والتقبيل والمضاجعة وجميع أنواع التلذذ يحرم الابنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r7.claim: Ḥalāʾil is plural of ḥalīla, wife, because she lives with her husband wherever he settles; it is a feminine active form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r7.anchor: والحلائل: جمع حليلة، وهي الزوجة، لأنها تحل مع الرجل حيث حل، فهي فعلية بمعنى فاعلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج وقوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj and others derive ḥalīla from the word for lawful, giving it the sense “made lawful.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r8.anchor: وذهب الزجاج وقوم: إلى أنها من لفظة الحلال، فهي حليلة بمعنى محللة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r9.claim: “Those from your loins” excludes adopted sons who were not biologically descended, a widespread Arab custom.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r9.anchor: وقوله: الذين من أصلابكم تخصيص ليخرج عنه كل من كانت العرب تتبناه ممن ليس للصلب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r10.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r10.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the verse descended when Muhammad married Zayd ibn Ḥāritha’s former wife and polytheists objected that he married his son’s wife.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r10.anchor: قال عطاء ابن أبي رباح: يتحدث- والله أعلم- أنها نزلت في محمد عليه السلام حين تزوج امرأة زيد بن حارثة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r11.claim: A milk-son’s wife is also prohibited by consensus, based on the Prophetic rule that breastfeeding prohibits what lineage prohibits.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r11.anchor: وحرمت حليلة الابن من الرضاع وإن لم يكن للصلب بالإجماع المستند إلى قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، يحرم من الرضاعة ما يحرم من النسب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r12.claim: The ban on combining sisters applies to marriage and ownership; the community unanimously forbids doing so in marriage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r12.anchor: لفظ يعم الجمع بنكاح وبملك يمين، وأجمعت الأمة على منع جمعهما بنكاح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r13.speaker: عثمان بن عفان، وابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r13.claim: ʿUthmān says one verse permits combining sisters and another forbids it, and personally regards it as improper; a similar view is attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r13.anchor: فقال عثمان بن عفان رضي الله عنه: أحلتهما آية، وحرمتهما آية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r14.speaker: إسحاق بن راهويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r14.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir reports that Isḥāq ibn Rāhwayh prohibited combining sisters in sexual relations under ownership.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r14.anchor: وذكر أن إسحاق بن راهويه حرم الجمع بينهما بالوطء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r15.speaker: جمهور أهل العلم، ومالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r15.claim: Most scholars disliked combining sisters under ownership; Mālik counted among them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p32#2/r15.anchor: وأن جمهور أهل العلم كرهوا ذلك، وجعل مالكا فيمن كرهه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r1.claim: There is no disagreement that a man may own two sisters together, or a mother and her daughter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r1.anchor: ولا خلاف في جواز جمعهما في الملك، وكذلك الأم وبنتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r2.speaker: إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya infers from Ishaq's position that a man who has intercourse with both sisters would be stoned.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r2.anchor: ويجيء من قول إسحاق أن يرجم الجامع بينهما بالوطء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r3.claim: Malik's ruling suspending a man after intercourse with both sisters implies disapproval; he imposed no fixed penalty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r3.anchor: وتستقرأ الكراهية من قول مالك: إنه إذا وطئ واحدة ثم وطئ أخرى وقف عنهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عمر والحسن البصري والأوزاعي والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r4.claim: These authorities forbid intercourse with the second sister until the first is removed from ownership by sale, emancipation, or marriage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r4.anchor: فقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه وابن عمر والحسن البصري والأوزاعي والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق: لا يجوز له وطء الثانية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r5.claim: Qatada's alternative permits intercourse with the second after the man intends to forbid himself the first, abstains, and completes her waiting period.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r5.anchor: وهو أنه إن كان يطأ واحدة وأراد وطء الأخرى فإنه ينوي تحريم الأولى على نفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r6.claim: In Malik's school, an owner may have intercourse with either sister, while restraint from the other is initially entrusted to his honesty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r6.anchor: فله أن يطأ أيتهما شاء، والكف عن الأخرى موكول إلى أمانته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r7.claim: To switch sisters under Malik's rule, he must prohibit himself from the first through disposal, marriage, emancipation for a term, or long-term service.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r7.anchor: فإن أراد وطء الأخرى فيلزمه أن يحرم على نفسه فرج الأولى بفعل يفعله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r8.claim: If he has intercourse with one and then unexpectedly with the other, both are suspended until he prohibits one, because he is now suspect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r8.anchor: وقف عنهما ولم يجز له قرب إحداهما حتى يحرم الأخرى، ولم يبق ذلك إلى أمانته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r9.speaker: المدونة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r9.claim: One Maliki position suspends both women when he contracts marriage to the slave sister, disliking a contract made where intercourse is forbidden except for a common temporary impediment such as menstruation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r9.anchor: في النكاح الثالث من المدونة أنه يوقف عنهما إذا وقع عقد النكاح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r10.speaker: قول آخر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r10.claim: Another position holds that the marriage contract does not take effect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r10.anchor: وفي الباب بعينه قول آخر: إن النكاح لا ينعقد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r11.speaker: أشهب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r11.claim: Ashhab says contracting marriage to one sister itself prohibits intercourse with the enslaved sister.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r11.anchor: عقد النكاح في الواحدة تحريم لفرج المملوكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r12.claim: The Prophet forbade combining a woman with her paternal or maternal aunt, and the community reached consensus on this prohibition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r12.anchor: وثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه نهى أن يجمع بين المرأة وعمتها، وبين المرأة وخالتها، وأجمعت الأمة على ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r13.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r13.claim: Some scholars considered the aunt-and-niece prohibition hadith to abrogate the general permission in 4:24.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p33/r13.anchor: وقد رأى بعض العلماء أن هذا الحديث ناسخ لعموم قوله تعالى: وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p123#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p123#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p123#2/r1.claim: Ḥalāʾil of one's sons are the wives of one's sons.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r1.claim: The original form of ummahāt is ummāt; the hāʾ was added for emphasis, as in ahraqt from araqt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r1.anchor: الأصل في أمهات أمات ولكن الهاء زيدت مؤكدة كما زادوها في أهرقت الماء وإنما أصله أرقت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r2.claim: Wet nurses are called mothers here because of the resulting prohibition of marriage.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r3.speaker: حنبل عن أحمد، عمر، علي، ابن عباس، ابن عمر، الحسن، طاووس، الشعبي، النخعي، الزهري، الأوزاعي، الثوري، مالك، أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r3.claim: One legal position makes even a single suckling establish the marriage prohibition; Ahmad's report through Hanbal and the listed early authorities hold this.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r3.anchor: نقل حنبل عن أحمد أنه يتعلق التحريم بالرضعة الواحدة وهو قول عمر وعلي وابن عباس وابن عمر والحسن وطاووس والشعبي والنخعي والزهري والأوزاعي والثوري ومالك وأبي حنيفة وأصحابه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r4.speaker: محمد بن العباس عن أحمد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r4.claim: A second report from Ahmad sets the threshold at three sucklings.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r4.anchor: نقل محمد بن العباس عن أحمد أنه يتعلق التحريم بثلاث رضعات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r5.speaker: أبو الحارث عن أحمد، الشافعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r5.claim: Another report from Ahmad requires at least five separate sucklings; al-Shafiʿi holds the same position.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p46/r5.anchor: نقل أبو الحارث عن أحمد لا يتعلق بأقل من خمس رضعات متفرقات وهو قول الشافعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r1.speaker: عمر وابن مسعود وابن عمر وعمران بن حصين ومسروق وعطاء وطاووس والحسن والجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r1.claim: A wife's mother becomes prohibited upon the marriage contract with her daughter, whether or not the husband consummated the marriage.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r1.anchor: أمهات النساء يحرمن بنفس العقد على البنت سواء دخل بالبنت أو لم يدخل وهذا قول عمر وابن مسعود وابن عمر وعمران بن حصين ومسروق وعطاء وطاووس والحسن والجمهور

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r2.speaker: علي، مجاهد، عكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r2.claim: Ali permits a man who divorces before consummation to marry his former wife's mother; Mujahid and Ikrima share this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r2.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه في رجل طلق امرأته قبل الدخول له أن يتزوج أمها وهذا قول مجاهد وعكرمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r3.claim: A rabība is one's wife's daughter from another man; the word derives from being raised by the husband, while the phrase about being in his household describes the usual case rather than a condition.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r3.anchor: الربيبة بنت امرأة الزوج من غيره ومعنى الربيبة مربوبة لأن الرجل يربيها وخرج الكلام على الأعم من كون التربية في حجر الرجل لا على الشرط

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says ḥalāʾil means wives and derives ḥalīla from muḥilla, something lawful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج الحلائل الأزواج وحليلة بمعنى محلة وهي مشتقة من الحلال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r5.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r5.claim: Another explanation derives the name from a wife being lawful to her husband wherever he is.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r5.anchor: وقال غيره سميت بذلك لأنها تحل معه أينما كان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r6.speaker: أبو منصور اللغوي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r6.claim: Al-Halil is the husband and al-halila the wife; one proposed derivation is that they settle in the same place.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r6.anchor: قال الحليل الزوج والحليلة المرأة وسميا بذلك إما لأنهما يحلان في موضع واحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r7.speaker: أبو منصور اللغوي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r7.claim: A second proposed derivation links the spouses' names to each overcoming or facing the other.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r7.anchor: أو لأن كل واحد منهما يحال صاحبه أي ينازله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r8.speaker: أبو منصور اللغوي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r8.claim: A third proposed derivation says each spouse loosens the other's waist-wrap.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r8.anchor: أو لأن كل واحد منهما يحل إزار صاحبه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r9.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r9.claim: The specification sons from your loins excludes adopted sons.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r9.anchor: قال عطاء إنما ذكر الأصلاب لأجل الأدعياء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r10.claim: The discussion of except what has passed follows the treatment of that phrase in the preceding verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r10.anchor: على نحو ما تقدم في الآية التي قبلها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r11.speaker: عطاء والسدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r11.claim: A reported interpretation applies the exception to Jacob's past marriage to Joseph's mother and her sister; the author calls it weak because laws differ and its transmission is hard to establish.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r11.anchor: أحدهما إلا ما قد سلف من أمر يعقوب عليه السلام لأنه جمع بين أم يوسف و أختها وهذا مروي عن عطاء و السدي وفيه ضعف لوجهين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r12.claim: The Jacob interpretation is weak: this prohibition belongs to our law, laws need not agree, others' acts cannot explain pardon for us, and the report is difficult to substantiate.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r12.anchor: أن هذا التحريم يتعلق بشريعتنا وليس كل الشرائع تتفق ولا وجه للعفو عنا فيما فعله غيرنا والثاني أنه لو طولب قائل هذا بتصحيح نقله لعسر عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r13.speaker: أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r13.claim: Another view preserves earlier marriages to two sisters without dissolution and gives the husband a choice of one; the report of Fayruz al-Daylami says the Prophet told him to divorce one sister.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p47/r13.anchor: أن العقود المتقدمة على الأختين لا تنفسخ ويكون للانسان أن يختار إحداهما ومنه حديث فيروز الديلمي قال أسلمت وعندي أختان فأتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال طلق إحداهما ذكره القاضي أبو يعلى

MAJAZ:v1p121/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p121/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p121/r6.claim: Al-muḥṣanāt here are women with husbands, while ḥāṣin means a chaste woman.

MAJAZ:v1p121/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p121/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p121/r7.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj’s line describes a chaste woman protected from harm and from contact with leprosy.
MAJAZ:v1p121/r7.anchor:
قال العجاج:
وحاصن من حاصنات ملس ... من الأذى ومن قراف الوقس

MAJAZ:v1p121/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p121/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p121/r8.claim: Kitāba Allāhi ʿalaykum means God prescribed that for you; Arabic uses the accusative when a noun stands where a verb would.
MAJAZ:v1p121/r8.anchor: «كتاب الله عليكم» (23) أي: كتب الله ذاك عليكم، والعرب تفعل مثل هذا إذا كان فى موضع «فعل»

MAJAZ:v1p121/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p121/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p121/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ explains Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr’s manṣūb qīlahum as “they say,” a noun used where a verb would stand.
MAJAZ:v1p121/r9.anchor:
عن أبى عمرو بن العلاء، قال كعب بن زهير:
تسعى الوشاة جنابيها وقيلهم ... إنك يا ابن أبى سلمي لمقتول

MAJAZ:v1p121/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p121/r10.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p121/r10.claim: The same accusative construction appears in ṣabran, mahlan, and ḥallan, meaning “be patient,” “wait,” and “loosen.”
MAJAZ:v1p121/r10.anchor: كقولك: «صبرا ومهلا وحلا، أي: اصبر، وأمهل، وتحلل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r1.claim: The verse prohibits marriage to relatives by blood, with further prohibitions through nursing and affinity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية الكريمة هي آية تحريم المحارم من النسب، وما يتبعه من الرضاع والمحارم بالصهر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas classifies seven prohibited relations by blood and seven by affinity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: حرمت عليكم سبع نسبا، وسبع صهرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r3.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r3.claim: Most scholars prohibit a daughter conceived through fornication because the verse’s general ‘your daughters’ includes her; Abu Hanifa, Malik, and Ahmad hold this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r3.anchor: وقد استدل جمهور العلماء على تحريم المخلوقة من ماء الزاني عليه بعموم قوله تعالى: {وبناتكم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r4.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r4.claim: A view attributed to al-Shafi‘i permits her because she is not a legally recognized daughter and, like a child outside the inheritance rule, does not inherit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p247#2/r4.anchor: وقد حكي عن الشافعي شيء في إباحتها؛ لأنها ليست بنتا شرعية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r1.claim: The Prophet taught that nursing prohibits the same relations as birth; Muslim also gives the wording that nursing prohibits what lineage prohibits.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r1.anchor: عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الرضاعة تحرم ما تحرم الولادة"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r2.claim: Reports that the nursing rule has four or six exceptions do not qualify the hadith: examples either exist through blood kinship or are prohibited by affinity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r2.anchor: والتحقيق أنه لا يستثنى شيء من ذلك؛ لأنه يوجد مثل بعضها في النسب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r3.claim: Malik and others hold that any nursing amount establishes prohibition, relying on the verse’s general wording; this is also attributed to Ibn Umar and early jurists.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r3.anchor: فذهب ذاهبون إلى أنه يحرم مجرد الرضاع لعموم هذه الآية. وهذا قول مالك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r4.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r4.claim: Another view requires at least three feeds, based on the Prophet’s statement that one or two sucks do not prohibit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r4.anchor: عن عائشة؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "لا تحرم المصة والمصتان"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r5.speaker: أم الفضل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r5.claim: Umm al-Fadl transmits a Prophetic report likewise ruling that one or two feeds or sucks do not establish prohibition.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r5.anchor: عن أم الفضل قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تحرم الرضعة ولا الرضعتان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r6.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r6.claim: A third view requires five feeds, based on Aisha’s report that ten known feeds were abrogated by five, which remained recited at the Prophet’s death.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p248/r6.anchor: عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها، قالت: كان فيما أنزل [الله] (5) من القرآن: عشر رضعات معلومات يحرمن.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r1.speaker: سهلة بنت سهيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r1.claim: In the Salim case the Prophet ordered Sahla to nurse Abu Hudhayfa’s freedman five times; Aisha used five feeds for women seeking access, and al-Shafi‘i and his followers adopted this view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r1.anchor: وفي حديث سهلة بنت سهيل: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أمرها أن ترضع مولى أبي حذيفة خمس رضعات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r2.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r2.claim: The majority require nursing to occur while the child is under two years old, linking the issue to 2:233.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r2.anchor: ثم ليعلم أنه لا بد أن تكون الرضاعة في سن الصغر دون الحولين على قول الجمهور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r3.speaker: جمهور الأئمة الأربعة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r3.claim: The four Sunni schools and others hold that milk kinship extends through the nursing father as well as the nursing mother.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r3.anchor: واختلفوا: هل يحرم لبن الفحل، كما هو قول جمهور الأئمة الأربعة وغيرهم؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r4.speaker: بعض السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r4.claim: Some early authorities restrict milk kinship to the nursing mother and do not extend it through the father.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249/r4.anchor: وإنما يختص الرضاع بالأم فقط، ولا ينتشر إلى ناحية الأب كما هو لبعض السلف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r1.claim: A wife’s mother becomes prohibited as soon as the marriage contract is made, whether or not the marriage is consummated.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r1.anchor: أما (11) أم المرأة فإنها تحرم بمجرد العقد على ابنتها، سواء دخل بها أو لم يدخل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r2.claim: A stepdaughter becomes prohibited only after consummation with her mother; if the mother is divorced before consummation, her daughter may be married.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r2.anchor: وأما الربيبة وهي بنت المرأة فلا تحرم بمجرد العقد على أمها حتى يدخل بها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r3.claim: Some interpret the consummation condition as applying to both mothers and stepdaughters, so neither is prohibited before consummation with the other.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r3.anchor: وقد فهم بعضهم عود الضمير إلى الأمهات [و] (13) الربائب فقال: لا تحرم واحدة من الأم ولا البنت بمجرد العقد على الأخرى حتى يدخل بها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r4.speaker: علي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r4.claim: Ali compares the wife’s mother to a stepdaughter in the case of a man who divorced before consummation, applying the entry condition to her too.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r4.anchor: عن علي، رضي الله عنه، في رجل تزوج امرأة فطلقها قبل أن يدخل بها، أيتزوج أمها؟ قال: هي بمنزلة الربيبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says a man who divorces before consummation may marry his former wife’s mother.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r5.anchor: عن زيد بن ثابت قال: إذا طلق الرجل امرأته قبل أن يدخل بها فلا بأس أن يتزوج أمها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r6.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r6.claim: Zayd disliked marrying the mother if the wife died and the husband inherited from her, but allowed it after divorce before consummation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r6.anchor: أنه كان يقول: إذا ماتت عنده وأخذ ميراثها كره أن يخلف على أمها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas permitted marrying the mother in a case where the man had not consummated the marriage to her daughter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r7.anchor: فسألت ابن عباس وأخبرته الخبر (5) فقال: انكح أمها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r8.claim: Ibn Umar forbade marrying the mother in that case.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r8.anchor: فسألت ابن عمر فقال: لا تنكحها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r9.speaker: معاوية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r9.claim: Muawiya declined to declare what God permitted or prohibited and pointed out that many other women were available.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p249#2/r9.anchor: فكتب معاوية: إني لا أحل ما حرم الله، ولا أحرم ما أحل [الله]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr treats the stepdaughter and her mother alike: both are permissible if the man did not consummate the marriage with the woman.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير قال: الربيبة والأم سواء، لا بأس بها إذا لم يدخل بالمرأة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r2.claim: Mujahid says the consummation condition applies to both the wife’s mother and her daughter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r2.anchor: أن مجاهدا قال له: {وأمهات نسائكم وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم} أراد (12) بهما الدخول جميعا (13)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir says most early and later scholars reject that reading: a stepdaughter is prohibited only after consummation with her mother, while the mother is prohibited at contract.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r3.anchor: وقد خالفه جمهور العلماء من السلف والخلف، فرأوا أن الربيبة لا تحرم بمجرد العقد على الأم، وأنها لا تحرم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly held that the wife’s mother remains prohibited if the wife dies or is divorced before consummation, calling her prohibition unrestricted.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أنه كان يقول إذا طلق الرجل امرأة قبل أن يدخل بها أو ماتت لم تحل (17) له أمها، أنه قال: إنها مبهمة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies the view that a wife’s mother is prohibited by contract as the position of the four imams, seven jurists, and the majority across generations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p250/r5.anchor: وهذا مذهب الأئمة الأربعة والفقهاء السبعة، وجمهور الفقهاء قديما وحديثا، ولله الحمد والمنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r1.claim: Although the cited Prophetic report has a problematic chain, Ibn Kathir says the established consensus makes separate authentication unnecessary.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r1.anchor: ثم قال: وهذا الخبر، وإن كان في إسناده ما فيه، فإن في إجماع الحجة على صحة القول به مستغنى عن الاستشهاد على صحته بغيره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r2.claim: The hadith also states that the Prophet’s stepdaughter was his niece through nursing, an additional bar to marriage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r2.anchor: إنها لو لم تكن ربيبتي في حجري ما حلت لي، إنها لبنت (9) أخي من الرضاعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r3.claim: The stepdaughter is prohibited whether or not she was raised in the husband’s home; ‘in your care’ describes what is usual and carries no restrictive implication, as at 24:33.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r3.anchor: فجمهور (5) الأئمة على أن الربيبة حرام سواء كانت في حجر الرجل أو لم تكن في حجره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r4.speaker: أم حبيبة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r4.claim: Umm Habiba asked the Prophet to marry her sister, and he answered that this was unlawful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r4.anchor: وفي الصحيحين أن أم حبيبة قالت: يا رسول الله، انكح أختي بنت أبي سفيان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Prophet’s ruling makes marriage to the mother the basis for the stepdaughter’s prohibition; the girl was also his milk-niece.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r5.anchor: فجعل المناط في التحريم مجرد تزويجه أم سلمة وحكم بالتحريم لذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r6.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r6.claim: A minority view says a stepdaughter is prohibited only if she was raised in the man’s household.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p251/r6.anchor: وقد قيل بأنه لا تحرم الربيبة إلا إذا كانت في حجر الرجل، فإذا لم يكن كذلك فلا تحرم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r1.claim: The chain supporting Ali’s view that a stepdaughter outside the husband’s household is lawful is strong by Muslim’s standard, though Ibn Kathir calls the view very unusual.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r1.anchor: هذا إسناد قوي ثابت إلى علي بن أبي طالب، على شرط مسلم، وهو قول غريب جدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r2.speaker: داود بن علي الظاهري وأصحابه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r2.claim: Daud al-Zahiri and his followers adopted Ali’s view; it was also attributed to Malik and chosen by Ibn Hazm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r2.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب داود بن علي الظاهري وأصحابه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r3.speaker: تقي الدين ابن تيمية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r3.claim: Ibn Taymiyya found Ali’s household-based reading problematic and suspended judgment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r3.anchor: وحكى لي شيخنا الحافظ أبو عبد الله الذهبي أنه عرض هذا على الشيخ الإمام تقي الدين ابن تيمية، رحمه الله، فاستشكله، وتوقف في ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses ‘in your care’ as ‘in your houses.’
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r4.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة قوله: {اللاتي في حجوركم} قال: في بيوتكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r5.claim: When asked about having sex with a female slave and her daughter, Umar said he disliked having relations with both.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r5.anchor: أن عمر بن الخطاب سئل عن المرأة وبنتها (3) من ملك اليمين توطأ إحداهما بعد الأخرى؟ فقال عمر: ما أحب أن أخبرهما جميعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas said one verse permits and another forbids intercourse with a female slave and her daughter, adding that he would not do it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r6.anchor: قلت لابن عباس: أيقع الرجل على امرأة وابنتها مملوكين (4) له؟ فقال: أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية، ولم (5) أكن لأفعله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r7.speaker: ابن عبد البر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r7.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says scholars agree that one may not have sex with a female slave and her daughter because slave relations follow marriage prohibitions; only reports from Umar and Ibn Abbas depart from this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r7.anchor: لا خلاف بين العلماء أنه لا يحل لأحد أن يطأ امرأة وابنتها (6) من ملك اليمين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r8.claim: Qatada and al-Hasan al-Basri say the stepdaughter’s daughter and descendants many generations below are also prohibited.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r8.anchor: عن قتادة: بنت الربيبة وبنت ابنتها لا تصلح وإن كانت أسفل ببطون كثيرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas and others explain ‘consummated with them’ as having sexual relations with the women.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r9.anchor: ومعنى قوله تعالى: {اللاتي دخلتم بهن} أي: نكحتموهن. قاله ابن عباس وغير واحد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r10.speaker: عطاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r10.claim: Ata defines consummation as bringing the woman to oneself, uncovering and inspecting her, and sitting between her legs; he says this suffices even at her family’s home.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p252/r10.anchor: وقال ابن جريج عن عطاء: هو أن تهدى إليه فيكشف ويفتش ويجلس بين رجليها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r1.claim: Ibn Jarir argues that ‘consummated with them’ means intercourse: seclusion alone does not prohibit the daughter if divorce precedes intercourse or passionate viewing of the private parts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r1.anchor: وقال ابن جرير: وفي إجماع الجميع على أن خلوة الرجل بامرأته لا يحرم (1) ابنتها عليه إذا طلقها قبل مسيسها ومباشرتها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r2.claim: The wives of biological sons are prohibited; specifying sons ‘from your loins’ excludes adopted sons from the pre-Islamic custom, linked to 33:37.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r2.anchor: أي: وحرمت عليكم زوجات أبنائكم الذين ولدتموهم من أصلابكم، يحترز بذلك عن الأدعياء الذين كانوا يتبنونهم في الجاهلية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r3.speaker: عطاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r3.claim: Ata reports that Meccans criticized the Prophet’s marriage to Zayd’s former wife, after which 4:23, 33:4, and 33:40 were revealed concerning adopted sons and the Prophet’s status.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r3.anchor: أن رسول الله (4) صلى الله عليه وسلم لما نكح امرأة زيد، قال (5) المشركون بمكة في ذلك، فأنزل الله [عز وجل] (6)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r4.speaker: الحسن بن محمد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r4.claim: Hasan ibn Muhammad calls the prohibitions of sons’ wives and wives’ mothers general, applying whether the marriage was consummated or not; Ibn Kathir says this is agreed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r4.anchor: عن الحسن بن محمد (8) أن هؤلاء الآيات مبهمات: {وحلائل أبنائكم} {أمهات نسائكم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r5.claim: A wife’s son by nursing is also prohibited because the Prophet said nursing forbids the same relations as lineage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253/r5.anchor: فالجواب من قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يحرم من الرضاع (11) ما يحرم من النسب"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r1.claim: The verse forbids simultaneously marrying two sisters or having them as concubines; pre-Islamic cases are forgiven.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r1.anchor: وحرم عليكم الجمع بين الأختين معا في التزويج، وكذا في ملك اليمين إلا ما كان منكم في جاهليتكم فقد عفونا عن ذلك وغفرناه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r2.claim: The past exception grants no future dispensation; as with 44:56, an exception can describe only what happened before.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r2.anchor: لا مثنوية فيما يستقبل ولا استثناء فيما (13) سلف

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r3.claim: Scholars from the Companions through later imams agree that marriage to two sisters at once is forbidden; a convert with two sister-wives must keep one and divorce the other.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r3.anchor: وقد أجمع العلماء من الصحابة والتابعين والأئمة قديما وحديثا على أنه يحرم الجمع بين الأختين في النكاح، ومن أسلم وتحته أختان خير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك بن فيروز
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r4.claim: Dhahhak ibn Fayruz reported that he entered Islam with two sisters as wives and the Prophet ordered him to divorce one; al-Tirmidhi's version says to choose either and he grades the report hasan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي وهب الجيشاني عن الضحاك بن فيروز، عن أبيه قال: أسلمت وعندي امرأتان أختان، فأمرني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن أطلق إحداهما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r5.speaker: أبو خراش الرعيني
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r5.claim: A second report says a man who had married two sisters before Islam was told to divorce one on returning home; Ibn Kathir says Abu Khirash may be Dhahhak or another narrator.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي خراش الرعيني (4) قال: قدمت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وعندي أختان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r6.speaker: الديلمي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r6.claim: A report attributed to al-Daylami says that, while he had two sisters as wives, the Prophet told him to divorce whichever one he wished.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p253#2/r6.anchor: عن كثير بن مرة، عن الديلمي قال: قلت: يا رسول الله، إن تحتي أختين؟ قال: "طلق أيهما شئت"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir identifies the first Dailami in the reports as Dhahhak ibn Fayruz; Abu Zur'a says he accompanied Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r1.anchor: فالديلمي المذكور أولا هو الضحاك بن فيروز الديلمي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r2.claim: The other Dailami is Abu Fayruz, one of the Yemeni commanders who took part in killing the false prophet al-Aswad al-Ansi.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r2.anchor: والثاني هو أبو فيروز الديلمي، رضي الله عنه، وكان من جملة الأمراء باليمن الذين ولوا قتل الأسود العنسي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r3.claim: The general wording also forbids combining two sisters in ownership for sexual relations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r3.anchor: وأما الجمع بين الأختين في ملك اليمين فحرام أيضا لعموم الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r4.claim: Ibn Mas'ud disapproved of a man combining two sisters and rejected the appeal to the exception for those owned by the right hand, noting that a camel is also so owned.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r4.anchor: فقال له ابن مسعود: وبعيرك مما ملكت يمينك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r5.speaker: الجمهور والأئمة الأربعة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r5.claim: The majority, including the four imams, forbid combining enslaved sisters; some early authorities reserved judgment, but Ibn Kathir presents the majority as the well-known position.
