IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r5.anchor: وهذا هو المشهور عن الجمهور والأئمة الأربعة وغيرهم، وإن كان بعض السلف قد توقف في ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r6.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r6.claim: Asked whether two enslaved sisters may be combined, Uthman said one verse permits them and another forbids them, and he would not do it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r6.anchor: فقال عثمان: أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية، وما كنت لأصنع ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r7.claim: A Companion, whom Ibn Shihab identifies as probably Ali and whom Ibn Kathir says Abu Umar understood to be Ali, threatened exemplary punishment for anyone who did this; a similar view is reported from al-Zubayr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r7.anchor: فقال: لو كان لي من الأمر شيء ثم وجدت أحدا فعل ذلك لجعلته نكالا. قال مالك: قال ابن شهاب: أراه علي بن أبي طالب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r8.speaker: أبو عمر بن عبد البر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r8.claim: Abu Umar explains that Qabisa concealed Ali's name because people under Abd al-Malik found mentioning Ali burdensome.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r8.anchor: إنما كنى قبيصة بن ذؤيب عن علي بن أبي طالب، لصحبته عبد الملك بن مروان، وكانوا يستثقلون ذكر علي بن أبي طالب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r9.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r9.claim: Ali advised freeing the concubine a man had been having intercourse with before he had intercourse with his other enslaved sister; freeing her avoids the risk that a later divorce or death returns her to the owner.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r9.anchor: فقال علي، رضي الله عنه: تعتق التي كنت تطأ ثم تطأ الأخرى. قلت: فإن ناسا يقولون: بل تزوجها ثم تطأ الأخرى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r10.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r10.claim: Ali says sexual prohibitions for owned women follow those for free women, except the numerical limit, and that nursing relations carry the same prohibitions as lineage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p254/r10.anchor: إنه يحرم عليك ما ملكت يمينك ما يحرم عليك في كتاب الله عز وجل من الحرائر إلا العدد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r1.claim: Ali described the two-sisters rule as a case where one verse forbids and another permits; Ibn Abbas then explained that kinship to a man, not kinship between enslaved women, prohibits them to him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال لي علي بن أبي طالب: حرمتهما آية وأحلتهما آية -يعني الأختين-قال ابن عباس:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says kinship to the man bars the women to him, not on the basis of relationship between enslaved women; he adds that pre-Islamic people observed these prohibitions except for a father's wife and combining sisters, which the revelation prohibits in marriage.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يحرمهن علي قرابتي منهن، ولا يحرمهن على قرابة بعضهن من بعض -يعني الإماء-وكانت الجاهلية يحرمون ما تحرمون إلا امرأة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r3.claim: Ibn Mas'ud, with similar views from Ibn Sirin and al-Sha'bi, held that the prohibitions for enslaved women match those for free women except for the limit on number.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: يحرم من الإماء ما يحرم من الحرائر إلا العدد. وعن ابن سيرين والشعبي مثل ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r4.claim: Abu Umar says a view like Uthman's was also transmitted from Ibn Abbas, though reports attributed to Ibn Abbas differ.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r4.anchor: وقد روي مثل قول عثمان عن طائفة من السلف، منهم: ابن عباس، ولكنهم اختلف عليهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r5.speaker: جمهور الفقهاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r5.claim: Jurists across the regions reject combining enslaved sisters in intercourse; Ibn Kathir says only an outlier literalist position that rejects analogy departed from their consensus.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r5.anchor: وجماعة الفقهاء متفقون على أنه لا يحل الجمع بين الأختين بملك اليمين في الوطء، كما لا يحل ذلك في النكاح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r6.claim: Muslims agree that the listed prohibitions apply to marriage and ownership alike; by analogy the same rule bars combining sisters, mothers-in-law, and stepdaughters through ownership, as most jurists hold.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p255/r6.anchor: أن النكاح وملك (6) اليمين في هؤلاء كلهن سواء، فكذلك يجب أن يكون نظرا وقياسا الجمع بين الأختين وأمهات النساء والربائب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p258/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p258/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p258/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir says this verse was cited by those arguing that combining two sisters is lawful because one verse permits it while another forbids it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p258/r9.anchor: وهذه الآية هي (5) التي احتج بها من احتج على تحليل الجمع بين الأختين، وقول من قال: أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية (6)

NAHHAS:v1p444/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p444/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p444/r5.claim: أمهات is a plural of أمهة; أم and أمهة mean the same, and the Qurʾān uses both forms.
NAHHAS:v1p444/r5.anchor: جمع أمهة يقال أم وأمهة بمعنى واحد وجاء القرآن بهما

NAHHAS:v1p444/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p444/r6.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v1p444/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd says أمهاتكم is the passive subject because with its verb it forms a clause like a subject, and the verb cannot dispense with it.
NAHHAS:v1p444/r6.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد لأنه مع الفعل جملة كالفاعل ولا يستغني عنه الفعل

NAHHAS:v1p444/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p444/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p444/r7.claim: بناتكم is coordinated; بنات is from بنية, while ابنة and بنت are the forms in use.
NAHHAS:v1p444/r7.anchor: ( وبناتكم ) عطف جمع بنة والأصل بنية والمستعمل ابنة وبنت

NAHHAS:v1p444/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p444/r8.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p444/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the kasra in بنت as marking the deletion of the yāʾ.
NAHHAS:v1p444/r8.anchor: قال الفراء كسرت الباء من بنت لتدل الكسرة على حذف الياء

NAHHAS:v1p444/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p444/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p444/r9.claim: أخواتكم is a coordinated plural of أخوة; عماتكم is likewise coordinated through the list.
NAHHAS:v1p444/r9.anchor: ( وأخواتكم ) عطف جمع أخوة ( وعماتكم ) عطف عليه

NAHHAS:v1p444/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p444/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p444/r10.claim: أن تجمعوا is nominative: the prohibited act is combining two sisters.
NAHHAS:v1p444/r10.anchor: ( وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين ) أن في موضع رفع أي وحرم عليكم الجمع بين الأختين

NAHHAS:v1p444/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p444/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p444/r11.claim: إلا ما قد سلف is an exception that does not come from the preceding category.
NAHHAS:v1p444/r11.anchor: ( إلا ما قد سلف ) استثناء ليس من الأول

JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r1.claim: The common reading has اللاتي with tāʾ; Ibn Masud reads اللائي without tāʾ, as in Qur'an 65:4.
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r1.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود: اللائي أرضعنكم: بغير تاء كقوله:

JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r2.claim: أمهات is a plural of أم; one derivation has an original hāʾ that disappears in the singular and returns in the plural, while another gives أمه as the root and أمات as its plural.
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r2.anchor: الأمهات: جمع أم، والأم في الأصل أمهة على وزن فعلة

JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r3.claim: A poet's line preserves the hāʾ in أمهتي, supporting the proposed original form.
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر: أمهتي خندف وإلياس أبي

JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r4.claim: A rabība is a man's stepdaughter, called that because he raises her; the word has the sense of the passive مربوبة.
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r4.anchor: والربيبة: بنت امرأة الرجل من غيره وقيل لها ربيبة

JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r5.claim: A ḥalīla is a son's wife; one derivation says spouses are mutually lawful for intercourse, with حليل formed like صحيح.
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r5.anchor: والحلائل: أزواج الابن، والذكر حليل، وجمعه أحلة كأعزة وأعزاء

JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r6.claim: Another derivation says spouses are called ḥalīl and ḥalīla because they share a bed, from the sense of dwelling or lodging.
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: لأنها يحل معها في فراش من الحلول، وهو النزول

JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r7.claim: The phrase وأن تجمعوا is nominative by estimation: it is forbidden to combine the two sisters; ما is an accusative exception for what occurred before the prohibition.
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r7.anchor: وأن تجمعوا محله رفع على تقدير: وحرم الجمع إلا ما قد سلف. قوله: ما في محل النصب

JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r8.claim: The first اللاتي is nominative as an adjective of ربائبكم, and the second is genitive as an adjective of النساء.
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r8.anchor: اللاتي محله رفع نعتا لربائبكم، واللاتي الثاني محله خفض نعتا للنساء

JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r9.speaker: عطاء
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r9.claim: Ata says the rule on sons' wives was revealed when the Prophet married Zayd b. Haritha's former wife; the polytheists criticized him, and Qur'an 33:4 and 33:40 also came down.
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r9.anchor: قال عطاء: نزل قوله: وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم

JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r10.claim: The revelation account also links this passage to the declaration that adopted sons are not biological sons and Muhammad is not the father of any adult man.
JISHUMI:v2p1507#2/r10.anchor: ونزل: (وما جعل أدعياءكم أبناءكم) و(ما كان محمد أبا أحد من رجالكم)

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r1.claim: The prohibition means that marriage to these women is forbidden, as shown by the explicit marriage prohibition in 4:22 and by ordinary uses of prohibiting wine or pork to mean forbidding their consumption.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r1.anchor: ولأن تحريم نكاحهن هو الذي يفهم من تحريمهن كما يفهم من تحريم الخمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r2.claim: A reading lightens the hamza in بنات الأخت.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r3.claim: God makes nursing relationships equivalent to lineage: the wet nurse is mother, the nursing sister is a sister, and the wet nurse's husband and their relatives establish corresponding paternal and maternal relations.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r3.anchor: وقد نزل الله الرضاعة منزلة النسب حتى سمى المرضعة أما للرضيع والمراضعة أختا وكذلك زوج المرضعة أبوه وأبواه جداه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r4.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says that nursing prohibits the same relationships that lineage prohibits.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r4.anchor: ومنه قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم 265 ( يحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم من النسب )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r5.claim: Two differences remain: a man may marry his foster son's sister because the lineage prohibition comes from intercourse with her mother, absent in nursing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r5.anchor: إلا في مسألتين إحداهما أنه لا يجوز للرجل أن يتزوج أخت ابنه من النسب ويجوز أن يتزوج أخت ابنه من الرضاع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r6.claim: A man may marry his foster brother's mother because the lineage prohibition comes from the father having intercourse with her, a cause absent in nursing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p525#2/r6.anchor: والثانية لا يجوز أن يتزوج أم أخيه من النسب ويجوز في الرضاع لأن المانع في النسب وطء الأب إياها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r1.claim: The phrase ‘from your women’ modifies stepdaughters: a stepdaughter whose mother the man has entered is forbidden, while one whose mother he has not entered is lawful.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r1.anchor: متعلق بربائبكم ومعناه أن الربيبة من المرأة المدخول بها محرمة على الرجل حلال له اذا لم يدخل بها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r2.claim: Attaching ‘from your women’ to both mothers-in-law and stepdaughters would make ‘from’ mean specification for the former but derivation for the latter, an impermissible shift within one expression.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r2.anchor: فقد جعلت ( من ) لبيان النساء وتمييز المدخول بهن من غير المدخول بهن واذا قلت وربائبكم من نسائكم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r3.claim: Attaching the phrase only to mothers-in-law would leave the stepdaughter restriction ambiguous; the nearer phrase normally governs unless an obstacle intervenes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r3.anchor: ولا يجوز الثاني لأن ما يليه هو الذي يستوجب التعليق به ما لم يعترض أمر لا يرد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r4.claim: A possible alternative is to attach it to both women and stepdaughters, taking ‘from’ to express connection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526/r4.anchor: الا ان تقول اعلقه بالنساء والربائب وأجعل ( من ) للاتصال كقوله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r1.claim: The sense of connection is illustrated by ‘the hypocrite men and women are of one another’; mothers-in-law connect to wives as mothers, and stepdaughters to their mothers as daughters.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض ﴾ التوبة 67 فإني لست منك ولست مني ما انا من دد ولا الدد مني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r2.claim: Scholars agree that the prohibition of mothers-in-law is unconditional, unlike the stepdaughter prohibition, following the apparent wording of the verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r2.anchor: اتفقوا على أن تحريم امهات النساء مبهم دون تحريم الربائب على ما عليه ظاهر كلام الله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r3.claim: A report says a man who divorced his wife before consummation may marry her daughter but may not marry her mother.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r3.anchor: وقد روى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في رجل تزوج امراة ثم طلقها قبل ان يدخل بها انه قال ( لا بأس ان يتزوج ابنتها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r4.speaker: عمر وعمران بن الحصين
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r4.claim: They held that a mother-in-law becomes forbidden as soon as the marriage contract is made.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r4.anchor: وعن عمر وعمران بن الحصين رضي الله عنهما ان الأم تحرم بنفس العقد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r5.speaker: مسروق
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r5.claim: Masruq said the mother-in-law prohibition is unrestricted, so people should leave unrestricted what God left unrestricted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r5.anchor: وعن مسروق هي مرسلة فأرسلوا ما أرسل الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise urged leaving ambiguous what God left ambiguous.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أبهموا ما أبهم الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r7.speaker: علي وابن عباس وزيد وابن عمر وابن الزبير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r7.claim: These authorities are reported to have read ‘and your wives’ mothers who have entered them’; Ibn Abbas swore that this was the revealed wording.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r7.anchor: الا ما روي عن علي وابن عباس وزيد وابن عمر وابن الزبير انهم قرءوا ( وأمهات نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r8.speaker: جابر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r8.claim: Two different reports are transmitted from Jabir on this question.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r8.anchor: وعن جابر روايتان وعن سعيد بن المسيب عن زيد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r9.speaker: زيد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r9.claim: Zayd, transmitted by Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, disliked a man marrying his deceased wife’s mother if he inherited from her; divorce before consummation left the choice open, since death substitutes for consummation here as it does for dowry.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r9.anchor: وعن سعيد بن المسيب عن زيد اذا ماتت عنده فأخذ ميراثها كره ان يخلف على امها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r10.claim: A wife’s child by another man is called rabīb/rabība because a stepfather generally raises the child as he raises his own; the term later broadened to children he did not raise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r10.anchor: وسمى ولد المرأة من غير زوجها ربيبا وربيبة لأنه يربهما كما يرب ولده في غالب الأمر ثم اتسع فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r11.claim: ‘In your care’ explains the prohibition: after consummation, marriage creates intimacy and affection that ordinarily lead a man to treat his wife’s children as his own.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r11.anchor: فائدته التعليل للتحريم وانهن لاحتضانكم لهن أو لكونهن بصدد احتضانكم وفي حكم التقلب في حجوركم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r12.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r12.claim: Ali required a stepdaughter to be in the man’s care for the prohibition to apply; Dawud adopted this view.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p526#2/r12.anchor: وعن على رضي الله عنه انه شرط ذلك في التحريم وبه اخذ داود

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r1.claim: ‘Entered upon them’ is a euphemism for intercourse, like saying that a man built over a woman or drew the curtain over her.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r1.anchor: ﴿ دخلتم بهن ﴾ قلت هي كناية عن الجماع كقولهم بني عليها وضرب عليها الحجاب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r2.claim: The preposition is causative; Abu Hanifa treats touching and similar contact as taking the place of consummation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r2.anchor: والباء للتعدية واللمس ونحوه يقوم مقام الدخول عند أبي حنيفة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r3.speaker: عمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r3.claim: Umar ruled that a son could not marry a slave girl after Umar had secluded himself with her and stripped her, when the son asked for her.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r3.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه خلا بجارية فجردها فاستوهبها ابن له فقال إنها لا تحل لك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r4.speaker: مسروق
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r4.claim: Masruq ordered his slave girl sold after his death, saying he had touched and looked at her in ways that made her forbidden to his son.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r4.anchor: وعن مسروق أنه امر ان تباع جاريته بعد موته وقال اما إني لم اصب منها الا ما يحرمها على ولدي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r5.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r5.claim: Hasan held that a man’s lustful squeezing, kissing, or uncovering of a slave woman makes her forbidden to his son in every case.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r5.anchor: وعن الحسن في الرجل يملك الأمة فيغمزها لشهوة أو يقبلها أو يكشفها أنها لا تحل لولده بحال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r6.speaker: عطاء وحماد بن أبي سليمان
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r6.claim: ʿAta and Hammad held that looking at a woman’s genitals prevents a man from marrying either her mother or daughter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r6.anchor: وعن عطاء وحماد بن أبي سليمان اذا نظر إلى فرج امرأة فلا ينكح امها ولا بنتها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r7.speaker: الأوزاعي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r7.claim: Al-Awzaʿi held that entering the mother’s room, exposing her, touching her, closing the door, and lowering the curtain forbids marrying her daughter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r7.anchor: وعن الأوزاعي اذا دخل بالأم فعراها ولمسها بيده وأغلق الباب وأرخى الستر فلا يحل له نكاح ابنتها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وطاوس وعمرو بن دينار
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, Tawus, and Amr ibn Dinar held that the prohibition arises only from intercourse itself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عباس وطاوس وعمرو بن دينار ان التحريم لا يقع الا بالجماع وحده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r1.claim: ‘Of your loins’ excludes adopted sons; the Prophet married Zaynab bint Jahsh after Zayd ibn Haritha divorced her, as anticipated by the rule about adopted sons’ wives.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r1.anchor: وقد تزوج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زينب بنت جحش الاسدية بنت عمته أميمة بنت عبد المطلب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r2.claim: ‘And that you combine’ is nominative, coordinated with the prohibited women, and prohibits combining two sisters in marriage.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r2.anchor: في موضع الرفع عطف على المحرمات أي وحرم عليكم الجمع بين الأختين والمراد حرمة النكاح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r3.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r3.claim: Ali treated the prohibition of combining two sisters as applying to two women owned as slaves, since one verse permits them and another forbids them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r3.anchor: فعن عثمان وعلي رضي الله عنهما أنهما قالا أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية يعنيان هذه الآية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r4.speaker: عثمان
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r4.claim: Uthman resolved the conflict between the prohibition and the permission for two owned sisters in favor of permissibility.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r4.anchor: يعنيان هذه الآية وقوله ﴿ أو ما ملكت أيمانكم ﴾ النساء 3 فرجح على التحريم وعثمان التحليل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r5.claim: The exception for what preceded means past conduct is forgiven, as confirmed by the following statement that God is forgiving and merciful.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p528#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ إلا ما قد سلف ﴾ ولكن ما مضى مغفور بدليل قوله

MUQATIL:4:23/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:23/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:23/r1.claim: The listed mothers, daughters, sisters, aunts, and nieces are forbidden through blood relationship.
MUQATIL:4:23/r1.anchor: وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت } ، فهذا النسب

MUQATIL:4:23/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:23/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:23/r2.claim: Foster mothers and sisters, mothers-in-law, and stepdaughters of wives with whom the man has consummated marriage are forbidden.
MUQATIL:4:23/r2.anchor: وأمهاتكم اللاتي أرضعنكم وأخواتكم من الرضاعة وأمهات نسآئكم وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم

MUQATIL:4:23/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:23/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:23/r3.claim: If he has not consummated marriage with their mothers, there is no sin in marrying the daughters.
MUQATIL:4:23/r3.anchor: فلا جناح عليكم } ، يقول: فلا حرج عليكم فى تزوج البنات

MUQATIL:4:23/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:23/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:23/r4.claim: A son's wife is forbidden when the son is the man's biological child, born from his loins rather than adopted; this is affinity.
MUQATIL:4:23/r4.anchor: وحرم ما تزوج الابن الذى خرج من صلب الرجل ولم يتبناه، فهذا الصهر

MUQATIL:4:23/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:23/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:23/r5.claim: Combining two sisters is forbidden, except when one is held in ownership and he marries her to someone else.
MUQATIL:4:23/r5.anchor: فحرم جمعهما، إلا أن يكون إحداهما بملك، فزوجها غيره، فلا بأس

MUQATIL:4:23/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:4:23/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:4:23/r6.claim: The exception for past conduct means God forgives intercourse with two sisters before the prohibition.
MUQATIL:4:23/r6.anchor: إلا ما قد سلف } قبل التحريم، { إن الله كان غفورا رحيما } [آية: 23] لما كان من جماع الأختين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r1.claim: After permitting suitable marriages and mentioning wives of fathers, the passage lists the remaining forbidden women: seven through blood relation and seven through marriage or other affinity.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر فى أول السورة نكاح ما طاب أى حل من النساء وذكر بعض ما حرم قبل هذا وهو نساء الآباء ذكر المحرمات الباقيات وهن سبع من النسب وسبع من السبب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r2.claim: Some take the prohibition of mothers to mean specifically that marrying them is forbidden; Nasafi refers to his preferred analysis in Sharḥ al-Manār.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r2.anchor: والمراد تحريم نكاحهن عند البعض وقد ذكرنا المختار فى شرح المنار

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r3.claim: Grandmothers through either parent are included among mothers, and granddaughters through sons or daughters are included among daughters.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r3.anchor: ﴿ وبناتكم ﴾ وبنات الابن وبنات البنت ملحقات بهن

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r4.claim: When plural groups are paired, the members distribute individually: each person is forbidden their own mother and daughter.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r4.anchor: والأصل أن الجمع إذا قوبل بالجمع ينقسم الآحاد على الآحاد فتحرم على كل واحد أمه وبنته

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r5.claim: Sisters include full, paternal, and maternal sisters; aunts and nieces likewise include all three relevant lines of descent.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r5.anchor: ﴿ وإخوانكم ﴾ لأب و أم أو لأب أو لأم ﴿ وعماتكم ﴾ من الأوجه الثلاثة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r6.claim: God makes nursing relations equivalent to blood relations: the nurse is a mother, her co-nursing daughters are sisters, her husband and his parents are father and grandparents, his sister is an aunt, and his other children are paternal siblings; the nurse's own mother, sister, and children by another man create grandmother and maternal-sibling relations.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r6.anchor: ﴿ وأمهاتكم اللاتي أرضعنكم وأخواتكم من الرضاعة ﴾ الله تعالى نزل الرضاعة منزلة النسب فسمى المرضعة أما للرضيع

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r7.claim: A Prophetic report states that nursing forbids the same relations that blood kinship forbids.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r7.anchor: وأصله قوله عليه السلام يحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم من النسب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r8.claim: Mothers of one's wives become forbidden as soon as the marriage contract is made.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r8.anchor: ﴿ وأمهات نسائكم ﴾ وهن محرمات بمجرد العقد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r9.claim: A wife's child from another man is called a stepchild because the husband usually raises the child; the term extends even where he did not raise the child.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r9.anchor: ﴿ وربائبكم ﴾ سمى ولد المرأة من غير زوجها ربيبا وربيبة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r10.speaker: داود
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r10.claim: Dāwūd holds that a stepdaughter is forbidden only if she was in the husband's household.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r10.anchor: قال داود إذا لم تكن فى حجره لا تحرم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r11.claim: Nasafi rejects household custody as a condition: the phrase describes the usual situation and gives the reason, since the stepdaughters are cared for as one's own daughters would be.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r11.anchor: قلنا ذكر الحجر على غلبة الحال دون الشرط وفائدته التعليل للتحريم وانهن لاحتضانكم لهن أو لكونهن بصدد احتضانكم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r12.claim: A stepdaughter from a wife with whom the man has had intercourse is forbidden; without intercourse, he may marry her after separating from the mother. Dukhūl euphemizes intercourse, and touching or similar contact can stand in its place.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r12.anchor: ﴿ من نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن ﴾ متعلق بربائبكم أى الربيبة من المرأة المدخول بها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r13.claim: Nasafi rejects making the phrase about women with whom one has had intercourse an adjective for both nearby groups: their different governing constructions prevent one adjective from modifying both.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r13.anchor: وقد جعل بعض العلماء اللاى دخلتم بهن وصفا للنساء المتقدمة والمتاخرة وليس كذلك لأن الوصف الواحد لا يقع على موصوفين مختلفى العامل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r14.claim: The syntax is clearer than al-Zajjāj's and al-Kashshāf author's proposed attachment, as one adjective cannot modify nouns governed differently.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r14.anchor: وهذا لأن النساء الاولى مجرورة بالإضافة والثانية بمن ولا يجوز أن تقول مررت بنسائك وهربت من نساء زيد الظريفات

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r15.claim: A son's wife is forbidden when he is a biological son, not an adopted son; the Prophet's marriage to Zaynab after Zayd and the stated purpose of removing hardship demonstrate this. Nursing son's wives remain forbidden.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r15.anchor: ﴿ الذين من أصلابكم ﴾ دون من تبنيتم فقد تزوج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم زينب حين فارقها زيد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r16.claim: Combining two sisters means having both in one marriage; the phrase is grammatically coordinated with the list of forbidden women.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r16.anchor: ﴿ وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين ﴾ أي في النكاح وهو في موضع الرفع عطف على المحرمات

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r17.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r17.claim: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan says pre-Islamic Arabs knew the other forbidden relations, but not the bans on marrying one's father's wife and marrying two sisters, which explains the exception for past conduct.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r17.anchor: وعن محمد بن الحسن رحمه الله إن أهل الجاهلية كانوا يعرفون هذه المحرمات إلا نكاح امرأة الأب ونكاح الأختين فلذا قال فيهما إلا ما قد سلف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r18.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r18.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r18.claim: The verse closes by saying God is forgiving and merciful toward what has passed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p214/r18.anchor: ﴿ إلا ما قد سلف ﴾ ولكن ما مضى مغفور بدليل قوله ﴿ إن الله كان غفورا رحيما ﴾

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r1.claim: The verse means that marriage to the listed women is forbidden; it enumerates lawful and forbidden women, with seven prohibited by lineage and seven by affinity or nursing when the related texts are counted.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r1.anchor: أي نكاح أمهاتكم ونكاح بناتكم فذكر الله تعالى في هذه الآية ما يحل من النساء وما يحرم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r2.speaker: السنة المتواترة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r2.claim: The mass-transmitted Sunna adds a prohibition against marrying a woman together with her aunt, a rule Qurtubi says is established by consensus.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r2.anchor: وألحقت السنة المتواترة سابعة وذلك الجمع بين المرأة وعمتها، ونص عليه الإجماع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r3.speaker: ابن عابس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbis counts seven forbidden by lineage and seven by affinity and recites this verse as evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r3.anchor: وثبتت الرواية عن ابن عابس قال: حرم من النسب سبع ومن الصهر سبع، وتلا هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r4.speaker: عمرو بن سالم مولى الأنصار
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r4.claim: Amr ibn Salim agrees with the seven-and-seven count but identifies the seventh as the women described as muḥṣanāt.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r4.anchor: وقال عمرو بن سالم مولى الأنصار مثل ذلك، وقال: السابعة قوله تعالى: { والمحصنات }

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r5.claim: The lineage list is mothers, daughters, sisters, paternal and maternal aunts, and nieces; the affinity and nursing list includes milk kin, wives’ mothers, stepdaughters, sons’ wives, sisters together, and fathers’ wives.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r5.anchor: فالسبع المحرمات من النسب: الأمهات والبنات والأخوات والعمات والخالات، وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r6.speaker: جمهور السلف
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r6.claim: Most early authorities hold that a wife’s mother becomes forbidden upon the marriage contract, while her daughter is forbidden only after consummation.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r6.anchor: فإن جمهور السلف ذهبوا إلى أن الأم تحرم بالعقد على الابنة، ولا تحرم الابنة إلا بالدخول بالأم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r7.speaker: طائفة من السلف
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r7.claim: A group of early authorities treats the wife’s mother and daughter alike: neither is forbidden until the man consummates the marriage with the other.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r7.anchor: وقالت طائفة من السلف: الأم والربيبة سواء، لا تحرم منهما واحدة إلا بالدخول بالأخرى

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r8.speaker: خلاس عن علي بن أبي طالب; ابن عباس وجابر وزيد بن ثابت; ابن الزبير ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r8.claim: The alternative reading that the consummation condition applies to both mothers and stepdaughters is transmitted from Ali, Ibn ʿAbbas, Jabir, Zayd, Ibn al-Zubayr, and Mujahid.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r8.anchor: رواه خلاس عن علي بن أبي طالب. وروي عن ابن عباس وجابر وزيد بن ثابت، وهو قول ابن الزبير ومجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r9.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r9.claim: Mujahid explicitly says consummation is intended in both cases mentioned by the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r9.anchor: قال مجاهد: الدخول مراد في النازلتين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r10.claim: Qurtubi sides with the majority position as the operative legal ruling and fatwa; he and al-Shafiʿi require a valid marriage, since illicit sex does not make lawful relations forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r10.anchor: وقول الجمهور مخالف لهذا وعليه الحكم والفتيا، وقد شدد أهل العراق فيه حتى قالوا: لو وطئها بزنى أو قبلها أو لمسها بشهوة حرمت عليه ابنتها. وعندنا وعند الشافعي إنما تحرم بالنكاح الصحيح والحرام لا يحرم الحلال

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r11.claim: Qurtubi rejects the report of Khilas from Ali as insufficient proof and says the sound report from Ali matches the majority.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r11.anchor: وحديث خلاس عن علي لا تقوم به حجة، ولا تصح روايته عند أهل العلم بالحديث، والصحيح عنه مثل قول الجماعة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r12.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r12.claim: Aṭaʾ tells Ibn Jurayj that a man who contracts marriage and then divorces or is widowed without seeing or having intercourse with the wife still may not marry her mother.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r12.anchor: قلت لعطاء الرجل ينكح المرأة ثم لا يراها ولا يجامعها حتى يطلقها أو تحل له أمها؟ قال: لا، هي مرسلة دخل بها أو لم يدخل

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r13.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r13.claim: Zayd says a wife’s mother is unqualified and prohibited by the contract; only the stepdaughter clause carries a consummation condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r13.anchor: فقال زيد لا، الأم مبهمة ليس فيها شرط وإنما الشرط في الربائب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r14.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r14.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir calls the majority view correct because the verse includes all wives’ mothers without qualification.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23/r14.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وهذا هو الصحيح لدخول جميع أمهات النساء في قوله تعالى: { وأمهات نسآئكم }

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r1.claim: The grammar supports separating the clauses: when two predicates have different governing words, one adjective cannot qualify both, so al-lātī cannot modify both groups together.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r1.anchor: ويؤيد هذا القول من جهة الإعراب أن الخبرين إذا اختلفا في العامل لم يكن نعتهما واحدا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r2.claim: Al-Khalil and Sibawayh cite a poetic example where khuwairibīn is an explanatory insertion meaning “I mean,” showing how the construction can work.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r2.anchor: وأنشد الخليل وسيبويه: إن بها أكتل أو رزاما خويربين ينقفان الهاما

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r3.claim: A Prophetic report states that a wife’s mother is forbidden as soon as the man marries the daughter, while the daughter is lawful if he marries the mother and divorces her before consummation; Qurtubi says it is in both Sahih collections.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r3.anchor: وقد جاء صريحا من حديث عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r4.claim: Prohibition is not an attribute of people or objects and does not inhere in them; legal commands concern acts, while the persons are named figuratively as the locus of those acts.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r4.anchor: أن التحريم ليس صفة للأعيان، والأعيان ليست موردا للتحليل والتحريم ولا مصدرا، وإنما يتعلق التكليف بالأمر والنهي بأفعال المكلفين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r5.claim: The word mothers gives an unrestricted prohibition in every case; scholars call it mubham because the prohibition has no route or exception, and the same applies to the other listed close relatives.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r5.anchor: تحريم الأمهات عام في كل حال لا يتخصص بوجه من الوجوه ولهذا يسميه أهل العلم المبهم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r6.claim: The singular forms umm and ummah mean the same, and the Qur’an uses both; Qurtubi says the word’s earlier discussion is in al-Fatiha.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r6.anchor: والأمهات جمع أمهة يقال: أم وأمهة بمعنى واحد، وجاء القرآن بهما. وقد تقدم في الفاتحة بيانه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r7.claim: One etymology derives umm from ummah on the pattern of qubbarah and ḥamrah, with the h restored in the plural; a poet uses the form ummahatī.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن أصل أم أمهة على وزن فعلة مثل قبرة وحمرة لطيرين، فسقطت وعادت في الجمع. قال الشاعر: أمهتي خندف والدوس أبي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#2/r8.claim: Another view derives umm from ummah; its plural is ummāt, as al-Rāʿī’s line about the she-camels of Mundhir and Muḥarriq illustrates.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r1.claim: Mother includes every female who bore the person, including his mother and all ascending grandmothers through either parent.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r1.anchor: فالأم اسم لكل أنثى لها عليك ولادة فيدخل في ذلك الأم دنية، وأمهاتها وجداتها وأم الأب وجداته وإن علون

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r2.claim: Daughter includes every female descended from the person by birth, directly or through later generations, including daughters of sons.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r2.anchor: والبنت اسم لكل أنثى لك عليها ولادة، وإن شئت قلت: كل أنثى يرجع نسبها إليك بالولادة بدرجة أو درجات

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r3.claim: Sister means a female who shares both parents or either one of them with you.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r3.anchor: والأخت اسم لكل أنثى جاورتك في أصليك أو في أحدهما

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r4.claim: Bint is the plural of bint, whose origin is bunayya; the common forms are ibnah and bint, and al-Farrāʾ explains the kasra and the deleted wāw in ukht.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r4.anchor: والبنات جمع بنت، والأصل بنية، والمستعمل ابنة وبنت. قال الفراء: كسرت الباء من بنت لتدل الكسرة على الياء، وضمت الألف من أخت لتدل على حذف الواو

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r5.claim: A paternal aunt is a female sibling of one’s father or grandfather, including the sister of one’s maternal grandfather; a maternal aunt is a female sibling of one’s mother, including the sister of one’s paternal grandmother.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r5.anchor: والعمة اسم لكل أنثى شاركت أباك أو جدك في أصليه أو في أحدهما

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r6.claim: A niece is every female born to one’s brother or sister, directly or through an intermediary.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r6.anchor: وبنت الأخ اسم لكل أنثى لأخيك عليها ولادة بواسطة أو مباشرة وكذلك بنت الأخت

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r7.claim: In the transmission of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Uways, Nāfiʿ reads the khāʾ in al-akh with gemination when the word has the article, transferring the vowel.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r7.anchor: وقرأ نافع في رواية أبي بكر بن أبي أويس بتشديد الخاء من الأخ إذا كانت فيه الألف واللام مع نقل الحركة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r8.claim: The Prophet’s rule is that nursing makes prohibited the same relations that lineage makes prohibited.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r8.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r9.speaker: عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r9.claim: ʿAbd Allah reads allātī as al-lāʾī without the tāʾ, matching the form used in 65:4.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r9.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله «وأمهاتكم اللائي» بغير تاء كقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r10.claim: A poet also uses the plural lāʾī in a line describing those who seek a reward but instead kill an innocent man.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#3/r10.anchor: قال الشاعر: من اللاء لم يحججن يبغين حسبة ولكن ليقتلن البريء المغفلا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r1.claim: A woman who nurses a child becomes his mother; her daughter is his sister, her sister his maternal aunt, her mother his grandmother, and her husband’s daughter and sister are his sister and paternal aunt, with the husband’s mother his grandmother and their descendants also prohibited kin.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r1.anchor: فإذا أرضعت المرأة طفلا حرمت عليه لأنها أمه، وبنتها لأنها أخته، وأختها لأنها خالته، وأمها لأنها جدته

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r2.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r2.claim: Malik permits a woman to perform pilgrimage with her milk brother.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r2.anchor: سئل مالك عن المرأة أيحج معها أخوها من الرضاعة؟ قال: نعم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r3.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r3.claim: When a woman claimed she had nursed a married couple, Malik ordered them separated; she keeps what she already received and owes nothing further, citing the Prophet’s ruling in a similar case despite the claimant’s weakness.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r3.anchor: وسئل مالك عن امرأة تزوجت فدخل بها زوجها، ثم جاءت امرأة فزعمت أنها أرضعتهما قال: يفرق بينهما

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r4.claim: In the similar case, the Prophet answered the objection about the woman’s weakness by asking whether people say that a man married his sister.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r4.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r5.claim: Nursing creates marriage prohibition only when it occurs within the first two years, and Qurtubi discusses the rule earlier in al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r5.anchor: التحريم بالرضاع إنما يحصل إذا اتفق الإرضاع في الحولين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r6.claim: For Qurtubi and the Malikis, any amount of milk that reaches the child’s gut suffices, even a single suck.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r6.anchor: ولا فرق بين قليل الرضاع وكثيره عندنا إذا وصل إلى الأمعاء ولو مصة واحدة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r7.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r7.claim: Al-Shafiʿi requires five feedings and that they occur within two years; he relies on Aisha’s abrogation report, Sahla’s report, and the completed two-year nursing period in 2:233.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r7.anchor: واعتبر الشافعي في الإرضاع شرطين: أحدهما خمس رضعات لحديث عائشة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r8.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r8.claim: Aisha reports that ten known feedings were revealed, then abrogated by five known feedings, which remained recited at the Prophet’s death; Shafiʿi argues a solitary report or analogy cannot abrogate that rule.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r8.anchor: كان فيما أنزل الله عشر رضعات معلومات يحرمن، ثم نسخن بخمس معلومات، وتوفي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهن مما يقرأ من القرآن

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة; مالك; زفر; الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r9.claim: The reported timing limits after two years differ: Abu Hanifa adds six months, Malik about a month, Zufar allows nursing while milk still sustains an unweaned child even to age three, and al-Awzaʿi ends it after sustained weaning at one year.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r9.anchor: واعتبر أبو حنيفة بعد الحولين ستة أشهر. ومالك الشهر ونحوه. وقال زفر: ما دام يجتزىء باللبن ولم يفطم فهو رضاع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r10.speaker: الليث بن سعد; عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r10.claim: Al-Layth uniquely among the jurists and Aisha hold that nursing an adult creates prohibition; a report from Abu Musa suggests he later retracted that ruling.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r10.anchor: وانفرد الليث بن سعد من بين العلماء إلى أن رضاع الكبير يوجب التحريم وهو قول عائشة رضي الله عنها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r11.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r11.claim: Abu Musa first ruled that a man who accidentally swallowed some of his wife’s milk had separated from her; Ibn Masʿud corrected him, and Abu Musa then declined to rule with a learned scholar present, indicating retraction.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r11.anchor: فقال الأشعري: لا تسألوني عن شيء وهذا الحبر بين أظهركم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r12.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r12.claim: Aisha supports adult nursing with the report of Salim, a grown man, whom the Prophet told Sahla to nurse.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r12.anchor: واحتجت عائشة بقصة سالم مولى أبي حذيفة وأنه كان رجلا. فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لسهلة بنت سهيل:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r13.speaker: طائفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r13.claim: A group says ten feedings are required because that number was once revealed; Qurtubi says they apparently did not learn that it had been abrogated.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r13.anchor: وشذت طائفة فاعتبرت عشر رضعات تمسكا بأنه كان فيما أنزل: عشر رضعات. وكأنهم لم يبلغهم الناسخ

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r14.speaker: داود
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r14.claim: Dawud holds that only three feedings create prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#4/r14.anchor: وقال داود: لا يحرم إلا بثلاث رضعات واحتج بقول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r1.claim: Qurtubi reports that Muslim records the statement that one or two instances of suckling do not establish marriage prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r1.anchor: أخرجه مسلم. وهو مروي عن عائشة وابن الزبير

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r2.speaker: عائشة وابن الزبير; أحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور وأبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r2.claim: Aisha and Ibn al-Zubayr transmit the three-feedings position, followed by Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Thawr, and Abu Ubayd; it relies on the disputed implication of the wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r2.anchor: وهو مروي عن عائشة وابن الزبير، وبه قال أحمد وإسحاق وأبو ثور وأبو عبيد، وهو تمسك بدليل الخطاب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r3.speaker: أئمة الفتوى
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r3.claim: The other major authorities hold that one confirmed feeding suffices, appealing to the minimum meaning of nursing, Medinan practice, and analogy with affinity, which permanently prohibits without a number requirement.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r3.anchor: وذهب من عدا هؤلاء من أئمة الفتوى إلى أن الرضعة الواحدة تحرم إذا تحققت كما ذكرنا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r4.speaker: الليث بن سعد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r4.claim: Al-Layth claims Muslims agree that small and large amounts of nursing in infancy prohibit as much as breaks a fast; Abu Umar says al-Layth missed the disagreement.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r4.anchor: وقال الليث بن سعد: وأجمع المسلمون على أن قليل الرضاع وكثيره يحرم في المهد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r5.claim: Qurtubi calls the clearest text the report that one or two sucks do not prohibit, which explains the verse as requiring three or more feedings; he allows that the report may concern feeds not certainly reaching the stomach.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r5.anchor: قلت وأنص ما في هذا الباب قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r6.speaker: الطحاوي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r6.claim: Al-Tahawi says the one-or-two-suck report is not established because it is transmitted with conflicting attributions to the Prophet, Aisha, or her father, and such inconsistency undermines it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r6.anchor: وذكر الطحاوي أن حديث الإملاجة والإملاجتين لا يثبت لأنه مرة يرويه ابن الزبير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، ومرة يرويه عن عائشة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r7.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r7.claim: Reports from Aisha differ: some say seven feedings, while another says she told her sister Umm Kulthum to nurse Salim ibn ʿAbd Allah ten times.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r7.anchor: وروي عن عائشة أنه لا يحرم إلا سبع رضعات. وروي عنها أنها أمرت أختها «أم كلثوم» أن ترضع سالم بن عبد الله عشر رضعات

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r8.speaker: حفصة; الشافعي; إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r8.claim: Reports from Hafsa specify ten, three, or five feedings; five is also the position of al-Shafiʿi and is attributed to Ishaq.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r8.anchor: وروي عن حفصة مثله، وروي عنها ثلاث، وروي عنها خمس كما قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه، وحكي عن إسحاق

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r9.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب وإبراهيم النخعي وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r9.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib, Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi, and Abu Salama deny that the husband’s milk causes any nursing prohibition through the man.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r9.anchor: استدل به من نفى لبن الفحل، وهو سعيد ابن المسيب وإبراهيم النخعي وأبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r10.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r10.claim: The majority say the husband is also a milk father because the milk is attributed to him as it arose through his child.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r10.anchor: وقال الجمهور: قوله تعالى: { وأمهاتكم اللاتي أرضعنكم } يدل على أن الفحل أب لأن اللبن منسوب إليه فإنه در بسبب ولده

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r11.claim: Qurtubi rejects that reasoning: milk comes from the woman, not the man; the man only caused conception, and the milk appears by God’s creation after birth, so it cannot be inferred from analogy with semen.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#5/r11.anchor: وهذا ضعيف فإن الولد خلق من ماء الرجل والمرأة جميعا، واللبن من المرأة ولم يخرج من الرجل

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r1.claim: A report about a stepdaughter in the man’s household says that without this household condition she would remain lawful to him because she is his milk brother’s daughter.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r1.anchor: لو لم تكن ربيبتي في حجري ما حلت لي إنها ابنة أخي من الرضاعة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r2.claim: A report is transmitted from Ali permitting the view that the stepdaughter’s residence in the man’s household is a condition.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r2.anchor: ورووا عن علي بن أبي طالب إجازة ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r3.speaker: ابن المنذر والطحاوي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r3.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tahawi reject the Ali report because its transmitter Ibrahim ibn ʿUbayd is unknown and scholars generally disputed it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r3.anchor: قال ابن المنذر والطحاوي: أما الحديث عن علي فلا يثبت

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r4.claim: Abu Ubayd counters the household condition with a general Prophetic prohibition on offering one’s daughters or sisters, which does not limit the rule to those living in the household.

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r5.speaker: الطحاوي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r5.claim: Al-Tahawi says the household wording describes the usual situation of stepdaughters and is not a condition of their prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r5.anchor: قال الطحاوي: وإضافتهن إلى الحجور إنما ذلك على الأغلب مما يكون عليه الربائب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r6.claim: If the man has not consummated the marriage with the mother, he may marry her daughter after divorce or her death; scholars agree on this rule.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r6.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فإن لم تكونوا دخلتم بهن } يعني بالأمهات. { فلا جناح عليكم } يعني في نكاح بناتهن

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and others define consummation with the mother as sexual intercourse.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r7.anchor: واختلفوا في معنى الدخول بالأمهات الذي يقع به تحريم الربائب فروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: الدخول الجماع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r8.speaker: مالك والثوري وأبو حنيفة والأوزاعي والليث; أحد قولي الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r8.claim: Malik, al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa, al-Awzaʿi, al-Layth, and one Shafiʿi view hold that touching the woman with desire prohibits her mother and daughter and makes her prohibited to the man’s father and son.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r8.anchor: واتفق مالك والثوري وأبو حنيفة والأوزاعي والليث على أنه إذا مسها بشهوة حرمت عليه أمها وابنتها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r9.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r9.claim: Malik says looking pleasurably at the woman’s hair, chest, or other beauty prohibits her mother and daughter.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r9.anchor: فقال مالك: إذا نظر إلى شعرها أو صدرها أو شيء من محاسنها للذة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r10.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r10.claim: The Kufans equate looking at the woman’s genitals with desire to touching her with desire.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r10.anchor: وقال الكوفيون: إذا نظر إلى فرجها للشهوة كان بمنزلة اللمس للشهوة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r11.speaker: الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r11.claim: Al-Thawri says deliberate looking at her genitals or touching her makes the prohibition apply, without stating a desire requirement.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r11.anchor: وقال الثوري: يحرم إذا نظر إلى فرجها متعمدا أو لمسها ولم يذكر الشهوة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r12.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r12.claim: Ibn Abi Layla, like al-Shafiʿi, says looking alone does not prohibit; touching is required.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r12.anchor: وقال ابن أبي ليلى: لا تحرم بالنظر حتى يلمس وهو قول الشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r13.claim: Qurtubi argues that looking can trigger prohibition because it is a kind of enjoyment and legal rulings follow underlying meanings, not merely words.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r13.anchor: والدليل على أن بالنظر يقع التحريم أن فيه نوع استمتاع فجرى مجرى النكاح إذ الأحكام تتعلق بالمعاني لا بالألفاظ

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r14.claim: He also treats gaze as a kind of intimate meeting and cites poets who describe night uniting a man with Umm ʿAmr and the pair seeing the same moon.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#6/r14.anchor: وقد بالغ في ذلك الشعراء فقالوا:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r1.claim: Ḥalāʾil means wives and is the plural of ḥalīlah; Qurtubi derives it from sharing a dwelling place, while al-Zajjaj and others derive it from halal, and another view refers to spouses loosening one another’s waistwrap.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r1.anchor: الحلائل جمع حليلة، وهي الزوجة. سميت حليلة لأنها تحل مع الزوج حيث حل فهي فعيلة بمعنى فاعلة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r2.speaker: الزجاج وقوم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj and others derive ḥalīlah from halal, meaning a woman made lawful.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r2.anchor: وذهب الزجاج وقوم إلى أنها من لفظة الحلال فهي حليلة بمعنى محللة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r3.claim: Another etymology says husband and wife are called ḥalīlah because each loosens the other’s waistwrap.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r3.anchor: وقيل: لأن كل واحد منهما يحل إزار صاحبه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r4.claim: Scholars agree that a father’s marriage partner is forbidden to his son, and a son’s marriage partner to his father, whether or not the marriage was consummated.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r4.anchor: أجمع العلماء على تحريم ما عقد عليه الآباء على الأبناء، وما عقد عليه الأبناء على الآباء، كان مع العقد وطء أو لم يكن

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r5.claim: A unanimously invalid marriage has no legal effect; a disputed invalid marriage still creates the prohibition because it may count as valid, and where sexual permissibility and prohibition conflict, prohibition prevails.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r5.anchor: فإن كان متفقا على فساده لم يوجب حكما وكان وجوده كعدمه. وإن كان مختلفا فيه فيتعلق به من الحرمة ما يتعلق بالصحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r6.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r6.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says the regional scholars he knows agree that intercourse in an invalid marriage makes the woman forbidden to the man’s father, son, ancestors, and descendants.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r6.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: أجمع كل من يحفظ عنه من علماء الأمصار على أن الرجل إذا وطىء امرأة بنكاح فاسد أنها تحرم على أبيه وابنه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r7.claim: Buying a slave woman alone does not make her forbidden to the buyer’s father or son, but touching or kissing her does; scholars do not disagree on that, while sight alone is disputed.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r7.anchor: عقد الشراء على الجارية لا يحرمها على أبيه وابنه فإذا اشترى الرجل جارية فلمس أو قبل حرمت على أبيه وابنه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r8.speaker: يعقوب ومحمد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r8.claim: Yaʿqub and Muhammad say looking at a woman’s genitals with desire makes her forbidden to the man’s father and son, and makes her mother and daughter forbidden to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r8.anchor: وقال يعقوب ومحمد: إذا نظر رجل في فرج امرأة من شهوة حرمت على أبيه وابنه، وتحرم عليه أمها وابنتها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r9.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r9.claim: Malik extends the rule to intercourse, taking the intercourse position, kissing, touching, or squeezing the enslaved woman for pleasure, making her forbidden to the buyer’s son.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r9.anchor: وقال مالك: إذا وطىء الأمة أو قعد منها مقعدا لذلك وإن لم يفض إليها، أو قبلها أو باشرها أو غمزها تلذذا فلا تحل لابنه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r10.speaker: الشافعي والأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r10.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and al-Awzaʿi hold that touching creates the prohibition but looking without touching does not.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#7/r10.anchor: وقال الشافعي: إنما تحرم باللمس ولا تحرم بالنظر دون اللمس وهو قول الأوزاعي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r1.speaker: أكثر أهل العلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r1.claim: Most scholars say adultery does not prohibit marrying the woman or her mother or daughter, nor does adultery with a wife’s mother or daughter prohibit the wife; the offender is subject to the prescribed penalty.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r1.anchor: ومن زنى بامرأة ثم أراد نكاح أمها أو ابنتها لم تحرما عليه بذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r2.speaker: عمران بن حصين والشعبي وعطاء والحسن وسفيان الثوري وأحمد وإسحاق وأصحاب الرأي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r2.claim: A group says adultery does create the prohibition; this is reported from the named authorities and held by the Iraqi jurists.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r2.anchor: روي هذا القول عن عمران بن حصين وبه قال الشعبي وعطاء والحسن وسفيان الثوري وأحمد وإسحاق وأصحاب الرأي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r3.claim: Qurtubi prefers the position of Malik’s sound view, the Hijazis, al-Shafiʿi, and Abu Thawr: zina has no legal effect because the woman is not a wife and her daughter is not a stepdaughter; zina lacks marriage’s legal consequences.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r3.anchor: والصحيح من قول مالك وأهل الحجاز: أن الزنى لا حكم له

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r4.claim: A report from Aisha says the Prophet ruled that unlawful sex does not forbid lawful marriage; only a relationship formed by marriage creates this prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r4.anchor: وروى الدارقطني من حديث الزهري عن عروة عن عائشة قالت:

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r5.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r5.claim: The opposing side invokes the Prophet’s account of Jurayj, where a child named a shepherd as his father, to argue that adultery creates kinship prohibitions between the man, the woman, and their relatives; Ibn al-Qasim records this in al-Mudawwana.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r5.anchor: فهذا يدل على أن الزنى يحرم كما يحرم الوطء الحلال فلا تحل أم المزني بها ولا بناتها لآباء الزاني ولا لأولاده وهي رواية ابن القاسم في المدونة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r6.claim: The Jurayj story is also used to argue that a child conceived through zina creates prohibited kinship ties with the man; this is described as the well-known view.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r6.anchor: ويستدل به أيضا على أن المخلوقة من ماء الزاني لا تحل للزاني بأمها، وهو المشهور

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r7.claim: Two further reports forbid looking at a woman’s private parts together with her daughter, or uncovering a woman and her daughter, without distinguishing lawful from unlawful relations.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r7.anchor: قال عليه السلام: «لا ينظر الله إلى رجل نظر إلى فرج امرأة وابنتها»

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r8.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r8.claim: Ibn Khuwayz Mindad infers that kissing and all other forms of sexual enjoyment also spread the prohibition.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r8.anchor: قال ابن خويز منداد: ولهذا قلنا إن القبلة وسائر وجوه الاستمتاع ينشر الحرمة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r9.speaker: عبد الملك الماجشون
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r9.claim: ʿAbd al-Malik al-Majishun says such a woman remains lawful, which Qurtubi endorses on the basis of 25:54, understood as referring to valid marriage.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r9.anchor: وقال عبد الملك الماجشون: إنها تحل وهو الصحيح لقوله تعالى: وهو الذي خلق من المآء بشرا فجعله نسبا وصهرا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r10.claim: Qurtubi argues that God and the Prophet certify the paternity claim in the Jurayj story when the child speaks, establishing filiation and its legal effects.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r10.anchor: فكانت تلك النسبة صحيحة بتصديق الله تعالى وبإخبار النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن ذلك فثبتت البنوة وأحكامها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r11.claim: Although one may object that this would entail inheritance and guardianship despite consensus against inheritance, Qurtubi says agreed exceptions are set aside and the remaining implications stand.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#8/r11.anchor: وما انعقد عليه الإجماع من الأحكام استثنيناه، وبقي الباقي على أصل ذلك الدليل

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r1.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r1.claim: They hold that sodomy does not create a marriage prohibition by affinity.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r1.anchor: قال مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابهم لا يحرم النكاح باللواط

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r2.speaker: الثوري وأحمد بن حنبل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r2.claim: Al-Thawri, followed here by Ahmad, says sexual play with a boy makes the boy's mother forbidden to the man.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r2.anchor: إذا لعب بالصبي حرمت عليه أمه وهو قول أحمد بن حنبل

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r3.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r3.claim: Ahmad also holds that sodomizing a wife's son, father, or brother makes the wife forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r3.anchor: إذا تلوط بابن امرأته أو أبيها أوأخيها حرمت عليه امرأته

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r4.speaker: الأوزاعي وأحمد بن حنبل
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r4.claim: If a boy sodomized by a man later fathers a daughter, they bar the man from marrying her because she is the daughter of one with whom he had intercourse.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r4.anchor: إذا لاط بغلام وولد للمفجور به بنت لم يجز للفاجر أن يتزوجها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r5.claim: The phrase restricts the son's wife prohibition to biological sons, excluding Arabs' adopted sons; the Prophet's marriage to Zayd's former wife prompted the objection that he married his son's wife.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r5.anchor: تخصيص ليخرج عنه كل من كانت العرب تتبناه ممن ليس للصلب

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r6.claim: A son's wife through breastfeeding is also forbidden by consensus, even without biological descent, on the hadith that breastfeeding prohibits what lineage prohibits.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r6.anchor: وحرمت حليلة الابن من الرضاع وإن لم يكن للصلب بالإجماع المستند إلى قوله عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r7.claim: The conjunction أن is nominative by coordination with the opening prohibited categories; الأختان covers sisters together in marriage or ownership.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r7.anchor: رفع على العطف على { حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم }. والأختان لفظ يعم الجميع بنكاح وبملك يمين

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r8.claim: The community agrees that two sisters cannot be joined in one marriage contract, supported by the verse and a Prophetic prohibition against offering daughters or sisters.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r8.anchor: وأجمعت الأمة على منع جمعهما في عقد واحد من النكاح لهذه الآية، وقوله عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r9.claim: The Prophet said not to offer one's daughters or sisters for marriage in this context.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r9.anchor: لا تعرضن علي بناتكن ولا أخواتكن

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r10.speaker: كافة العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r10.claim: All scholars forbid intercourse with two owned sisters together, while agreeing that both may be owned; the same ownership distinction applies to a woman and her daughter.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r10.anchor: ذهب كافة العلماء إلى أنه لا يجوز الجمع بينهما بالملك في الوطء، وإن كان يجوز الجمع بينهما في الملك بإجماع

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r11.speaker: الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r11.claim: Al-Awza'i bars marrying the sister of a slave woman after having intercourse with that woman by ownership.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r11.anchor: إذا وطىء جارية له بملك اليمين لم يجز له أن يتزوج أختها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r12.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r12.claim: Al-Shafi'i permits marrying the sister of a slave woman, since ownership does not bar the marriage.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r12.anchor: وقال الشافعي ملك اليمين لا يمنع نكاح الأخت

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r13.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r13.claim: Abu Umar explains that those equating marriage with purchase permit the contract, while those equating it with intercourse forbid it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r13.anchor: من جعل عقد النكاح كالشراء أجازه، ومن جعله كالوطء لم يجزه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r14.claim: Scholars agree that a man may not contract marriage with his wife's sister; here combining two sisters means two wives under marriage contracts.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r14.anchor: وقد أجمعوا على أنه لا يجوز العقد على أخت الزوجة لقول الله تعالى: { وأن تجمعوا بين الأختين } يعني الزوجتين بعقد النكاح

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r15.speaker: أهل الظاهر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r15.claim: The anomalous literalist view permits intercourse with two owned sisters just as it permits owning both.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r15.anchor: شذ أهل الظاهر فقالوا: يجوز الجمع بين الأختين بملك اليمين في الوطء كما يجوز الجمع بينهما في الملك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r16.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r16.claim: Uthman answered a question about two owned sisters by saying one verse permits them and another forbids them.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r16.anchor: فقال: لا آمرك ولا أنهاك أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r17.speaker: رجل من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r17.claim: A Companion rebuked the permissive answer, saying he would forbid the practice and make an offender an example if he had authority.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#9/r17.anchor: لكني أنهاك، ولو كان لي عليك سبيل ثم فعلت لجعلتك نكالا

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r1.speaker: الطحاوي والدارقطني
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r1.claim: Al-Tahawi and al-Daraqutni also transmit from Ali and Ibn Abbas a position like Uthman's on two owned sisters.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r1.anchor: وذكر الطحاوي والدارقطني عن علي وابن عباس مثل قول عثمان

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r2.claim: The verse used to permit intercourse with both is 4:24, but no authoritative jurist accepted that reading because they understood the Qur'an differently.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r2.anchor: والآية التي أحلتهما قوله تعالى: { وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم }

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r3.speaker: عمر وعلي وابن مسعود وعثمان وابن عباس وعمار وابن عمر وعائشة وابن الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r3.claim: These Companions held the contrary interpretation of the Qur'an; al-Qurtubi calls them its learned authorities and deems their opponents' reading forced.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r3.anchor: وممن قال ذلك من الصحابة: عمر وعلي وابن مسعود وعثمان وابن عباس وعمار وابن عمر وعائشة وابن الزبير

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r4.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r4.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir reports that Ishaq ibn Rahawayh forbade intercourse with both sisters; most scholars disliked it, including Malik.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r4.anchor: وذكر ابن المنذر أن إسحاق بن راهويه حرم الجمع بينهما بالوطء، وأن جمهور أهل العلم كرهوا ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r5.claim: There is no disagreement that both sisters may be jointly owned, just as a mother and her daughter may be jointly owned.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r5.anchor: ولا خلاف في جواز جمعهما في الملك، وكذلك الأم وابنتها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya infers from Ishaq's position that a man who has intercourse with both would be stoned.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r6.anchor: ويجيء من قول إسحاق أن يرجم الجامع بينهما بالوطء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r7.claim: Malik's rule implies no fixed penalty: after intercourse with one sister, the man is stopped from both until he makes one forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r7.anchor: تستقرأ الكراهية من قول مالك: إنه إذا وطىء واحدة ثم وطيءالأخرى وقف عنهما

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r8.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r8.claim: Abu Umar says Ali threatened to make an offender an example rather than impose the adulterer's penalty because mistaken scriptural interpretation is not fornication by consensus, absent inexcusable ignorance.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r8.anchor: فليس بزان بإجماع وإن كان مخطئا، إلا أن يدعي من ذلك ما لا يعذر بجهله

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r9.claim: The preserved early saying that one verse permits the sisters and another forbids them creates a strong legal doubt against treating the act as adultery.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r9.anchor: معلوم محفوظ فكيف يحد حد الزاني من فعل ما فيه مثل هذا من الشبهة القوية

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r10.speaker: علي وابن عمر والحسن البصري والأوزاعي والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r10.claim: They forbid intercourse with the second owned sister until the first is removed from ownership by sale, manumission, or marriage.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r10.anchor: لا يجوز له وطء الثانية حتى يحرم فرج الأخرى بإخراجها من ملكه ببيع أو عتق، أو بأن يزوجها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r11.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r11.claim: Qatadah's second view lets a man intend to forbid the first to himself, abstain from both through her waiting-out period, then approach the second.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r11.anchor: وهو أنه إذا كان يطأ واحدة وأراد وطء الأخرى فإنه ينوي تحريم الأولى على نفسه وألا يقربها

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r12.speaker: الحكم وحماد والنخعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r12.claim: A third view, held by al-Hakam and Hammad and also reported from al-Nakha'i, forbids approaching either sister while he owns both.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r12.anchor: وفيه قول ثالث وهو إذا كان عنده أختان فلا يقرب واحدة منهما. هكذا قال الحكم وحماد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r13.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r13.claim: Malik permits intercourse with either owned sister and leaves abstention from the other to the man's trust; to switch, he must act to remove the first from ownership.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r13.anchor: ومذهب مالك: إذا كان أختان عند رجل بملك فله أن يطأ أيتهما شاء، والكف عن الأخرى موكول إلى أمانته

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r14.claim: If a man has already had intercourse with one and then approaches the other, he is suspect and must avoid both until he makes one forbidden; before intercourse he was not suspect.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#10/r14.anchor: وقف عنهما، ولم يجز له قرب إحداهما حتى يحرم الأخرى ولم يوكل ذلك إلى أمانته

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r1.speaker: الثوري وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r1.claim: The Kufan view forbids intercourse with a second owned sister; if the first is sold or married and returns during her waiting period, he may approach the second, but not after that period until another man acquires sexual access to the first.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r1.anchor: الثوري وأبي حنيفة وأصحابه أنه إن وطىء إحدى أمتيه لم يطأ الأخرى فإن باع الأولى أو زوجها ثم رجعت إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r2.speaker: الثوري وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r2.claim: They reason that the ownership which originally barred intercourse still exists, so a woman's return is no different from her remaining in the man's possession.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r2.anchor: قالوا: لأن الملك الذي منع وطء الجارية في الابتداء موجود، فلا فرق بين عودتها إليه وبين بقائها في ملكه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
