QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers Malik: a sale or marriage creates a valid immediate prohibition, and there is no duty to account for a possible future return.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r3.anchor: وقول مالك حسن لأنه تحريم صحيح في الحال ولا يلزم مراعاة المآل

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r4.claim: There is no disagreement about manumission, which cannot be undone; a contracted slave woman may default and return to ownership.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r4.anchor: ولم يختلفوا في العتق لأنه لا يتصرف فيه بحال وأما المكاتبة فقد تعجز فترجع إلى ملكه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r5.speaker: أهل المذهب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r5.claim: The Mudawwana's third position suspends access to both sisters and dislikes the marriage, since intercourse is barred where the contract occurs.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r5.anchor: الثالث في المدونة أنه يوقف عنهما إذا وقع عقد النكاح حتى يحرم إحداهما مع كراهية لهذا النكاح إذ هو عقد في موضع لا يجوز فيه الوطء

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r6.claim: The Mudawwana position indicates that ownership does not itself prevent marriage, as al-Shafi'i had argued.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r6.anchor: وفي هذا ما يدل على أن ملك اليمين لا يمنع النكاح كما تقدم عن الشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r7.speaker: الأوزاعي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r7.claim: Another position, associated with al-Awza'i, holds that the marriage contract does not take effect.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r7.anchor: وفي الباب بعينه قول آخر: أن النكاح لا ينعقد وهو معنى قول الأوزاعي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r8.speaker: أشهب
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r8.claim: Ashhab says contracting marriage with one sister itself makes the slave woman's sexual access forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r8.anchor: عقد النكاح في الواحدة تحريم لفرج المملوكة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r9.claim: Scholars unanimously bar a man with a revocably divorced wife from marrying her sister or a fourth wife until her waiting period ends.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r9.anchor: ليس له أن ينكح أختها أو أربعا سواها حتى تنقضي عدة المطلقة

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r10.speaker: علي وزيد بن ثابت ومجاهد وعطاء والنخعي والثوري وأحمد وأصحاب الرأي
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r10.claim: One group also bars marriage to the sister or another wife after an irrevocable divorce until the divorced woman's waiting period ends.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r10.anchor: فقالت طائفة: ليس له أن ينكح أختها ولا رابعة حتى تنقضي عدة التي طلق

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r11.speaker: عطاء وسعيد بن المسيب والحسن والقاسم وعروة بن الزبير وابن أبي ليلى والشافعي وأبو ثور وأبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r11.claim: The other group permits marrying her sister or a fourth wife after an irrevocable divorce; the stronger report from Ata and another report from Zayd support it.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r11.anchor: وقالت طائفة: له أن ينكح أختها وأربعا سواها وروي عن عطاء، وهي أثبت الروايتين عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r12.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r12.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir supposes the permissive position is Malik's view, and al-Qurtubi says this is the position they follow.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r12.anchor: ولا أحسبه إلا قول مالك وبه نقول

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r13.claim: The exception may carry the same meaning as the exception in the preceding verse about marrying fathers' wives.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r13.anchor: في قوله: { ولا تنكحوا ما نكح آباؤكم من النسآء إلا ما قد سلف }

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r14.claim: Alternatively, it may grandfather pre-Islamic unions of two sisters; in Islam, as Malik and al-Shafi'i hold, the man chooses one, whether the two were joined in one contract or separate contracts.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r14.anchor: وأنه إذا جرى الجمع في الجاهلية كان النكاح صحيحا، وإذا جرى في الإسلام خير بين الأختين على ما قاله مالك والشافعي

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r15.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r15.claim: Abu Hanifa invalidates both marriages when the two sisters are joined in a single contract.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r15.anchor: وأبو حنيفة يبطل نكاحهما إن جمع في عقد واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r16.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r16.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan says pre-Islamic Arabs knew the listed prohibitions except marrying a father's wife and combining sisters, as only these two mention an exception for the past.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:23#11/r16.anchor: كان أهل الجاهلية يعرفون هذه المحرمات كلها التي ذكرت في هذه الآية إلا اثنتين

RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r1.claim: The verse names fourteen forbidden categories: seven through blood relationship, and seven otherwise—foster mothers and sisters, wives' mothers, consummated wives' daughters, sons' wives, fathers' wives (in the prior verse), and combining two sisters.
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r1.anchor: نص على تحريم أربعة عشر صنفا من النسوان : سبعة منهن من جهة النسب

RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r2.speaker: الكرخي
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r2.claim: Al-Karkhī calls the verse ambiguous because prohibition is attached to persons rather than an explicitly named act, and no act is stated as its object.
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r2.anchor: ذهب الكرخي إلى أن هذه الآية مجملة قال : لأنه أضيف التحريم فيها إلى الأمهات والبنات

RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r3.claim: Al-Razi rejects the ambiguity claim: the preceding prohibition of marrying fathers' former wives (4:22) makes marriage the intended prohibited act here.
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r3.anchor: أن تقديم قوله تعالى : { ولا تنكحوا ما نكح ءاباؤكم } ( النساء : 22 ) يدل على أن المراد

RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r4.claim: Ordinary usage and necessary religious knowledge identify the prohibited act when permission or prohibition is attached to persons: eating carrion and blood, marrying mothers and daughters, and shedding a Muslim's blood.
RAZI-FULL:v10p21/r4.anchor: الأصل فيه أن الحرمة والاباحة إذا أضيفتا إلى الاعيان ، فالمراد تحريم الفعل المطلوب منها في العرف

RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r1.claim: Because the clause is passive, it does not expressly name God as the agent of prohibition; that must be supplied by consensus, so the verse alone proves nothing further.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r1.anchor: أن قوله : { حرمت عليكم } مذكور على ما لم يسم فاعله ، فليس فيه تصريح بأن فاعل هذا التحريم هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r2.claim: The wording does not specify that the prohibition lasts forever; permanence requires evidence beyond the verse's apparent wording.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r2.anchor: أن قوله : { حرمت عليكم } ليس نصا في ثبوت التحريم على سبيل التأييد

RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r3.claim: As direct address, the wording appears limited to those present, so applying the rule to everyone requires separate evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r3.anchor: أن قوله : { حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم } خطاب مشافهة فيخصص بأولئك الحاضرين

RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r4.claim: As a past-tense report, the wording does not itself cover the present or future; that extension needs separate evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r4.anchor: قوله : { حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم } إخبار عن ثبوت هذا

RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r5.claim: The plural wording superficially says each person is forbidden every mother and daughter, whereas the intended distributive sense pairs each person with his own mother and daughter.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r5.anchor: ظاهر قوله : { حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم } يقتضي أنه قد حرم على كل أحد جميع أمهاتهم وجميع بناتهم

RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r6.claim: The past form suggests a new prohibition after prior permissibility; if these relations had always been forbidden, it would imply re-creating an existing prohibition, so separate evidence is needed.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22/r6.anchor: أن قوله : { حرمات } يشعر ظاهره بسبق الحل

RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r1.claim: Mothers and daughters have been forbidden from Adam's time onward in every revealed religion; Zoroaster, whom most Muslims considered a liar, reportedly allowed them.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r1.anchor: حرمة الأمهات والبنات كانت ثابتة من زمن آدم عليه السلام إلى هذا الزمان

RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r2.claim: Sister marriage was reportedly permitted in Adam's time as a necessity.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r2.anchor: أما نكاح الاخوات فقد نقل أن ذلك كان مباحا في زمن آدم عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r3.speaker: بعض المشايخ
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r3.claim: Some shaykhs deny that Adam's children married their sisters and say God sent houris from Paradise to marry his sons.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r3.anchor: ورأيت بعض المشايخ أنكر ذلك ، وقال : انه تعالى كان يبعث الحواري من الجنة ليزوج بهن أبناء آدم عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi calls that account implausible: if their wives and their daughters' husbands came from Paradise, Adam's descendants would not be exclusively his children, contrary to consensus.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r4.anchor: وهذا بعيد ، لأنه إذا كان زوجات أبنائه وأزواج بناته من أهل الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r5.claim: Intercourse is degrading: people are ashamed to mention it, do it in seclusion, and use it in many insults; mothers deserve protection because their benefaction to children is greatest.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r5.anchor: أن الوطء إذلال وإهانة ، فان الانسان يستحي من ذكره ولا يقدم عليه إلا في الموضع الخالي

RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r6.claim: A daughter is part of a person, as the Prophet says of Fāṭima, so intercourse with her is likewise degrading and she must be protected.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r6.anchor: والبنت بمنزلة جزء من الانسان وبعض منه ، قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( فاطمة بضعة مني )

RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r7.claim: Al-Wāḥidī explains that ummāt is a plural of umm, whose original form was ummah; the hāʾ was dropped in the singular.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r7.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : الأمهات جمع الأم والأم في الأصل أمهة فأسقط الهاء في التوحيد

RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r8.speaker: شاعر
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r8.claim: A cited line uses the plural ummahāt and names Khindif as the poet's mother and Iyās as his father.
RAZI-FULL:v10p22#2/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر : أمهتى خندف والياس أبي

RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r1.speaker: الراعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r1.claim: Al-Rāʿī's verse uses ummāt for animal mothers, illustrating that this plural is especially common for nonhuman animals.

RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r2.claim: A mother includes every woman in one's birth ancestry, through one or more generations and through either female or male links.
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r2.anchor: كل امرأة رجع نسبك اليها بالولادة من جهة أبيك أو من جهة أمك بدرجة أو بدرجات

RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r3.claim: If umm is a univocal term shared literally by one's immediate mother and all grandmothers, the verse explicitly prohibits marrying both.
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r3.anchor: فان كان لفظ الأم حقيقة في الأم الأصلية وفي الجدات ، فاما أن يكون لفظا متواطئا

RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r4.claim: If umm is homonymous for mother and grandmother, those who allow one shared expression to carry both senses make the verse explicit about prohibiting all grandmothers too.
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r4.anchor: فمن جوزه حمل اللفظ ههنا على الكل ، وحينئذ يكون تحريم الجدات منصوصا عليه

RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r5.claim: Those who forbid using a homonym for both senses either take the verse to mean only the immediate mother, leaving grandmother prohibition to consensus, or posit two divine utterances with distinct senses.
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r5.anchor: فتحريم نكاحها مستفاد من هذا الوجه ، وأما تحريم نكاح الجدات فغير مستفاد من هذا النص

RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r6.claim: The same interpretive options apply if the word is literal for the immediate mother but metaphorical for grandmothers, since one word cannot simultaneously carry its literal and figurative senses.
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r6.anchor: ثبت أنه لا يجوز استعمال اللفظ الواحد دفعة واحدة في حقيقته ومجازه معا

RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r7.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r7.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires the legal penalty for a man who marries and consummates marriage with his mother; Abū Ḥanīfa does not.
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r7.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمه الله : إذا تزوج الرجل بأمه ودخل بها يلزمه الحد ، وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله لا يلزمه

RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r8.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r8.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that such a marriage is void and the intercourse is therefore unqualified zinā, requiring the penalty in 24:2; its offer and acceptance cannot form a valid contract, and scripture categorically invalidates it.
RAZI-FULL:v10p23/r8.anchor: حجة الشافعي أن وجود هذا النكاح وعدمه بمثابة واحدة ، فكان هذا الوطء زنا محضا فيلزمه الحد

RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r1.claim: A daughter is every female descended from a person by birth through one or more generations, through either female or male links.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r1.anchor: كل أنثى يرجع نسبها اليك بالولادة

RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r2.claim: Whether a son's or daughter's daughter is literally or figuratively called a daughter is the same lexical question discussed for grandmothers.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r2.anchor: وأما بنت الابن وبنت البنت فهل تسمى بنتا حقيقة أو مجازا ؟ فالبحث فيه عين ما ذكرناه في الأمهات

RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r3.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r3.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī holds that a daughter conceived through fornication is not forbidden to the fornicator; Abū Ḥanīfa holds that she is.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r3.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمه الله : البنت المخلوقة من ماء الزنا لا تحرم على الزاني . وقال أبو حنيفة : تحرم

RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r4.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that biological conception cannot establish paternity consistently under Abū Ḥanīfa's rules: a child of a purchased virgin may lack paternity, while a child of distant spouses has it despite no biological conception by the husband.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r4.anchor: الأول : أن أبا حنيفة إما أن يثبت كونها بنتا له بناء على الحقيقة ، وهي كونها مخلوقة من مائه

RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r5.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī argues that legal lineage from adultery is denied by Muslim consensus, and a judge would have to prevent the child from claiming the fornicator as her father.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r5.anchor: أجمع المسلمون على أنه لا نسب لولد الزنا من الزاني ، ولو انتسب إلى الزاني لوجب على القاضي منعه

RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r6.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī cites the Prophet's rule that a child belongs to the marital bed and the adulterer receives the stone, restricting lineage to the marriage bed.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r6.anchor: الوجه الثاني : التمسك بقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( الولد للفراش وللعاهر الحجر )

RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r7.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r7.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī infers she is not his daughter because she inherits (4:11), could be subject to his marriage guardianship, and would be owed maintenance and custody; none applies, and solitude with her would be permitted.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r7.anchor: لو كانت بنتا له لأخذت الميراث لقوله تعالى : { للذكر مثل حظ الانثيين } ( النساء : 11 )

RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r8.claim: Since she is not his daughter and fornication does not create affinity prohibition either, she is not forbidden to marry him.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24/r8.anchor: فثبت أنها غير محرمة على الزاني والله أعلم

RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r1.claim: The forbidden sisters include full sisters, paternal half-sisters, and maternal half-sisters.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r1.anchor: ويدخل فيه الأخوات من الأب والأم معا

RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r2.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī defines a paternal aunt as the sister of any male ancestor, including a mother's father's sister; a maternal aunt is a sister of any female ancestor, including a father's mother's sister.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r2.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : كل ذكر رجع نسبك اليه فأخته عمتك

RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r3.claim: Nieces through brothers and sisters follow the same rule as daughters descended directly from oneself.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r3.anchor: والقول في بنات الأخ وبنات الأخت كالقول في بنات الصلب

RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r4.claim: The seven blood-relationship categories are expressly prohibited and, according to the commentators, can never become lawful.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون : كل امرأة حرم الله نكاحها للنسب والرحم ، فتحريمها مؤبد لا يحل بوجه من الوجوه

RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r5.claim: The rest of the verse names women who would otherwise be lawful but become prohibited through a temporary circumstance.
RAZI-FULL:v10p24#2/r5.anchor: وأما اللواتي يحل نكاحهن ثم يصرن محرمات بسبب طارىء ، فهن اللاتي ذكرن في باقي الآية

RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r1.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says wet nurses are called mothers because they create a prohibition, just as the Prophet's wives are called the believers' mothers because of their protected status (33:6).
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : المرضعات سماهن أمهات لأجل الحرمة

RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r2.claim: Although the verse expressly names foster mothers and sisters, the Prophet's rule extends the prohibition of nursing to every relation forbidden by blood kinship.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى نص في هذه الآية على حرمة الأمهات والأخوات من جهة الرضاعة إلا أن الحرمة غير مقصورة عليهن

RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r3.claim: Naming a nursing mother and sister signals that nursing follows lineage: of seven blood-prohibited classes, two arise through birth and five through sibling relationships; the verse names one example from each group, and the hadith confirms the inference.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r3.anchor: لما سمى المرضعة أما ، والمرضعة أختا ، فقد نبه بذلك على أنه تعالى أجرى الرضاع مجرى النسب

RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r4.claim: A milk-mother is the woman who nursed someone and any woman maternally related to her through birth or nursing; the same applies to the milk-father and the descendants treated as daughters.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r4.anchor: أم الأنسان من الرضاع هي التي أرضعته ، وكذلك كل امرأة انتسبت إلى تلك المرضعة بالأمومة

RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r5.claim: A full foster sister shares both milk parents: she is a stranger nursed by one's mother with one's father's milk, whether nursed at the same time or before or after.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r5.anchor: وهي الصغيرة الأجنبية التي أرضعتها أمك بلبن أبيك ، سواء أرضعتها معك أو مع ولد قبلك أو بعدك

RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r6.claim: A paternal foster sister shares one's father but not one's mother: one's father's wife nursed her with his milk.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r6.anchor: وهي التي أرضعتها زوجة أبيك بلبن أبيك

RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r7.claim: A maternal foster sister shares one's mother but not one's father: one's mother nursed her with another man's milk.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r7.anchor: وهي التي أرضعتها أمك بلبن رجل آخر

RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r8.claim: Once foster parents are defined, the same method identifies foster aunts, uncles, nieces, and nephews.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25/r8.anchor: واذا عرفت ذلك سهل عليك معرفة العمات والخالات وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت

RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r1.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī requires five nursing sessions for prohibition; Abū Ḥanīfa considers even one session sufficient.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r1.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمة الله عليه : الرضاع يحرم بشرط أن يكون خمس رضعات ، وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه : الرضعة الواحدة كافية

RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r2.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī argues that the verse ties maternal or sibling status to nursing, so any occurrence of nursing should trigger the ruling.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r2.anchor: واحتج أبو بكر الرازي بهذه الآية فقال : انه تعالى علق هذا الاسم يعني الأمومة والاخوة بفعل الرضاع

RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r3.claim: He answers an objection that ‘mothers who clothed you’ would imply prior motherhood: nursing itself confers the maternal name, unlike clothing.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r3.anchor: الرضاع هو الذي يكسوها سمة الأمومة ، فلما كان الاسم مستحقا بوجود الرضاع كان الحكم معلقا به

RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r4.claim: When told that Ibn al-Zubayr allowed one or two feeds, Ibn ʿUmar answered that God's ruling is better and cited foster sisters, understanding the verse to prohibit even little nursing.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r4.anchor: فقال ابن عمر : قضاء الله خير من قضاء ابن الزبير ، قال الله تعالى : { وأخواتكم من الرضاعة }

RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r5.claim: Al-Razi calls Abū Bakr's argument circular: whether motherhood arises after one or five feeds is the disputed issue, so using this verse to assume it follows any nursing begs the question.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r5.anchor: وهل النزاع الا فيه ، فان عندي أن اسم الأمومة إنما جاء من الرضاع خمس مرات ، وعندك إنما جاء من أصل الرضاع

RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿUmar's reading is countered by Ibn al-Zubayr's opposite reading; because both were learned Companions and Arabic speakers, one cannot count one as proof while excluding the other.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r6.anchor: فهو معارض بما أن ابن الزبير ما فهمه

RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r7.claim: Al-Razi says only extreme partisanship that blinds the heart could hide the weakness in these arguments.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r7.anchor: ولولا التعصب الشديد المعمي للقلب لما خفي ضعف هذه الكلمات

RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r8.claim: Abū Bakr al-Rāzī then relied on hadith and analogy, but al-Razi says a Qur'anic legal discussion should derive only from the verse; other proofs belong in jurisprudence books.
RAZI-FULL:v10p25#2/r8.anchor: ومن تكلم في أحكام القرآن وجب أن لا يذكر إلا ما يتسنبطه من الآية ، فأما ما سوى ذلك فانما يليق بكتب الفقه

RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r1.claim: The prohibition of a wife's mother includes her original mother and all grandmothers through either parent, as with lineage generally.
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r1.anchor: الأمهات الأصلية وجميع جداتها من قبل الأب والأم كما بينا مثله في النسب

RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r2.speaker: الأكثرين من الصحابة والتابعين
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r2.claim: The majority of Companions and Successors hold that marrying a woman prohibits her mother whether or not the marriage is consummated.
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r2.anchor: مذهب الأكثرين من الصحابة والتابعين أن من تزوج بامرأة حرمت عليه أمها سواء دخل بها أو لم يدخل

RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r3.speaker: علي وزيد وابن عمر وابن الزبير وجابر وابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r3.claim: A group of Companions, including Ali, Zayd, Ibn Umar, Ibn al-Zubayr, Jabir, and according to the strongest reports Ibn Abbas, hold that the mother is forbidden only after intercourse with the daughter, like a stepdaughter.
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r3.anchor: وهو قول علي وزيد وابن عمر وابن الزبير وجابر ، وأظهر الروايات عن ابن عباس

RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r4.speaker: جمع من الصحابة
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r4.claim: Their grammatical argument is that the verse states two rulings and then one condition, so the condition applies to both rulings.
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r4.anchor: ذكر حكمين وهو قوله : { وأمهات نسائكم وربائبكم اللاتى فى حجوركم } ثم ذكر شرطا

RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r5.claim: The author favors the majority: 'your wives' mothers' is an independent clause, and no proof makes the later condition govern it.
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى : { وأمهات نسائكم } جملة مستقلة بنفسها ولم يدل الدليل على عود ذلك الشرط اليه

RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r6.claim: A condition must attach to something already stated; attaching it to one clause suffices, while extending it to the other abandons the apparent wording without proof.
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r6.anchor: الشرط لا بد من تعليقه بشيء سبق ذكره فاذا علقناه باحدى الجملتين لم يكن بنا حاجة إلى تعليقه بالجملة الثانية

RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r7.claim: The clause's general meaning is certain, whereas the condition's return to it is only a possibility; restricting the generality on that uncertain basis is impermissible.
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r7.anchor: عموم هذه الجملة معلوم ، وعود الشرط اليه محتمل

RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r8.claim: If the condition applies only to mothers-in-law, stepdaughters would be forbidden without consummation, which consensus rejects.
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r8.anchor: يلزم القول بتحريم الربائب مطلقا ، وذلك باطل بالاجماع

RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r9.claim: If it applies to both clauses, 'min' would have to mean 'from among' for mothers-in-law and origin for stepdaughters, improperly giving one word two senses.
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r9.anchor: فيلزم استعمال اللفظ الواحد المشترك في كلا مفهوميه وانه غير جائز

RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r10.claim: A possible reply is that 'min' means connection in both clauses, as in the verse describing believing men and women as allies of one another.
RAZI-FULL:v10p26/r10.anchor: إن كلمة ( من ) للاتصال كقوله تعالى : { والمؤمنون والمؤمنات بعضهم أولياء بعض }

RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r1.claim: A report from Amr ibn Shuayb, from his father, from his grandfather, says a man may not marry his wife's mother whether or not he consummated the marriage; if he married the mother and divorced her before consummation, he may marry the daughter. Al-Tabari challenged its authenticity.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r1.anchor: عن أبيه عن جده عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : اذا نكح الرجل المرأة فلا يحل له أن يتزوج أمها

RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r2.speaker: محمد بن جرير الطبري
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r2.claim: Al-Tabari criticized the authenticity of the report about marrying a wife's mother.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r2.anchor: وطعن محمد بن جرير الطبري في صحة هذا الحديث

RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r3.speaker: عبدالله بن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r3.claim: Ibn Masud once permitted marrying a woman's mother after divorcing her before intercourse; after seeing the people of Medina united against his ruling, he returned to Kufa and ordered a man to leave that wife.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r3.anchor: وكان عبدالله بن مسعود يفتي بنكاح أم المرأة اذا طلق بنتها قبل المسيس

RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r4.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit says that after divorce before consummation a man may marry his wife's mother, but after her death he may not.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r4.anchor: روى قتادة عن سعيد بن المسيب أن زيد بن ثابت قال : الرجل اذا طلق امرأته قبل الدخول

RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r5.claim: The author explains that divorce before consummation carries no rulings of consummation, including no waiting period, while death counts like consummation for the waiting-period rule and therefore triggers this prohibition.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27/r5.anchor: الطلاق قبل الدخول لا يتعلق به شيء من أحكام الدخول ، ألا ترى أنه لا يجب عليها عدة ، وأما الموت فلما كان في حكم الدخول في باب وجوب العدة

RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r1.claim: A stepdaughter (rabiba) is a man's wife's daughter by another man; the word means one brought up because the man raises her, and the two cited verbs have the same meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r1.anchor: الربائب : جمع ربيبة ، وهي بنت امرأة الرجل من غيره ، ومعناها مربوبة

RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r2.speaker: ابن السكيت
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit records two case-vowel pronunciations for حجر, with fatḥ or kasr.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن السكيت : حجر الانسان وحجره بالفتح والكسر

RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r3.claim: 'In your care' means in your upbringing; it is a metaphor because a person raising a child seats the child in his lap, like saying she is in someone's custody, whose root is the armpit or bosom.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بقوله : { فى حجوركم } أي في تربيتكم

RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda interprets 'in your care' as being in your homes.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : في حجوركم أي في بيوتكم

RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r5.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r5.claim: Ali permitted marrying a stepdaughter living elsewhere and outside the husband's care after he had consummated marriage with her mother, reasoning that being in his care is a condition of the prohibition.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r5.anchor: روى مالك بن أوس بن الحدثان عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال : الربيبة اذا لم تكن في حجر الزوج

RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r6.speaker: سائر العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r6.claim: Other scholars hold that consummation with the mother forbids her daughter whether or not she was raised by the husband, because the verse makes absence of consummation the basis for there being no blame.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r6.anchor: وأما سائر العلماء فانهم قالوا : إذا دخل بالمرأة حرمت عليه ابنتها سواء كانت في تربيته أو لم تكن

RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r7.claim: The author rejects care as a legal condition: the verse mentions the usual case, since a wife's daughter is ordinarily raised by her husband.
RAZI-FULL:v10p27#2/r7.anchor: هذا الكلام على الأعم ، لا أن هذا القيد شرط في حصول هذا التحريم

RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r1.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r1.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi argues that adultery creates affinity prohibitions: 'entering' a woman means intercourse whether lawful or illicit, so adultery with a mother forbids her daughter.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r1.anchor: تمسك أبو بكر الرازي في إثبات أن الزنا يوجب حرمة المصاهرة

RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r2.claim: The author calls this argument extremely weak because the verse concerns a woman who was already one of the man's wives before intercourse, a status an adulteress lacks.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r2.anchor: وهذا الاستدلال في نهاية الضعف ، وذلك لأن هذه الآية مختصة بالمنكوحة لدليلين

RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r3.claim: The wording 'from your women whom you entered' implies that being one of his women precedes intercourse; the verse also divides his women into those entered and not entered, so the two statuses differ.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r3.anchor: قوله : { من نسائكم اللاتى دخلتم بهن } يقتضي أن كونها من نسائه يكون متقدما على دخوله بها

RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r4.claim: Marriage makes a woman one of a man's wives by contract before intercourse, but adultery creates no prior status that makes her one of his women.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r4.anchor: في النكاح صارت المرأة بحكم العقد من نسائه سواء دخل بها أو لم يدخل بها ، أما في الزنا

RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r5.claim: An adulteress is likewise excluded from a bequest to a man's wives and from a legally binding oath about a family's wives, reinforcing that she is not included in the wording.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28/r5.anchor: لو أوصى لنساء فلان ، لا تدخل هذه الزانية فيهن ، وكذلك لو حلف على نساء بني فلان

RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r1.claim: Al-Shafii prohibits a father from marrying his son's slave woman, whereas Abu Hanifa permits it.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r1.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمه الله : لا يجوز للأب أن يتزوج بجارية ابنه ، وقال أبو حنيفة

RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r2.claim: Al-Shafii's argument is that the son's slave woman is his halila, and the verse prohibits a son's halila to his father.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r2.anchor: جارية الابن حليلة ، وحليلة الابن محرمة على الأب

RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r3.claim: The author derives halila from permissibility, making it a woman made lawful, and from hulul, making it a place where the master resides; both cover a slave woman.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون مأخوذا من الحل الذي هو الاباحة ، فالحليلة تكون بمعنى المحلة

RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r4.claim: The author gives two further derivations: the pair is as if settled together in one garment, cover, or home, or each settled in the other's heart and spirit through love and intimacy.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r4.anchor: لشدة اتصال كل واحد منهما بالآخر كأنهما يحلان في ثوب واحد وفي لحاف واحد وفي منزل واحد

RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r5.claim: The conventional phrase 'a man's halila' meaning his wife does not exclude a slave woman; defining the word broadly to include both defeats the contrary linguistic claim, which is only negative testimony.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r5.anchor: إنا لا ننكر أن لفظ الحليلة يتناول الزوجة ، ولكنا نفسره بمعنى يتناول الزوجة والجارية

RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r6.claim: 'From your loins' excludes an adopted son: early Islam treated an adopted child as a son, but the wife of a man merely claimed as a son is not forbidden if he is not his biological son.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r6.anchor: قوله : { الذين من أصلابكم } احترازا عن المتبني ، وكان المتبني في صدر الاسلام بمنزلة الابن

RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r7.claim: After Zayd ibn Haritha divorced Zaynab bint Jahsh, the Prophet married her; the polytheists accused him of marrying his son's wife, and the cited verses denied that adoption makes adopted sons true sons and removed blame from marrying their former wives.
RAZI-FULL:v10p28#2/r7.anchor: نكح الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم زينب بنت جحش الأسدية وهي بنت أميمة بنت عبد المطلب

RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r1.claim: The apparent wording excludes a milk-son's wife, while 'what is beyond these' in the next verse appears to permit her; the Prophetic rule that nursing forbids what lineage forbids specifies that general permission, so a solitary report narrows the Qur'an's general wording.
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r1.anchor: ظاهر قوله : { وحلائل أبنائكم الذين من أصلابكم } لا يتناول حلائل الأبناء من الرضاعة

RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r2.claim: Scholars agree that a son's wife becomes forbidden to his father as soon as the marriage contract is made, whether or not the son consummated it, because the verse is general.
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r2.anchor: اتفقوا على أن حرمة التزوج بحليلة الابن تحصل بنفس العقد

RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says to leave unspecified the condition God left unspecified; here that means the prohibition is permanent, not that the ruling is obscure, as with the seven permanently forbidden blood relations called the unspecified ones.
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r3.anchor: فقال ابن عباس : أبهموا ما أبهمه الله

RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r4.claim: The prohibition also covers a grandson's wife; this shows that a grandson is called one of the grandfather's loins and is descended from him.
RAZI-FULL:v10p29/r4.anchor: اتفقوا على أن هذه الآية تقتضي تحريم حليلة ولد الولد على الجد

RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r1.claim: The phrase 'and combining two sisters' is grammatically nominative, with an implied sense: forbidden to you are your mothers, daughters, and combining two sisters.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r1.anchor: قوله : { وأن تجمعوا بين الاختين } في محل الرفع ، لأن التقدير : حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم وبناتكم والجمع بين الأختين

RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r2.claim: Combining two sisters occurs through marrying both, owning both, or marrying one while owning the other; simultaneous marriage to both raises the possible rulings of upholding the union, choosing one, allowing later choice, or voiding it.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r2.anchor: الجمع بين الأختين يقع على ثلاثة أوجه : إما أن ينكحهما معا ، أو يملكهما معا ، أو ينكح إحداهما ويمكل الاخرى

RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r3.claim: The simultaneous marriage is void under the verse; this challenges Abu Hanifa's principle that prohibition does not entail invalidity, illustrated by prohibited triple divorce, exchanging one dirham for two, and other corrupt sales.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r3.anchor: أما الجمع فباطل بحكم هذه الآية هكذا قالوا ، إلا أنه مشكل على أصل أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r4.claim: Although someone might compare this to prohibited divorce during menstruation or a post-menstrual purity in which intercourse occurred, the author says a subtle distinction between the cases is explained in his work on disputed issues.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r4.anchor: قلنا : بين الصورتين فرق دقيق لطيف ذكرناه في الخلافيات

RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r5.claim: Voiding both contracts is the remaining sound outcome: choosing one lacks a differentiating basis, and leaving the choice until later presupposes a valid continuing contract.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r5.anchor: وأما أن التعيين أيضا باطل ، فلأن الترجيح من غير مرجح باطل

RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r6.claim: If a man marries one sister and then the other, the second marriage is void because preventing a new prohibition is easier than undoing an established one.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r6.anchor: فههنا يحكم ببطلان نكاح الثانية ، لأن الدفع أسهل من الرفع

RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r7.speaker: علي وعمر وابن مسعود وزيد بن ثابت وابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r7.claim: Ali, Umar, Ibn Masud, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Ibn Umar prohibit combining two sisters through ownership, or by marriage to one and ownership of the other; other Companions permit it.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r7.anchor: فقد اختلفت الصحابة فيه ، فقال علي وعمر وابن مسعود وزيد بن ثابت وابن عمر : لا يجوز الجمع بينهما

RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r8.speaker: علي وعمر وابن مسعود وزيد بن ثابت وابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r8.claim: The prohibiting group argues that the verse's apparent generality forbids combining sisters in every form.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r8.anchor: ظاهر الآية يقتضي تحريم الجمع بين الأختين مطلقا

RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r9.speaker: عثمان
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r9.claim: Uthman says one verse permits the pairing and another forbids it, and that permission takes priority; he cites the exception for those owned by the right hand and a similar exception for spouses or those owned.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30/r9.anchor: وعن عثمان أنه قال : أحلتهما آية وحرمتهما آية ، والتحليل أولى

RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r1.claim: The cited permissions do not permit combining the sisters even in intercourse: Muslims agree intercourse with both is forbidden, and if ownership of both permitted intercourse by the cited rule, it would be permitted, which it is not.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r1.anchor: أن المسلمين أجمعوا على أنه لا يجوز الجمع بين الأختين في حل الوطء

RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r2.claim: The author reports the Prophetic rule that when the forbidden and permitted meet, the forbidden prevails, supporting the prohibition of combining them in ownership.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r2.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( ما اجتمع الحرام والحلال إلا وغلب الحرام الحلال )

RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r3.claim: The author also invokes the Prophetic advice to leave what causes doubt for what does not.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r3.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( دع ما يريبك إلى ما لا يريبك )

RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r4.claim: Ali's position is favored by caution: sexual relations are presumptively forbidden, and when evidence about a contract's conditions is balanced, prohibition is required; the lawfulness of marriage is an exception to that baseline.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r4.anchor: مبنى الابضاع في الأصل على الحرمة ، بدليل أنه إذا استوت الامارات في حصول العقد مع شرائطه وفي عدمه

RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r5.claim: The author reasons that if sexual relations lacked humiliation and harm, marriage to mothers would be lawful because serving them benefits them; its prohibition shows the practice entails harm, so prohibition is the baseline and lawfulness an exception.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r5.anchor: لو كان خاليا عن جهة الاذلال والضرر ، لوجب أن يكون مشروعا في حق الأمهات

RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r6.claim: Under the better-known juristic view, a man may own two enslaved sisters, but intercourse with one makes the other forbidden until he relinquishes ownership of the first by sale, gift, emancipation, manumission contract, or marriage.
RAZI-FULL:v10p30#2/r6.anchor: وهو أنه يجوز الجمع بين أمتين أختين في ملك اليمين ، فاذا وطىء إحداهما حرمت الثانية

SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r1.claim: The common plural of أم is أمهات, with an extra ه distinguishing rational mothers from non-rational ones; an anonymous line illustrates أمات for young animals.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r1.anchor: فالهاء زائدة في الجمع، فرقا بين العقلاء وغيرهم. يقال في العقلاء: " أمهات " وفي غيرهم: " أمات " كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r2.claim: Usage can reverse the common pattern, and one poet uses both forms for rational mothers in a single couplet.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r2.anchor: وقد يقال: " أمات " في العقلاء: و " أمهات " في غيرهم

SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r3.claim: The poet's line witnesses the forms الأمهات and أماتكا being used for rational mothers.

SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r4.claim: The form أمهة is also attested, with an added ه followed by feminine تاء; a poem uses it.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r4.anchor: وقد سمع " أمهة " في " أم " بزيادة هاء، بعدها تاء تأنيث قال:

SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r5.claim: Given the singular أمهة, أمهات may be its plural; the added ه also appears in هبلع and هجرع.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r5.anchor: فعلى هذا يجوز أن تكون " أمهات " جمع " أمهة " المزيد فيها الهاء، والهاء قد أتت زائدة في مواضع

SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r6.claim: بنات is the feminine plural of ابن; the source previously discussed its derivation and pattern at 2:40.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r6.anchor: وبنات جمع بنت، وبنت تأنيث ابن

SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r7.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r7.claim: Al-Farra says بنات is the plural of بنة with an open باء, with kasra signaling an omitted radical; the author says this works only if that radical is ياء, while the correct root is واو.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r7.anchor: حكى عن الفراء أن " بنات " ليس جمعا ل " بنت " يعني بكسر الباء بل جمع " بنة "

SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r8.claim: Another grammarian gives the original as بنوة; the author reconciles this with the بنة account, since both require the missing root letter to be واو.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r8.anchor: والذي قال: بنات جمع " بنوة " لفظ بالأصل فلا خلاف

SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r9.claim: The تاء in بنت and أخت compensates for an omitted root consonant rather than marking femininity: the preceding consonant is still, and the تاء does not become هاء in pause.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r9.anchor: واعلم أن تاء " بنت " و " أخت " تاء تعويض عن اللام المحذوفة كما تقدم تقريره، وليست للتأنيث

SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r10.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r10.claim: Abu al-Baqa asks why أخت restores the omitted consonant in its plural but بنت does not, explaining this by analogy of each feminine plural to its masculine.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23/r10.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " فإن قيل: لم رد المحذوف في " أخوات " ولم يرد في " بنات "؟ قيل:

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r1.claim: The author rejects Abu al-Baqa's comparison: he compares broken plurals with sound plurals, although broken plurals restore the missing consonant in both أبناء and إخوة, while sound plurals omit it in both.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r1.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله ليس بشيء لأنه أخذ جمع التكسير وهو إخوة وإخوان مقابلا ل " أخوات " جمع التصحيح

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r2.claim: The ألف in خالة and خال comes from واو, as shown by the plural أخوال and the phrase in 24:61.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r2.anchor: ألف " خالة " و " خال " منقلبة عن واو، بدليل جمعه على " أخوال " ، قال تعالى: أو بيوت أخوالكم

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r3.claim: من الرضاعة is an accusative circumstantial phrase modifying the sisters, understood as sisters who are from nursing.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r3.anchor: من الرضاعة }: في موضع نصب على الحال فيتعلق بمحذوف تقديره: وأخواتكم كائنات من الرضاعة

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r4.speaker: أبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r4.claim: Abu Haywa reads الرضاعة with kasra on the راء.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: " من الرضاعة " بكسر الراء

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r5.claim: من نسائكم may be a circumstantial phrase modifying ربائبكم, meaning stepdaughters from your women.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r5.anchor: فيه وجهان، أحدهما: أنه حال من " ربائبكم " تقديره: " وربائبكم كائنات من نسائكم "

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, من نسائكم may describe the implicit pronoun in في حجوركم, because a relative clause contains a pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r6.anchor: والثاني: أنه حال من الضمير المستكن في قوله: { في حجوركم } لأنه لما وقع صلة تحمل ضميرا

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r7.claim: ربائب is the plural of ربيبة, a spouse's daughter, and ربيب is the masculine; they are named for each spouse's rearing the other's child.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r7.anchor: والربائب: جمع " ربيبة " وهي بنت الزوج أو الزوجة، والمذكر: ربيب، سميا بذلك؛ لأن أحد الزوجين يربه

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r8.claim: The phrase اللاتي في حجوركم does not imply a legal restriction; it reflects the usual circumstance of stepdaughters being in the household.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r8.anchor: لا مفهوم له لخروجه مخرج الغالب

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r9.claim: حجور is the plural of حجر, with either vowel on حاء; it first means the front of a garment and then protection or shelter.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#2/r9.anchor: الحجور: جمع " حجر " بفتح الحاء وكسرها، وهو مقدم ثوب الإنسان ثم استعملت اللفظ في الحفظ والستر

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r1.claim: اللاتي دخلتم بهن modifies the second نسائكم governed by من; consummation with the mother is required for the stepdaughter to be prohibited.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r1.anchor: اشترط في تحريم الربيبة أن يدخل بأمها

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r2.claim: It cannot modify both occurrences of نسائكم because they have different governing prepositions and a shared adjective cannot modify nouns with different governors.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r2.anchor: فقد اختلف العاملان، وإذا اختلفا امتنع النعت

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r3.claim: It also cannot modify both on legal grounds: mothers-in-law are prohibited by contract alone according to the majority, whereas stepdaughters require consummation with their mother.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r3.anchor: أم المرأة تحرم بمجرد العقد على البنت دخل بها أو لم يدخل بها عند الجمهور

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's explanation makes the stepdaughter prohibited only when her mother has been consummated with; without that, she remains lawful.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r4.anchor: وفي كلام الزمخشري ما يلزم منه أنه يجوز أن يكون هذا الوصف راجعا إلى الأولى في المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r5.claim: If the phrase is linked to both mothers-in-law and stepdaughters, من would have to mean specification for one and source or origin for the other, an impermissible double sense in one expression.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r5.anchor: ولا يجوز الأول لأن معنى " من " مع أحد المتعلقين خلاف معناها مع الآخر

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r6.claim: If linked only to mothers-in-law, the nearer stepdaughter phrase should receive it absent a compelling reason, and everyone agrees mothers-in-law are prohibited without qualification.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r6.anchor: ولا يجوز الثاني لأن الذي يليه هو الذي يستوجب التعليق به ما لم يعرض أمر لا يرد

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows من to mean connection and link the phrase to both women and stepdaughters, comparing the mutual relationship in 9:67 and the relationship between daughters and mothers.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#3/r7.anchor: إلا أن تقول: أعلقه بالنساء والربائب، وأجعل " من " للاتصال كقوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r1.claim: An anonymous poem uses منك and مني to express connection between two people, offered as evidence for that sense of من.

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r2.claim: A second anonymous poetic line likewise uses من to express reciprocal connection.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r2.anchor: ما أنا من دد ولا دد مني

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r3.speaker: علي وابن عباس وزيد وابن عمرو وابن الزبير
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r3.claim: A reported reading adds اللاتي دخلتم بهن after mothers-in-law, making their prohibition conditional on consummation; Ibn Abbas reportedly swore this alone was revealed.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r3.anchor: إلا ما روي عن علي وابن عباس وزيد وابن عمرو وابن الزبير أنهم قرؤوا " وأمهات نسائكم اللاتي دخلتم بهن "

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reportedly swore that the conditional wording was the only revelation.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r4.anchor: فكان ابن عباس يقول: " والله ما أنزل إلا هكذا "

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r5.claim: The Shaykh says he knows no one who gives من the meaning of connection; the cited verse, poem, and report are all interpreted differently.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#4/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ولا نعلم أحدا أثبت ل " من " معنى الاتصال، أما الآية والبيت والحديث فمؤولة

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r1.claim: حلائل is the plural of حليلة, meaning wife, named because she dwells with her husband wherever he is; it is an active feminine form.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r1.anchor: سميت بذلك لأنها تحل مع زوجها حيث كان، فهي فعيلة بمعنى فاعلة

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r2.claim: An anonymous poem uses حليلها for the husband, illustrating the masculine counterpart.

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r3.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj and others derive حليلة from حلال, with each spouse being permitted to the other, so فعيل is passive; the author objects to the feminine ending unless it is treated as a frozen noun like نطيحة or ذبيحة.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r3.anchor: وهو قول الزجاج وجماعة، ف " فعيل " بمعنى مفعول أي: محللة له

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r4.claim: Another derivation uses حل as the opposite of tying: each spouse undoes the other's waist wrapper.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r4.anchor: هما من لفظ " الحل " ضد العقد؛ لأن كلا منهما يحل إزار صاحبه

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r5.claim: The phrase الذين من أصلابكم clarifies that the prohibited sons' wives are those of biological sons, since son can also refer to an adopted child.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r5.anchor: صفة مبينة؛ لأن الابن قد يطلق على المتبنى به وليست امرأته حراما على من تبناه

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r6.claim: A son through nursing has the same rule as a biological son here, established by the Sunnah and thus not a counterexample to the verse.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r6.anchor: وأما الابن من الرضاع فإنه وإن كان حكمه حكم ابن الصلب في ذلك فمبين بالسنة

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r7.claim: أصلاب is plural of صلب, the back, named for its firmness; the Hijazi pronunciation with ḍamma then sukūn is the most eloquent.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r7.anchor: وأصلاب: جمع " صلب " وهو الظهر، سمي بذلك لقوته اشتقاقا من الصلابة، وأفصح لغتيه:

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r8.claim: Al-Farra reports that Tamim and Asad pronounce the word صلب with fatḥa on both consonants.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r8.anchor: وبنو تميم وأسد يقولون " صلبا بفتحهما، حكى ذلك الفراء عنهم

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r9.claim: An anonymous poem witnesses the dialectal pronunciation in the phrase في صلب.

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r10.claim: Al-Farra also cites the spoken complaint إذا أقوم اشتكى صلبي for that dialectal form.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#5/r10.anchor: وحكى عنهم: " إذا أقوم اشتكى صلبي "

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r1.claim: وأن تجمعوا is in the nominative, coordinated with the nominative element of حرمت: combining two sisters in marriage is prohibited.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r1.anchor: { وأن تجمعوا } في محل رفع عطفا على مرفوع " حرمت " أي: وحرم عليكم الجمع بين الأختين

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r2.claim: Combining two sisters in ownership is unanimously allowed, while intercourse with both by right of ownership is disputed.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r2.anchor: أما في الملك فجائز اتفاقا، وأما الوطء بملك اليمين ففيه خلاف ليس هذا موضعه

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r3.claim: The exception after ما قد سلف is disconnected and accusative, meaning God forgives what occurred in pre-Islamic times.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r3.anchor: فهو منصوب المحل كما تقدم في نظيره

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r4.claim: An alternative takes the exception as connected: a pre-Islamic marriage of two sisters remains valid after Islam, but the man must choose one and leave the other.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r4.anchor: وقيل: المعنى إلا ما عقد عليه قبل الإسلام، فإنه بعد الإسلام يبقى النكاح على صحته، ولكن يختار واحدة منهما ويفارق الأخرى

SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r5.claim: Although a similar sense was possible for the earlier ما قد سلف in 4:22, the connected exception cannot work here because it yields a false meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:4:23#6/r5.anchor: وكان قد تقدم قريب من هذا المعنى في { ما قد سلف } الأول ويكون الاستثناء عليه متصلا، وهنا لا يتأتى الاتصال البتة لفساد المعنى

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r1.claim: Besides fathers' wives in 4:22, Muslim men cannot marry mothers, daughters, or sisters; mothers and daughters include grandmothers and granddaughters, and sisters include full and half siblings.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r1.anchor: Muslim men cannot marry their mothers, including grandmothers; their daughters, including granddaughters; or their sisters, including both full and half siblings

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r2.speaker: al-Shāfiʿī
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r2.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī suggests a biological daughter born out of wedlock might not be covered by the marriage prohibition.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r2.anchor:
Al-
Shāfiʿī suggests that a man’s biological daughter born out of wedlock might not be subject to this prohibition

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r3.speaker: all other schools of law
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r3.claim: All other legal schools prohibit marrying any biological daughter, including one born out of wedlock.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r3.anchor: but all other schools of law prohibit marriage to any biological daughter

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r4.claim: A milk-mother is a nonbiological woman who nurses a child; parents may pay a wet nurse under 2:233 and 65:6.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r4.anchor: A milk-mother is a wet nurse, a woman who nurses a child, but who is not the child’s biological mother.

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r5.claim: Milk-siblings are otherwise unrelated children nursed by the same woman, and suckling creates a legal status like blood relations.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r5.anchor:
Milk-siblings (here milk-sisters
) are otherwise unrelated persons who, as infants or children, were wet-nursed by the same woman.

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r6.claim: A woman who nursed a man is his maḥram, requiring no covering before her and prohibiting marriage; these rules also apply to her husband's and her biological children and others she nursed.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r6.anchor: meaning that she does not need to cover in front of him and he can never marry her.

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r7.claim: A man may marry the sister of his milk-son or the mother of his milk-brother as exceptions to the suckling rules.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r7.anchor: Two exceptions are that a man can marry the sister of his milk-son or the mother of his milk-brother

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r8.speaker: ʿĀʾishah
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r8.claim: ʿĀʾishah maintained that a revealed verse set ten sucklings for establishing milk relations, later changed to five.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r8.anchor: ʿĀʾishah maintained that a verse had been revealed requiring ten sucklings for the establishment of milk relations, but this was later changed to five

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r9.speaker: a more widely transmitted report
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r9.claim: A report says one or two sucklings do not establish legal milk relations, leading some to require at least three.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r9.anchor: A more widely transmitted report states that “one or two sucklings” do not establish legal milk relations, which led some to claim that at least three sucklings were required.

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r10.speaker: al-Shāfiʿī
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r10.claim: On the basis of other hadiths, al-Shāfiʿī required at least five sucklings.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r10.anchor: on the basis of other aḥādīth, al-Shāfiʿī required that a child be suckled at least five times

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r11.speaker: Twelver Shiite school
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r11.claim: The Twelver Shiite school requires fifteen sucklings, with variants requiring ten.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r11.anchor: the Twelver Shiite school requires fifteen (or, variously, ten;Ṭs).

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r12.speaker: most legal scholars
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r12.claim: Most legal scholars require nursing to occur in the child's first two to three years.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r12.anchor: For most legal scholars, the nursing has to occur within the first two to three years of the child’s life

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r13.speaker: community consensus
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r13.claim: The community's consensus is that the exception for unconsummated marriage clearly applies only to stepdaughters, not their mothers.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r13.anchor: The consensus of the community is that the exception only clearly applied to stepdaughters

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r14.speaker: some early authorities
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r14.claim: Some early authorities reportedly held that a man's wife's mother is prohibited only after he consummates marriage with the wife.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r14.anchor: some early authorities reportedly held that only when one had consummated marriage with a woman was one prohibited from marrying her mother

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r15.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r15.claim: Some reportedly read an addition limiting the prohibition on wives' mothers to those whose marriage was consummated.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r15.anchor: Some reportedly read the verse with the following addition: and the mothers of your wives “with whom you have consummated marriage”

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r16.speaker: early scholars
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r16.claim: As in the discussion of 4:21, early scholars disputed which intimate contact legally constituted consummation.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r16.anchor: As in the discussion of v. 21, some early scholars debated the extent of intimate contact that legally constituted consummation

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r17.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r17.claim: Some held that any intimate contact with a woman prohibited marriage to her daughter.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r17.anchor: Some viewed any intimate contact with a woman as prohibiting marriage to her daughter

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r18.speaker: Shāfiʿī school
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r18.claim: The Shāfiʿī school held that this prohibition applies only in the case of marriage.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r18.anchor: the Shāfiʿī school held that the prohibition pertained only in the case of marriage

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r19.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r19.claim: Some derive rabībah and rabīb from a stepparent undertaking stepchildren's upbringing, an idea reinforced by “in your care.”
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r19.anchor: The terms rabībah for “stepdaughter” and rabīb for “stepson” are said by some commentators to derive from the fact that a stepparent often undertakes the raising

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r20.speaker: a minority tradition
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r20.claim: A minority tradition treats being in the stepfather's care as a condition and says stepdaughters outside his home remain marriageable.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r20.anchor: A minority tradition suggests that this means that stepdaughters not living with their stepfathers are potential marriage partners.

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r21.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r21.claim: Most regard “in your care” as descriptive, not a legal condition; ordinary close family contact is what makes stepchildren forbidden spouses.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r21.anchor: But most understand this not as a condition

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r22.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r22.claim: The ban on marrying sons' former wives applies whether or not the marriage was consummated.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r22.anchor: the prohibition against marrying former wives of one’s sons applies regardless of whether the marriage was consummated or not

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r23.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r23.claim: The sons-from-loins limitation includes wives of milk-sons but excludes adoptive sons.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r23.anchor: The prohibition is limited to the wives of your sons who are from your loins, which includes the wives of one’s milk-sons

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r24.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r24.claim: Commentators connect the rule to the Prophet's marriage to Zayd ibn Ḥārithah's former wife; because Zayd was adopted, not from his loins, the marriage was permissible.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r24.anchor: Some commentators connected this verse to the Prophet’s marrying the former wife of his adopted son, Zayd ibn Ḥārithah.

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r25.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r25.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r25.claim: Marrying two sisters together is prohibited, while marriages arranged before revelation could stand.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r25.anchor: Marrying two sisters is forbidden, save for what is past, meaning that such marriages arranged prior to the revelation of this verse could stand

STUDYQURAN:4:23/r26.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r26.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r26.claim: The Prophet reportedly told converts who had two wives who were sisters to divorce one.
STUDYQURAN:4:23/r26.anchor: the Prophet reportedly ordered men who desired to enter Islam, but had two sister wives, to divorce one

TAB-FULL:v6p553#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p553#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p553#2/r1.claim: The verse forbids marrying the listed women, with “marriage” omitted because the context supplies it.
TAB-FULL:v6p553#2/r1.anchor: يعني بذلك تعالى ذكره: حرم عليكم نكاح أمهاتكم، فترك ذكر النكاح اكتفاء بدلالة الكلام عليه

TAB-FULL:v6p553#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p553#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v6p553#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās classifies seven prohibitions by blood relation and seven by marriage relation, citing the list here and adding the father's former wives; reports also extend his recitation to the next verse.
TAB-FULL:v6p553#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «حرم من النسب سبع، ومن الصهر سبع» ثم قرأ: {حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم} [النساء: 23]

TAB-FULL:v6p556/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r1.speaker: عمرو بن سالم
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r1.claim: ʿAmr ibn Sālim divides the prohibited women into seven by blood and seven by affinity, including the listed relatives, wet-nursing relations, wives' mothers and stepdaughters, sons' wives, and combining sisters.
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r1.anchor: عن مطرف، عن عمرو بن سالم، مولى الأنصار، قال: «حرم من النسب سبع، ومن الصهر سبع»

TAB-FULL:v6p556/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r2.claim: The women named in the passage are forbidden to marry by unanimous agreement, though early Companions disagreed about a wife’s mother if the daughter was divorced before consummation.
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r2.anchor: محرمات غير جائز نكاحهن لمن حرم الله ذلك عليه من الرجال، بإجماع جميع الأمة

TAB-FULL:v6p556/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r3.claim: All early and later scholars hold a wife’s mother forbidden whether or not the husband consummated the marriage; the entry condition applies only to stepdaughters, not mothers-in-law.
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r3.anchor: فقال جميع أهل العلم متقدمهم ومتأخرهم: من المبهمات، وحرام على من تزوج امرأة أمها دخل بامرأته التي نكحها أو لم يدخل بها

TAB-FULL:v6p556/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r4.claim: The condition attaches to the immediately preceding stepdaughter clause: by the same syntactic principle, the unanimous restriction of the exception in 4:24 to its adjacent class shows the condition does not reach mothers-in-law.
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r4.anchor: وفي إجماع الجميع على أن الاستثناء في ذلك إنما هو مما وليه من قوله: {والمحصنات} [النساء: 24] أبين الدلالة على أن الشرط

TAB-FULL:v6p556/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r5.speaker: بعض المتقدمين
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r5.claim: Some early authorities held it lawful to marry a wife’s mother if the marriage to her daughter ended before consummation, treating her like a stepdaughter.
TAB-FULL:v6p556/r5.anchor: وروي عن بعض المتقدمين أنه كان يقول: حلال نكاح أمهات نسائنا اللواتي لم ندخل بهن، وأن حكمهن في ذلك حكم الربائب

TAB-FULL:v6p557/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r1.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r1.claim: ʿAlī treats a former wife's mother as a stepdaughter: a man divorced her daughter before consummation still may not marry her.
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r1.anchor: في رجل تزوج امرأة فطلقها قبل أن يدخل بها، أيتزوج أمها؟ قال: «هي بمنزلة الربيبة»

TAB-FULL:v6p557/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r2.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r2.claim: Zayd reportedly disliked marrying the mother if the wife died and he inherited from her, but allowed it after divorce before consummation.
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r2.anchor: إذا ماتت عنده، وأخذ ميراثها، كره أن يخلف على أمها، وإذا طلقها قبل أن يدخل بها، فإن شاء فعل

TAB-FULL:v6p557/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the requirement of consummation applies both to mothers of wives and to stepdaughters.
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r3.anchor: أن مجاهدا قال له: {وأمهات نسائكم وربائبكم اللاتي في حجوركم من نسائكم} [النساء: 23] أريد بهما الدخول جميعا

TAB-FULL:v6p557/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the view that mothers-in-law are unconditionally forbidden: unlike stepdaughters, their prohibition is not qualified by consummation; he also cites consensus.
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r4.anchor: والقول الأول أولى بالصواب، أعني قول من قال: الأم من المبهمات؛ لأن الله لم يشرط معهن الدخول

TAB-FULL:v6p557/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r5.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says marrying a woman forbids her mother whether or not the daughter was entered, while marrying and divorcing an unconsummated mother leaves her daughter lawful.
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إذا نكح الرجل المرأة فلا يحل له أن يتزوج أمها، دخل بالابنة أم لم يدخل

TAB-FULL:v6p557/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī notes a flaw in the Prophetic report's chain, but says the consensus supporting the rule makes that report unnecessary as proof.
TAB-FULL:v6p557/r6.anchor: وهذا خبر وإن كان في إسناده ما فيه، فإن في إجماع الحجة على صحة القول به مستغنى عن الاستشهاد

TAB-FULL:v6p559/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p559/r1.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v6p559/r1.claim: Asked about a man who married but did not see or have intercourse with his wife before divorcing her, ʿAṭāʾ says her mother remains forbidden to him.
TAB-FULL:v6p559/r1.anchor: الرجل ينكح المرأة لم يرها، ولا يجامعها حتى يطلقها، أيحل له أمها؟ قال: «لا هي مرسلة»

TAB-FULL:v6p559/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v6p559/r2.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v6p559/r2.claim: A report records ʿAṭāʾ's answer to whether Ibn ʿAbbās read an added consummation qualifier after mothers of wives: «لا تبرأ».
