SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r11.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r11.claim: He cites the consecutive Ḥawāmīm and Alif Lām Rā groups, and the separation among the Musabbiḥāt, as signs of purposeful, divinely fixed sūrah order.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r11.anchor: ومما يدل على ذلك ويؤيده توالي الحواميم وذوات الر والفصل بين المسبحات

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r12.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r12.claim: Placing Ṭā Sīn before al-Qaṣaṣ and separating it from the paired Ṭā Sīn Mīm sūrahs reflects their shared opening and relative length.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r12.anchor: وتقديم طس على القصص مفصولا بها بين النظيرتين [ طسم الشعراء وطسم القصص ] في المطلع والطول

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r13.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r13.claim: Al-Muṭaffifīn separates al-Infiṭār and al-Inshiqāq, although the latter two resemble each other in opening and subject and are longer than al-Muṭaffifīn.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r13.anchor: وكذا الفصل بين الانفطار والانشقاق بالمطففين وهما نظيرتان في المطلع والمقصد وهما أطول منها

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r14.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r14.claim: He argues that without a divinely fixed order for wisdom, the Musabbiḥāt would be consecutive, Ṭā Sīn would follow al-Qaṣaṣ, and al-Muṭaffifīn would not separate the similar alif-lām-rā sūrahs.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p71/r14.anchor: فلولا أنه توقيفي لحكمة لتوالت المسبحات وأخرت طس عن القصص وأخرت المطففين أو قدمت ولم يفصل بين الر و الر

NASHR:v1p236/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p236/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p236/r1.claim: Sajawandi records many stops of this kind; readers should assess them and choose the soundest, closest stopping point.
NASHR:v1p236/r1.anchor: فلا يغتر بكل ما فيه، بل يتبع فيه الأصوب ويختار منه الأقرب.

NASHR:v1p236/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p236/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p236/r2.claim: During combined readings, careful recitation, or slow tartil, long separators, narratives, and parenthetical clauses can permit stops that would otherwise be disallowed; Sajawandi calls this licensed necessity.
NASHR:v1p236/r2.anchor: يغتفر في طول الفواصل والقصص والجمل المعترضة، ونحو ذلك في حالة جمع القراءات

NASHR:v1p236/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p236/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p236/r3.claim: The long prohibition list is an example of a licensed stop within a long passage; stopping at the preceding verse-end is the more complete choice.
NASHR:v1p236/r3.anchor: ونحو كل من حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم وبناتكم وأخواتكم إلى آخره، وهو إلى ما ملكت أيمانكم، إلا أن الوقف على آخر الفاصلة قبله أكفى

NASHR:v2p111/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p111/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p111/r1.claim: Lām is normally light; its thickening is a contextual exception, whereas tafkhim is the corresponding term for rā. Thickening is not automatic merely because an emphatic letter is nearby.
NASHR:v2p111/r1.anchor: الأصل في اللام الترقيق أبين من قولهم في الراء إن أصلها التفخيم، وذلك أن اللام لا تغلظ إلا لسبب

NASHR:v2p111/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p111/r2.speaker: ورش من طريق الأزرق وغيره
NASHR:v2p111/r2.claim: The Egyptian transmission of Warsh is distinctive: these routes thicken lām when it is adjacent to an emphatic letter.
NASHR:v2p111/r2.anchor: ورووا من طريق الأزرق، وغيره عن ورش تغليظ اللام إذا جاورها حرف تفخيم

NASHR:v2p111/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p111/r3.speaker: الجمهور
NASHR:v2p111/r3.claim: Most Egyptian transmitters thicken lām after open ṣād, ṭā, or ẓā when lām is open and the preceding emphatic is open or silent; they differ in other cases. “من أصلابكم” is among the cited ṣād-silent forms.
NASHR:v2p111/r3.anchor: واتفق الجمهور منهم على تغليظ اللام إذا تقدمها صاد، أو طاء، أو ظاء بشروط ثلاثة

NASHR:v1p452/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p452/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p452/r4.claim: The three occurrences of اللائي are written in the shape of إلى to allow four readings; the omitted alif and retained hamza or yāʾ images accommodate the readers’ variants.
NASHR:v1p452/r4.anchor: وأما اللاي فإنها كتبت في السور الثلاث

IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Nadr ibn Kinana had sons Malik and Yakhlud; Atika daughter of Adwan was Malik's mother, though he was unsure whether she also mothered Yakhlud.
IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r1.anchor: فولد النضر بن كنانة رجلين: مالك بن النضر، ويخلد بن النضر، فأم مالك: عاتكة بنت عدوان

IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r2.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r2.claim: Citing Abu Amr al-Madani, Ibn Hisham adds al-Salt and says the mother of the named sons was a daughter of Sa'd ibn Zarb al-Adwani.
IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r2.anchor: قال ابن هشام: والصلت بن النضر- فيما قال أبو عمرو المدني- وأمهم جميعا بنت سعد بن ظرب العدواني

IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r3.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r3.claim: Ibn Hisham identifies Kuthayr al-Azza's Khuza'a clan, Banu Mulayh ibn Amr, as those attributed to al-Salt; Kuthayr's poem claims descent from al-Salt and Nadr.
IBNHISHAM:v1p94/r3.anchor: قال كثير بن عبد الرحمن، وهو كثير عزة أحد بني مليح بن عمرو، من خزاعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r2.claim: Reports about occasions of revelation aid interpretation by clarifying intent, but they do not restrict a verse's wording to its occasion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r2.anchor: ومعنى كون أسباب النزول من مادة التفسير ، أنها تعين على تفسير المراد ، وليس المراد أن لفظ الآية يقصر عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r3.speaker: تقي الدين السبكي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r3.claim: Al-Subki says neither an occasion of revelation nor a specific discourse purpose restricts general wording; a specific statement followed by a general one does not narrow the general rule.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r3.anchor: قال تقي الدين السبكي : وكما أن سبب النزول لا يخصص ، كذلك خصوص غرض الكلام لا يخصص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r7.claim: Transmitted reports include the community's consensus on meanings, which must rest on evidence; examples include the maternal sister in the first inheritance passage and Friday prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r7.anchor: وتشمل الآثار إجماع الأمة على تفسير معنى ، إذ لا يكون إلا عن مستند

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r8.claim: Some meanings are known necessarily: prayer denotes the prescribed ritual form rather than supplication, and zakat the specified wealth paid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r8.anchor: وكذلك المعلومات بالضرورة كلها ككون الصلاة مرادا منها الهيئة المخصوصة دون الدعاء ، والزكاة المال المخصوص المدفوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r9.claim: Readings matter when one reading is used to interpret another, to prefer among available meanings, or to support an interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r9.anchor: وأما القراءات فلا يحتاج إليها إلا في حين الاستدلال بالقراءة على تفسير غيرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r10.claim: A well-known reading is valid linguistic evidence; an anomalous reading supports Arabic usage rather than transmission, since its reader relied on sound Arabic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r10.anchor: وإن كانت شاذة فحجتها لا من حيث الرواية ، لأنها لا تكون صحيحة الرواية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r12.claim: Reports about Arab history are useful literature, not idle talk: they clarify concise Qur'anic narratives, which are told for admonition and reflection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r12.anchor: وأما أخبار العرب فهي من جملة أدبهم . وإنما خصصتها بالذكر تنبيها لمن يتوهم أن الاشتغال بها من اللغو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r13.claim: Knowing Arab reports reveals the fine meanings alluded to in stories such as the woman who unraveled her yarn and the people of the trench.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p24/r13.anchor: فبمعرفة الأخبار يعرف ما أشارت له الآيات من دقائق المعاني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r1.claim: Estimating time by a number of verses, such as fifty, is approximate because verses differ in length.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r1.anchor: فتقدير الزمان بها في قولهم : مقدار ما يقرأ القارئ خمسين آية مثلا ، تقدير تقريبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r2.claim: Verse lengths vary with rhetorical needs, including the placement of end rhymes in relation to preceding speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r2.anchor: وتفاوت الآيات في الطول تابع لما يقتضيه مقام البلاغة من مواقع كلمات الفواصل على حسب ما قبلها من الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r5.claim: The prohibition list in this verse is shorter than those two longest verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r5.anchor: ودونهما قوله تعالى ) حرمت عليكم أمهاتكم ( إلى قوله ) إن الله كان غفورا رحيما ( في سورة النساء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r7.claim: Qur'anic pause marks do not necessarily follow verse endings, and a single verse can contain several pauses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r7.anchor: وأما وقوف القرآن فقد لا تساير نهايات الآيات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r8.claim: Differences among early verse counts can result either from variant transmission about verse endings or from scholarly judgment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r8.anchor: فقد يكون بعض ذلك عن اختلاف في الرواية كما قدمنا آنفا ، وقد يكون بعضه عن اختلاف الاجتهاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r9.claim: Al-Dani reports agreement that the Qur'an has at least six thousand verses, with disagreement over the additional total.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r9.anchor: قال أبو عمرو الداني في كتاب العدد : أجمعوا على أن عدد آيات القرآن يبلغ ستة آلاف آية ، واختلفوا فيما زاد على ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r12.claim: Ibn Ashur says the framing of the first rule in al-Itqan is imprecise and ultimately accords with al-Mazari's account.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r12.anchor: وفي الإتقان كلام في الضابط الأول من الضوابط غير محرر وهو آيل إلى ما قاله المازري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r13.claim: Medina had a first count agreed by four reciters and a second count unique to Ismail ibn Jafar; the second is also attributed to Ayyub ibn al-Mutawakkil.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r13.anchor: وقد اتفق هؤلاء الأربعة على عدد وهو المسمى بالعدد الأول ، ثم خالفهم إسماعيل ابن جعفر بعدد انفرد به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r14.claim: Mecca had one count, and verse counts could differ among Kufan, Basran, and Syrian codices, which exegetes sometimes specify.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p77/r14.anchor: ولأهل مكة عدد واحد ، وربما اتفقوا في عدد آي السورة المعينة ، وربما اختلفوا

MUSLIM:7464/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:7464/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
MUSLIM:7464/r1.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet barred entering the punished people of al-Hijr except while weeping, lest visitors suffer the same punishment; the report does not discuss 4:23’s marriage prohibitions.
MUSLIM:7464/r1.anchor: سمع عبد الله، بن عمر يقول قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأصحاب الحجر

MUSNAD-AHMAD:4561/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:4561/r1.speaker: النبي عن ابن عمر
MUSNAD-AHMAD:4561/r1.claim: The Prophet warns against entering the dwellings of a punished people unless weeping, lest the same punishment befall visitors.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:4561/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " لا تدخلوا على هؤلاء القوم الذين عذبوا إلا أن تكونوا باكين

MUSNAD-AHMAD:5225/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5225/r1.speaker: النبي عن ابن عمر
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5225/r1.claim: The Prophet forbids entering the punished people of al-Hijr without weeping, fearing visitors might suffer as they did.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5225/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا تدخلوا على هؤلاء القوم المعذبين أصحاب الحجر، إلا أن تكونوا باكين

MUSNAD-AHMAD:5404/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5404/r1.speaker: النبي عن ابن عمر
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5404/r1.claim: The Prophet says not to enter the punished people's dwellings unless weeping, lest their fate strike the visitor.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5404/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا تدخلوا على هؤلاء القوم المعذبين، إلا أن تكونوا باكين

MUSNAD-AHMAD:5441/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5441/r1.speaker: النبي عن ابن عمر
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5441/r1.claim: At al-Hijr, the Prophet warned people not to enter the dwellings of the punished unless they were weeping, lest the same happen to them.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5441/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو بالحجر: " لا تدخلوا على هؤلاء القوم المعذبين

MUSNAD-AHMAD:5931/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5931/r1.speaker: النبي عن ابن عمر
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5931/r1.claim: The Prophet told his companions not to enter the punished people's dwellings except in tears, lest they be struck by the same fate.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:5931/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لأصحابه: " لا تدخلوا على هؤلاء القوم المعذبين إلا أن تكونوا باكين

ITQAN:v1p259/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p259/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p259/r7.claim: When phonological and semantic causes coincide, Hamza fully lengthens for the stronger hamza cause and disregards the weaker semantic cause.
ITQAN:v1p259/r7.anchor: وقد يجتمع السببان اللفظي والمعنوي في نحو ﴿ لا إله إلا الله ﴾
